781.e: Too much food pollutes the water and harms the fish's health. That is why goldfish should only be fed a little.
781.m: Too much food harms the goldfish.

782.q: How do tapirs take in minerals?
a: They lick mineral-rich patches of earth
782.e: They take in minerals at so-called salt licks. These places are often visited regularly.

783.q: What does it mean if a guinea pig keeps completely still and draws its legs in when you pick it up?
a: It feels unsure or is frightened
783.e: Keeping still and tensing up are often signs of insecurity in guinea pigs. You should then handle them especially calmly and carefully.

a: Yes, it climbs over small obstacles too
No, hedgehogs can't climb at all
784.e: Hedgehogs are surprisingly good at climbing and can get over low walls or stones. When climbing down, they sometimes prefer to roll up and drop.
784.m: Hedgehogs can climb over small obstacles.

785.q: What is the difference between the UN General Assembly and the Security Council?
a: All states are represented in the General Assembly, only a few in the Security Council
Both are exactly the same body
The Security Council only meets every ten years
The General Assembly has only five members
785.e: Every UN member country has a seat and one vote in the General Assembly. The Security Council, on the other hand, consists of only 15 countries and makes important decisions about peace and security.
785.m: All states are in the General Assembly, only 15 in the Security Council.

786.q: How long does a young orang-utan stay with its mother?
a: Several years, often until about seven to nine years old
786.e: For a long time the young learn from their mother which food is edible and how to climb. That is why the bond lasts so long.
786.m: The young learn from their mother for years.

787.q: How does the Alpine newt defend itself against enemies?
a: Its skin gives off slightly poisonous substances
787.e: The skin of many newts and salamanders contains glands that release a slightly poisonous secretion when in danger. This protects them from some predators.
787.m: The skin protects with a mild poison.

788.q: How many legs does an adult earwig have?
788.e: Like all insects, the earwig has six legs. They are all attached to its thorax.

789.q: Which wild animal is the domestic llama descended from?
789.e: The domestic llama was bred from the wild guanaco. The guanaco still lives in South America today.
789.m: The guanaco is the wild form of the llama.

790.q: How many stomach chambers do alpacas have?
790.e: Camelids have a stomach with three chambers. Cattle, on the other hand, have four.

791.q: What do newly hatched grass snakes look like?
a: Like small versions of their parents
791.e: They are about 15 to 20 centimetres long. They have to look after themselves straight away.
791.m: The young are small copies of the adults.

792.q: In lynx, who looks after the young?
792.e: Male lynx do not help to raise the young. The mother raises her young alone and teaches them to hunt.
792.m: The mother raises the young alone.

793.q: What does the earthworm have on its body to grip the soil?
793.e: The earthworm has tiny bristles on each segment of its body. With these it can grip its tunnel when it moves.

794.q: What often attracts dung beetles to pastures in the evening?
794.e: Many species fly at dusk. They follow the smell of dung and then land nearby.
794.m: The smell of dung attracts the beetles.

795.q: What does the mirror test show in elephants?
a: Some recognise themselves in the mirror
They see nothing in the mirror
795.e: An Asian elephant has shown in the mirror test that it recognises itself. This is considered a sign of high intelligence.
795.m: Elephants recognise themselves in the mirror.

796.q: What is it better not to give a mute swan in the park?
796.e: Bread is unhealthy for swans and can make them ill. Natural food such as grass or plants is better.
796.m: Bread harms swans, so it is better not to feed them bread.

797.q: How do grey herons usually behave towards each other outside the breeding season?
a: They always hunt together in large groups
They fight each other all the time
They roam in packs like wolves
797.e: When hunting for fish, the grey heron is usually out on its own. Only in the breeding season do many birds gather in a colony.
797.m: When hunting it is usually on its own.

798.q: What does the Alpine salamander mainly use its short legs for?
a: Digging deep tunnels like a mole
798.e: The short, strong legs help the Alpine salamander to move over uneven, stony ground. They are not suited to swimming long distances.
798.m: Short legs help with climbing over stones.

799.q: What does the plumage of a young golden eagle look like compared with an adult?
a: It has striking white patches on the wings and tail
It is exactly the same as the adult's
799.e: Young golden eagles have clear white patches on the undersides of their wings and on their tail, which disappear as they get older. Only after a few years do they have the darker adult plumage.
799.m: Young birds show white patches in their plumage.

800.q: Which animal is heavier than any known dinosaur?
800.e: A blue whale can weigh up to 150 tonnes. Even the largest known dinosaurs were probably lighter.
800.m: The blue whale is heavier than any dinosaur.

801.q: How does a koala prefer to move about?
801.e: Koalas spend almost their whole life in trees and climb skilfully from branch to branch. On the ground they move rather slowly.

802.q: How many main parts does a grasshopper's body consist of?
a: Three parts: head, thorax and abdomen
802.e: As in all insects, the body consists of head, thorax and abdomen. The legs and wings are attached to the thorax.
802.m: Insects have a head, thorax and abdomen.

803.q: What colour is the skin of a common toad usually?
803.e: The common toad is usually brown or grey. This lets it hide well among leaves and on the ground.
803.m: Common toads wear inconspicuous brown camouflage.

804.q: What does the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC) do?
a: It supports projects in poorer countries
804.e: The SDC is part of the Federal Department of Foreign Affairs and funds projects that reduce poverty or promote education, for example in Africa or Asia. In this way Switzerland takes part in international development cooperation.
804.m: The SDC supports development projects abroad.

805.q: What especially hinders lake trout swimming up to their spawning streams?
805.e: Structures across the river such as weirs and walls block the fish's way upstream. As a result they often don't reach their spawning grounds.
805.m: Weirs block the way to the spawning grounds.

806.q: Which fruit is one of a chimpanzee's favourite treats?
806.e: Figs are especially popular with chimpanzees. In the forest they eat many different fruits from the trees.
806.m: Figs are among their favourite fruits.

807.q: How many fingers does the Alpine salamander typically have on its front legs?
807.e: Like many other salamander species, the Alpine salamander has four fingers on its front legs and five toes on its back legs. This is typical of newts and salamanders.
807.m: At the front it has four fingers.

808.q: What does a bee release into the skin when it stings?
808.e: Bee venom makes the sting hurt and can make it swell. For most people a sting is unpleasant but not dangerous.
808.m: When it stings, the bee releases venom.

809.q: Why do goats have such a good grip when climbing in the mountains?
a: Their hooves can adapt well to the rock
They have suckers on their feet
They have claws like a cat
809.e: A goat's hooves have hard edges and soft pads. This lets them adapt to stones so they hardly slip.
809.m: Goat hooves grip well on rock.

810.q: In which area of Switzerland were the first bearded vultures released back into the wild?
a: In the Jura and Central Plateau
810.e: From 1991, young bearded vultures were released in the Swiss National Park in the Engadine. From there they slowly spread across the Alps again.
810.m: The National Park was the starting point of their return.

811.q: What was a “Five-Year Plan” in the Soviet Union?
a: A state economic plan that set production targets for five years
A school plan for five years
811.e: With Five-Year Plans the Soviet government wanted to build up industry quickly. The state decided exactly what should be produced and how much.

812.q: How long do adult dragonflies usually live in our part of the world?
a: A few weeks to a few months
812.e: The adult insect usually only flies for one season. During this time it mates and lays eggs.
812.m: Adult dragonflies only live a short time.

813.q: What does the lynx do with remains of prey that it does not eat straight away?
a: It hides them under leaves or snow and comes back later
It always just leaves them lying
It shares them with other lynx
It takes them to its young in their hiding place
813.e: Lynx often cover leftover prey with leaves, earth or snow. This way they come back over several days to carry on eating.

814.q: How do you measure the size of a horse?
a: By its height at the withers in centimetres
With a tape measure round its belly
By the number of its teeth
814.e: A horse's height is measured from the ground to the withers. This makes it easy to compare horses.
814.m: A horse's size is measured as its height at the withers.

815.q: Some small animals just let larger animals carry them around. What happens to the carrier animal?
815.e: The larger animal only serves as a taxi. Mites, for example, travel on dung beetles to fresh dung without harming the beetle.
815.m: Hitching a ride does not harm the carrier.

816.q: Roughly how heavy does an adult cheetah get?
816.e: An adult cheetah usually weighs between 40 and 60 kilograms. That makes it lighter than a lion or a tiger.

817.q: What is a baby goat called?
817.e: A young goat is called a kid. It can stand shortly after birth.
817.m: A baby goat is called a kid.

818.q: Roughly how old can a roe deer get in the wild?
818.e: In the wild, roe deer usually don't get very old because they face many dangers. About 10 years already counts as a great age.
818.m: Wild roe deer live to about 10 years.

820.q: What colour are the small spots on the body of a brown trout usually?
820.e: The brown trout often has red and black spots on its body. These spots also help with camouflage.
820.m: Brown trout have red and black spots.

821.q: What happens when a bee colony gets too big for its hive?
a: Part of it swarms out and looks for a new home
821.e: When the hive gets too full, part of the colony flies out with the old queen. Together they then look for a new home.

822.q: Roughly how heavy can a Malayan tapir get at most?
822.e: The Malayan tapir is the largest tapir species and can weigh up to about 500 kilograms. The other species are somewhat lighter.
822.m: The Malayan tapir is the largest species.

823.q: What does the perch breathe with?
823.e: The perch takes oxygen from the water with its gills. It does not need to come up to the surface for this.

824.q: Where do the burrows that stoats live in often come from?
a: From the rodents they have caught
They always build everything new themselves
From abandoned birds' nests high in trees
824.e: Stoats like to take over the burrows of mice or voles that they have caught. This saves them a lot of work building a nest.
824.m: The stoat takes over its prey's burrows.

825.q: What role does the bison play in the prairie ecosystem?
a: It grazes the grass and keeps areas open
825.e: Its eating and trampling create varied grasslands. Many plants and animals benefit from this.

826.q: Which kind of tiger is the largest of all?
826.e: The Siberian tiger, also called the Amur tiger, is the largest tiger subspecies. It lives in the cold east of Russia.
826.m: The Siberian tiger is the largest.

827.q: What is considered proof of the raven's high intelligence?
a: It can use tools to get food
827.e: Ravens sometimes use objects on purpose to get food that is hard to reach. Such abilities are considered a sign of above-average intelligence in animals.

828.q: What makes the star-nosed mole from North America different from the European mole?
a: It has star-shaped feelers on its nose
It can fly like a bird
It has huge ears like a hare
828.e: The star-nosed mole is a relative of the mole that lives in North America. On its nose it has a ring of star-shaped feelers with which it detects prey in a flash.
828.m: The star-nosed mole has a star-shaped nose.

829.q: What colour is the beak of an adult grey heron usually?
829.e: The grey heron's strong beak is usually yellowish. It is long, pointed and ideal for spearing prey.

830.q: What colour is the fur of an adult harbour seal usually?
830.e: A harbour seal's fur is usually grey or brown with lots of small spots. Every harbour seal has a slightly different pattern of spots.

831.q: What do the dark patches in the giraffe's coat help with?
831.e: Under the dark patches there are many blood vessels close to the skin. There the giraffe can give off excess body heat more easily.
831.m: The patches help giraffes cool down.

832.q: How many pairs of legs does the garden spider have?
832.e: Eight legs make four pairs of legs. Each pair helps the spider to walk and hold on in its web.

833.q: Roughly how long do alpacas live?
833.e: With good care, alpacas can live to about 15 to 20 years. That is similar to many larger pets.
833.m: Alpacas live to about 15 to 20 years.

834.q: What causes the buzzing of a flying housefly?
834.e: The buzzing happens because the housefly moves its wings up and down incredibly fast. The faster the wingbeat, the higher the sound.

835.q: Which birds, like the duck, belong to the waterfowl family?
835.e: Together with geese and swans, ducks belong to the waterfowl family. These birds usually live on or in water.
835.m: Ducks, geese and swans are waterfowl.

836.q: How many eggs does a magpie usually lay in a clutch?
836.e: A magpie's clutch usually has five to eight eggs. The female incubates them for about three weeks.
836.m: Magpies often lay five to eight eggs.

837.q: What colour is a giraffe's skin often under the patches?
837.e: Under the dark patches the giraffe's skin is often almost black. Many blood vessels run there too, which help the giraffe give off heat.
837.m: Under the giraffe's patches the skin is dark.

838.q: What do people in the desert use from dromedaries as food?
838.e: Camel milk is an important food for many desert peoples. The females provide it even in dry regions.

839.q: What is special about the claws of an eagle owl?
a: They are very strong and are used to grip and kill prey
They are soft and only used for climbing
They all fall out every year
They have shrunk completely and are useless
839.e: With its strong, sharp claws, called talons, the eagle owl grips and kills its prey. Its grip can be enormously powerful.
839.m: The eagle owl kills prey with strong claws.

840.q: Why does the cheetah have especially large nostrils?
a: So that it can take in a lot of air when running
So that it can smell better
So that it can roar louder
So that it can swim better
840.e: When running fast, the cheetah needs a great deal of oxygen. The large nostrils help it breathe fast enough.
840.m: Large nostrils help with fast breathing.

841.q: How many young does an otter mother usually have per litter?
841.e: An otter mother usually gives birth to two or three young. Sometimes there is only one, or up to four.
841.m: Usually two or three young per litter.

842.q: Roughly how many eggs can a female goldfish lay in a single spawning?
842.e: A female goldfish can lay several hundred to a thousand small eggs in one spawning. Only some of them later develop into young fish.
842.m: Goldfish lay a great many eggs.

843.q: Is the mallard a migratory bird or a resident bird?
a: Both are possible, depending on the area
It is always only a migratory bird
It always stays in the same place, without exception
843.e: Some mallards stay in one place all year, others move to warmer areas in winter. This depends a lot on whether there is enough open water.
843.m: Mallards are sometimes migratory, sometimes not.

844.q: What does the elephant mainly use its large ears for?
844.e: The large ears are full of blood vessels. When the elephant flaps them, the blood cools down and the whole body gets cooler.
844.m: Large ears help against the heat.

845.q: How does a kangaroo usually move about?
845.e: Kangaroos have strong back legs and hop forwards with them. This lets them move along very fast.

846.q: Which custom involving geese takes place in many areas in mid-November?
846.e: On St Martin's Day people traditionally eat a roast goose. This custom goes back to an old legend about Saint Martin.
846.m: On St Martin's Day people eat a St Martin's goose.

847.q: What colour is the underside of the stoat usually in summer?
847.e: In summer the stoat's underside is usually pale, yellowish white. Only its back shows the brown summer coat.
847.m: The underside is pale in summer.

848.q: How big can the home ranges of wild dog packs be?
a: Very big, often several hundred square kilometres
About as big as a football pitch
848.e: Wild dogs cover long distances and need a lot of space. That is why small nature reserves are often too small.

849.q: Which behaviour do otters especially like to show just for fun?
849.e: Otters are considered very playful animals and like sliding down muddy or snowy slopes into the water. In doing so they also practise important skills.
849.m: Otters love sliding just for fun.

850.q: What does a hedgehog's snout look like?
a: Short and round like a cat's
850.e: The hedgehog has a narrow, pointed snout, which it can use to root around in leaves and soil for food. This helps it to search for insects.
850.m: Hedgehogs have a long, pointed snout.

851.q: What is a female chamois called?
851.e: The female animal is called a nanny or doe. She is a bit smaller and lighter than the buck.

852.q: What is the female rabbit called?
852.e: The female rabbit is called a doe. Later she looks after her young in the nest.
852.m: The mother rabbit is called a doe.

853.q: Does a koala often drink a lot of water?
a: No, it hardly needs any water
853.e: Koalas get most of their water from the eucalyptus leaves they eat. That is why they only rarely need to drink.

854.q: How can you recognise a pike easily?
a: By the long barbels on its mouth
By a hump on its back
854.e: The long, flat snout is typical of the pike. It makes it easy to recognise.
854.m: The shape of its snout makes the pike recognisable.

855.q: Why are young stone martens only born in spring, even though the parents mate in summer?
a: The development inside the mother pauses for months
The mother hibernates for a long time
The young only hatch from eggs in spring
The mother waits until winter to mate
855.e: After mating in summer, the tiny embryo rests for several months. Only in winter does it grow further, so the young are born in spring, when there is plenty of food.
855.m: A long pause moves the birth to spring.

856.q: What sound does a stoat make when it feels threatened?
856.e: When a stoat feels threatened, it often makes loud hissing or screeching sounds. It uses them to try to scare off the attacker.
856.m: The stoat hisses when in danger.

857.q: How does a mother duck often call her ducklings?
a: With special sounds and quiet quacking
With a whistle like a bird whistle
She never calls; the ducklings come by themselves
857.e: Mother ducks constantly make quiet sounds so that the ducklings can hear and find them. This keeps the family together as they move about.
857.m: Mother ducks call their ducklings all the time.

858.q: How heavy does an adult hippopotamus usually get?
858.e: An adult hippo usually weighs well over 1000 kilograms. Large males can even weigh over three tonnes.
858.m: Hippos weigh more than a tonne.

859.q: What does the great tit do in severe cold to stay warm?
859.e: In the cold the great tit fluffs up its feathers. This creates a layer of air that keeps it warm like a down jacket.

860.e: A municipality is like a village or a town where people live. The people who live there can have a say on many questions.
860.m: The municipality is the smallest political unit.

861.q: What is a group of goats living together called?
861.e: Goats like living together in a herd. There they feel safer than on their own.

862.q: How does a trout move fastest in the water?
a: With powerful movements of its tail
862.e: The trout's tail is very strong. It beats it from side to side and so swims quickly forwards.
862.m: The tail drives the trout forward.

863.q: On which cards do you often see the robin, especially in the snow?
863.e: Because of its pretty red breast, the robin is often painted on Christmas cards, especially in the snow. Many people see it as a winter bird.
863.m: Robins are popular on Christmas cards.

864.q: What makes wels catfish important for lakes and rivers?
a: As predatory fish they regulate other fish populations
They fertilise the bank with seeds
864.e: As predatory fish, wels catfish influence the number of other fish. This helps keep the waters in balance.
864.m: Predatory fish keep populations in balance.

865.q: What does the great tit do with large caterpillars before it eats them?
a: It pecks them into small pieces with its beak
It buries them in the ground first
865.e: With its strong beak the great tit pecks insects and caterpillars into small pieces. This makes them easier to swallow.
865.m: The beak pecks the food into small pieces.

866.q: What do dolphin mothers sometimes do to teach their calf to hunt?
a: They show it how to catch fish
They let it learn about fish from a book
866.e: Young dolphins learn how to hunt by watching their mother. In this way they pick up important skills for surviving in the sea.
866.m: Dolphin calves learn hunting from their mother.

867.q: Which animal has a very long neck to eat leaves from tall trees?
867.e: The giraffe is the tallest land animal alive today and lives in Africa. Its long neck helps it reach leaves that other animals can't.
867.m: The giraffe has the longest neck.

868.q: What does a wild boar do when it is agitated?
a: It raises the bristles on its back
It wags its tail like a dog
868.e: When a wild boar is agitated or threatened, it raises the bristles on its back. You can see this even from a distance.

869.q: Which habitats does the brown bear live in around the world?
869.e: Brown bears live in very different habitats, including dense forests, mountain regions and cold tundra. They are found on several continents in the northern hemisphere.
869.m: Brown bears live in forests and mountains.

870.q: What do you call several cows that live together in a field?
870.e: Several cows that live together are called a herd. In the herd there is often a pecking order too.
870.m: Many cows together are a herd.

871.q: What do you call several roe deer that move about together in winter?
871.e: A small group of roe deer in winter is called a bevy. It usually consists of a mother with her fawns and other animals.
871.m: A group of roe deer is called a bevy.

873.q: What does the ‘militia system’ mean in Swiss politics?
a: Many politicians do their political job alongside another job
Politics is a full-time main job for everyone
873.e: In Switzerland many politicians, especially in municipalities and in parliament, do this work part-time.
873.m: Politics is often a part-time job.

874.q: What does a starfish sense with its tiny tube feet?
874.e: With its tube feet the starfish can detect the smell of food. This is how it finds mussels, for example.

875.q: In which baboon do the males have a silvery grey mane like a cape?
875.e: Male hamadryas baboons have a long, silvery grey mane over their shoulders and back. It looks like a cloak.
875.m: The hamadryas baboon wears a mane like a cloak.

876.q: What is the consequence of the Alpine salamander having so few young?
a: Populations recover only slowly after losses
As a result there are no more predators
Because of this the species never dies out
876.e: Because only one or two young are born at a time and their development takes a long time, Alpine salamander populations grow only slowly. This makes losses especially serious.

877.q: What are the loud calls of deer and moose in the rutting season called?
877.e: During the rut the bulls call loudly and deeply. They use this to attract females and warn rivals.
877.m: Bulls in the rut roar loudly.

878.q: What do mute swans usually do when people come too close to their young?
878.e: A hissing sound is a clear warning from the swan. It shows that you should keep your distance.

881.q: Roughly how big does the body of an adult garden spider get?
a: About the size of a fingernail
As big as a whole hand
As small as a speck of dust
881.e: The body of an adult garden spider is usually one to two centimetres long. With its legs it looks a bit bigger.
881.m: The body is only a few centimetres big.

882.q: Roughly how old can brown bears get in the wild?
882.e: In the wild, brown bears often reach an age of 20 to 30 years. In captivity they can sometimes live even a little longer.
882.m: Brown bears can live to over twenty.

883.q: What call does the grey heron typically make?
883.e: The grey heron's call sounds rough and croaky, especially when it takes off. You often hear it before you see the bird.
883.m: Its call sounds rough and croaky.

884.q: At about what age are carrion crows old enough to breed?
884.e: Carrion crows are usually old enough to breed at two to three years and can then start a family of their own. Before that, many young crows still live in loose groups.
884.m: Crows usually breed from the age of two.

885.q: Can you also see hippos in a Swiss zoo?
a: Yes, for example at Basel Zoo
No, they only live in the wild
885.e: In Switzerland you can see hippos in some zoos, for example at Basel Zoo. There they have large pools of water.
885.m: Hippos also live in Swiss zoos.

886.q: Which country has the most wild polar bears?
886.e: Most of the world's wild polar bears live in Canada. There are many coasts with pack ice there.
886.m: Most polar bears live in Canada.

887.q: Where does the female common earwig lay her eggs?
a: In a hollow in the ground
On leaves at the top of a tree
In the water of a pond
887.e: The female digs a small nest in the soil. There the eggs are protected.
887.m: The eggs lie in a hollow in the soil.

888.q: Which animal is one of the natural enemies of ducklings?
888.e: Ducklings are small and still defenceless. The fox and some birds of prey are among their natural enemies.

889.q: Which bird family does the peregrine falcon belong to?
889.e: The peregrine falcon belongs to the falcon family. This family includes several fast, skilful hunting birds.

890.q: What is the largest species of cat in the world called?
890.e: The tiger is the largest of all cat species. It can grow even bigger than a lion.
890.m: The tiger is the largest cat.

891.q: What striking feature do many male blackbirds have around their eyes?
891.e: Around the eye of many male blackbirds you can see a narrow yellow ring. It matches the colour of the beak well.
891.m: The male has a yellow eye ring.

892.q: What do some ducks do when lakes and rivers freeze over in winter?
a: They move to waters that don't freeze
They dig themselves into the ground
892.e: When their water freezes over, ducks fly to open places or warmer areas. There they can still find water and food.

893.q: In North America, what is the animal called that used to be often wrongly called a buffalo?
893.e: In North America people often say buffalo, but they are actually bison. True buffalo live in Asia and Africa.
893.m: The American buffalo is a bison.

894.q: When is a squirrel usually active?
a: During the day, especially in the morning and evening
Only in the middle of the night
894.e: Squirrels are active during the day and are out and about especially in the morning and evening. At night they usually rest in their drey.
894.m: Squirrels are active during the day.

895.q: What do you usually feel when you touch a lion's mane jellyfish?
a: A strong burning on the skin
895.e: The lion's mane jellyfish has a strong stinging venom. If you touch it, you feel a burning, stinging sensation on your skin.
895.m: The lion's mane jellyfish causes a strong burning.

896.q: How do male ibex fight over females during the rutting season?
a: They rear up on their hind legs and crash their horns together
They race each other up the mountain
They fight with loud roars without touching
896.e: In contests, ibex rear up on their hind legs and crash their heavy horns together with great force. You can often hear it from far away.

897.q: How do adult golden eagles behave towards their territory over the year?
a: They usually stay in the same area all year
They fly to Africa every winter
They leave the territory for ever after each brood
897.e: Golden eagles in the Alps are resident birds and usually stay in their traditional territory all year round. Only young eagles that have not yet settled roam about to some extent.
897.m: Golden eagles stay put all year.

898.q: Where do ladybirds often spend the winter together in large groups?
a: Under tree bark or in piles of leaves
In the middle of the road
In the water of a stream
On high mountain peaks in the snow
898.e: In winter many ladybirds look for a sheltered hiding place together, for example under loose bark. There they huddle close together until it gets warmer again.
898.m: Many ladybirds spend the winter together.

899.q: How can you recognise a female stag beetle?
a: It only has small upper jaws
It has four pairs of wings
It has a sting on its abdomen
899.e: Females are usually smaller and their jaws are short. They can still give a good pinch.

900.e: Unlike in votes, children and teenagers may also take part in a petition. This way everyone can show their opinion.

901.q: What happened to the otter in Switzerland in the last century?
a: It was almost completely wiped out and is only slowly returning
It was never hunted and was always very common
It has always been a popular pet
It only arrived in Switzerland a few years ago
901.e: Because of hunting and polluted waters, the otter almost completely disappeared from Switzerland for a long time. Thanks to clean waters and protection measures, it is slowly coming back today.
901.m: Otters are slowly returning to Switzerland.

902.q: What happens to the roe buck's antlers every year?
a: They fall off and grow again
They stay the same for ever
902.e: In winter the roe buck loses its antlers. After that, new ones grow.
902.m: The antlers grow again every year.

903.q: In which season do you see ladybirds most often?
903.e: When it gets warm, ladybirds wake up from their winter torpor and become active. Then they hunt for aphids on plants.
903.m: Spring and summer are ladybird time.

905.q: How many hours a day does a panda usually spend eating?
905.e: Because bamboo gives little energy, the panda has to eat a great deal of it. That is why it eats almost all day.

906.q: Which group of animals do baboons belong to?
906.e: Baboons belong to the guenon family and therefore to the Old World monkeys. They live in Africa and in the south-west of the Arabian Peninsula.

907.q: Why can houseflies multiply so quickly in summer?
a: Because warmth speeds up their development
Because they don't lay eggs in summer
Because there are no predators in summer
907.e: In warm weather the eggs and maggots develop much faster than in the cold. That is why there are often a great many houseflies in summer.

908.q: How many young does a cat usually have per litter?
908.e: A cat usually gives birth to between four and six kittens at a time. The little kittens are still blind at birth.
908.m: A litter usually has four to six kittens.

909.q: Apart from running and jumping, what ability does a stoat have?
a: It can walk backwards like a crab
909.e: Stoats are surprisingly good swimmers and cross streams when they need to. This helps them reach new hunting grounds.

910.q: Roughly how long can a female orca live?
a: Often over 50 years, sometimes even 80 to 90 years
910.e: Female orcas can get very old, sometimes as old as a human. Males usually don't live quite as long.
910.m: Female orcas can get very old.

911.q: Which parents take turns incubating the eggs in the bearded vulture?
911.e: Both parents share the care of the eggs and take turns sitting on them. This way one parent can always look for food.

912.q: What are the fine hairs on the legs of the pond skater for?
912.e: The hairs are water-repellent, so the legs don't get wet. This keeps the pond skater on the surface.
912.m: Water-repellent hairs keep the legs dry.

913.q: Where does the koala get most of its water from?
a: From the eucalyptus leaves it eats
913.e: Eucalyptus leaves contain a lot of moisture, which provides the koala with most of its water. That is why it only rarely needs to drink.
913.m: The leaves give the koala water.

914.q: What do you often notice when you see a kestrel sitting on an electricity pylon?
a: It is looking out for mice in the grass nearby
It is charging up its energy for flying
It is waiting for other birds to bring it food
It is sleeping there for several hours during the day
914.e: Electricity pylons give the kestrel a raised perch with a good view all round. From there it calmly watches the surrounding ground for prey.
914.m: Pylons serve as a lookout when hunting.

915.q: What does the bumblebee feed its larvae with?
915.e: The larvae in the nest are given pollen and nectar to eat by the workers. This makes them grow quickly.
915.m: The larvae are given pollen and nectar.

916.q: How big can a fully grown carp get?
916.e: Some carp grow very big and heavy, more than a metre long. But it takes them many years to get that big.

917.q: What helps the red fox most when it catches mice in the snow?
917.e: Foxes can hear mice rustling even under a thick layer of snow. Then they leap high into the air and dive head first into the snow.
917.m: Foxes can hear mice under the snow.

919.q: What do great crested grebe chicks love to do soon after hatching?
a: They ride on their parents’ backs
They build their own nest straight away
They fly after just a few hours
They bury themselves in the mud
919.e: The chicks like to climb onto a parent’s back, where they are protected and kept warm. They often stay there even while the parent looks for food.
919.m: Chicks love riding on their parents.

920.q: How much can an ant carry compared with its own weight?
a: Exactly as much as it weighs
920.e: Ants are incredibly strong. They can carry much more than they weigh themselves.

921.q: Why do woodlice often gather in groups?
a: In groups it stays damper and they are better protected
Because they form a colony like ants
921.e: Huddled close together, woodlice lose less moisture. However, they do not form a colony where jobs are shared.
921.m: Groups protect woodlice from drying out.

922.q: Which habitat does the chamois like best?
922.e: Chamois are perfectly adapted to steep, rocky mountain landscapes. There they find shelter and can climb quickly.

923.q: How many eyes does a garden cross spider have?
923.e: The garden cross spider has eight small eyes on the front part of its body. Even so, it does not see very sharply.

924.q: What is the name of the smallest and most endangered lynx in the world?
924.e: The Iberian lynx now lives only in small populations on the Iberian Peninsula. It is one of the most endangered cat species in the world.
924.m: The Iberian lynx is highly endangered.

926.q: What does a hamster often do when it gets a fright?
a: It stands up on its back legs and hisses
It lies flat and goes to sleep
926.e: A frightened hamster may rear up, hiss or even bite. This is how it shows that it is scared.

927.q: What sound do reindeer often make when they walk?
927.e: When reindeer walk, the tendons in their legs crack or click. This helps animals in the herd stay in touch during a snowstorm.

928.q: What colour is the head of a male mallard, the drake?
928.e: The drake has a bright green head that shines in the sun. This makes it easy to recognise from far away.

929.q: What do meerkats mainly use their long claws for?
929.e: Their strong claws are good for digging burrows and scratching for food. They are not built for climbing.
929.m: They dig tunnels with their claws.

930.q: Where can the edible dormouse sometimes cause trouble for homeowners?
a: In lofts, where it gnaws on cables
In the cellar, where it drinks water
In the garden, where it eats flowers
In the cowshed, where it bothers the cows
930.e: Edible dormice sometimes move into lofts and gnaw on cables or insulation there. This can be annoying for homeowners.
930.m: In lofts it sometimes gnaws on cables.

932.q: What is a baby rhino called?
932.e: A young rhino is called a calf, just like a baby elephant. It stays with its mother for a long time.
932.m: A baby rhino is called a calf.

933.q: What does a red fox like to eat most?
a: Mice, birds, insects, fruit and berries
933.e: The red fox is an omnivore and eats very different things depending on the season. In autumn it also enjoys ripe berries and fallen fruit.

934.q: What happens when a fox hears people or dogs in a garden at night?
a: It usually runs away quickly and quietly
It stands still and barks back loudly
It calls its whole family to fight
934.e: When a fox is surprised, it would rather run away quickly and silently than risk a fight. By nature it is more cautious than brave.
934.m: Foxes would rather flee than fight.

935.q: Why can cats still see well in very little light?
a: A special layer in the eye (tapetum lucidum) boosts the light
They smell their surroundings and need no light
935.e: Behind the retina, cats have a mirror-like layer called the tapetum lucidum. It reflects incoming light back and greatly improves night vision.
935.m: The tapetum lucidum improves night vision.

936.q: Which sense helps reindeer find lichen under the snow?
936.e: Reindeer can smell food even under a layer of snow. That way they know where it is worth scraping.

937.q: Roughly how much does an adult bearded vulture weigh?
937.e: Despite its huge wingspan, a bearded vulture weighs only about five to seven kilograms. Its body is built very light for efficient flying.
937.m: A light body despite big wings.

938.q: What is the meeting called where all the residents of a municipality gather to make decisions?
938.e: In many small municipalities the voters meet and decide together, often by a show of hands.
938.m: Deciding together at the municipal assembly.

939.q: What role does the herd play for a buffalo calf?
939.e: In the middle of the herd, calves are better protected. That makes things harder for lions.

940.q: Which animals are enemies of the common toad?
a: Grass snakes, hedgehogs and grey herons
940.e: Grass snakes, hedgehogs and some birds such as the grey heron eat common toads. So despite its poison, the toad is not completely safe.

941.q: Which two main species of gorilla do scientists distinguish?
941.e: There is the western gorilla and the eastern gorilla. They live in different parts of Africa.
941.m: There are two main species of gorilla.

942.q: In which canton were women only given the vote in 1990, by a court ruling?
942.e: Appenzell Innerrhoden was the last canton to give women the vote, and only after a ruling by the Federal Supreme Court.
942.m: Appenzell Innerrhoden was the last canton to give women the vote, in 1990.

944.q: What covers the body of a carp?
a: Bare, smooth skin with nothing on it
944.e: The carp’s body is covered with scales that protect it. The scales often shine golden or brownish.

945.q: What is the oldest age a raven can reach in human care?
945.e: In captivity, for example in zoos, ravens can live much longer than in the wild because there are no dangers and they are well looked after. Ages of over 40 years have been recorded.
945.m: Over 40 years is possible in captivity.

946.q: Where does the wood mouse like to live best?
a: Only high in the mountains above the snow line
946.e: The wood mouse feels at home wherever there are plants and hiding places. It is found most often in woods, hedges and gardens.
946.m: The wood mouse lives in woods and gardens.

947.q: How many young does a female chamois usually have?
947.e: A female chamois usually has only one kid a year. Twins are rare.
947.m: Female chamois usually have just one kid.

948.q: How often does the common earwig fly?
948.e: It has working wings but hardly uses them. Most of the time it prefers to walk.
948.m: It can fly but rarely does.

949.q: How are the jaguar’s legs built compared with other big cats?
949.e: The jaguar has a stocky, muscular build. This helps it climb, swim and overpower prey.

950.q: Does the golden eagle also eat carrion as well as live prey?
a: Yes, sometimes it eats dead animals too
950.e: Golden eagles are flexible hunters and will eat carrion when they get the chance, especially in winter when live prey is scarce. So they are not pure hunters.
950.m: Golden eagles sometimes eat carrion too.

951.q: In what state are young stone martens born?
a: With open eyes and full fur
951.e: Like many young predators, stone martens are born blind and without fur. That is why they need a lot of care from their mother.
951.m: Young stone martens are born blind.

952.q: Does a chimpanzee have a tail?
a: Yes, but only a short stump
Yes, a gripping tail like some monkeys
952.e: Chimpanzees are great apes and, like humans, have no tail. This makes them different from many other kinds of monkey.

953.q: Which habitat suits the black-backed jackal?
953.e: It lives in open and partly open landscapes in Africa. There it finds food and places for its den.

954.q: What does a cow like to eat most?
954.e: Cows are herbivores and like to eat grass in the field or hay in the barn best. Grass gives them lots of energy.

955.q: Roughly how long is a stone marten’s body, without the tail?
955.e: A stone marten’s body usually measures around 45 centimetres. On top of that comes a bushy tail of about 25 centimetres.
955.m: Stone martens are about as long as a cat.

956.q: Whose old nest does the red kite sometimes use as a base for its own eyrie?
956.e: Instead of always building from scratch, the red kite likes to use old nests of crows or other birds of prey and add to them. This saves it time and energy.
956.m: The red kite often builds on old crows’ nests.

957.q: How do gibbons move on the ground when they do walk?
a: Upright on their back legs, with their arms raised for balance
On all fours with their belly on the ground
957.e: On the ground, gibbons usually walk on two legs and hold their arms up for balance. But they are only rarely on the ground.
957.m: On the ground, gibbons walk upright.

958.q: What does the snow leopard use its very long tail for?
a: For balance and as a warm blanket
958.e: The tail helps it keep its balance on steep rocks. When resting, the animal wraps it around its body and face to keep warm.

959.q: What is the difference between an otter and a beaver?
a: The otter eats fish, the beaver eats plants
959.e: While the otter is a predator and eats fish, the beaver eats plants such as bark and twigs. Both live near water, but they are very different animals.
959.m: Otters eat fish, beavers eat plants.

960.q: Roughly how big is a cuckoo compared with other birds?
a: About as big as a pigeon, but slimmer
960.e: The cuckoo is about as long as a pigeon but looks slimmer because of its long tail and narrow shape. It weighs much less than a pigeon.
960.m: A cuckoo is pigeon-sized but slim.

961.q: Where does the housefly especially like to be, as its name suggests?
961.e: The housefly likes to live near people, in houses, stables and kitchens.
961.m: The housefly likes to live near people.

962.q: What stops a pond skater from sinking into the water?
a: The surface tension of the water
962.e: The surface of the water acts like a thin, stretchy skin. The light pond skater only presses it down a little and is carried.
962.m: The water surface carries the light body.

963.q: What happens if a swift accidentally lands on the ground?
a: It often struggles to take off again
It digs itself in straight away
963.e: Because of its short legs and long wings, the swift has hardly any chance to build up speed on flat ground. It often needs help or a raised place to take off.
963.m: Taking off from the ground is very hard for it.

964.q: Which sea turtle has a particularly strong beak for cracking shellfish?
964.e: The loggerhead turtle has very strong jaws. It uses them to crack hard shellfish and crabs. The leatherback mainly eats jellyfish, and the green turtle eats seagrass.
964.m: A strong beak cracks hard shellfish.

965.q: What does a jellyfish mostly feed on?
965.e: Jellyfish use their tentacles to catch small fish, crustaceans and tiny living things called plankton.
965.m: Jellyfish eat plankton and small fish.

966.q: How many legs does a stork often stand on when it rests?
a: Always on both legs, stretched out
966.e: You often see storks standing on one leg with the other one tucked up. This saves warmth and energy.
966.m: Storks often stand on one leg.

967.q: How do eagle owls usually react when people disturb them near their nesting site?
a: Very sensitively, they may even abandon their eggs
Not at all, they are never disturbed
They move to another town straight away
967.e: Eagle owls are sensitive to disturbance near their nesting site and, in the worst case, may even give up their brood. That is why it is important to leave known nesting cliffs in peace.
967.m: Disturbance can put eagle owl broods at risk.

968.q: What is the larva of a housefly called?
968.e: The larva of the housefly is called a maggot. It is white, has no legs and eats its way through its surroundings.
968.m: A fly’s larva is called a maggot.

969.q: Why is the least weasel useful for farming?
a: It keeps the mouse population down naturally
It spreads diseases among farm animals
969.e: Since mice can damage fields, the least weasel helps as a natural enemy. So farmers benefit indirectly from this small hunter.
969.m: Least weasels help against plagues of mice.

970.q: What do many zoos do to give penguins a good home?
a: They build cool pools with rocks to climb on
They keep them in desert enclosures
They let them fly around freely
970.e: Penguins in zoos need cool water to swim in and rocks to waddle on. That way they feel at home, as in their natural habitat.
970.m: Zoos build cool pools for penguins.

971.q: How does an elk defend itself against a wolf?
a: With powerful kicks of its front legs
971.e: Elk lash out with their hooves. This can seriously injure attackers.
971.m: Elk defend themselves with their hooves.

973.q: Where does the common frog lay its eggs in spring?
a: Under a stone in the forest
973.e: In spring, common frogs travel to ponds. There the females lay their eggs in the water in large clumps.
973.m: Many clumps of spawn can lie in the same pond.

974.q: What does the hedgehog do in winter?
a: It stays awake and keeps hunting
974.e: When it gets cold, the hedgehog can no longer find food, so it hibernates. This saves energy until spring.

975.q: What keeps a polar bear warm in icy water?
975.e: Under its skin, the polar bear has a thick layer of fat. It keeps it warm even when swimming in icy water.
975.m: Fat keeps the polar bear warm in the water.

976.q: What happens to young male elephants when they grow up?
a: They stay with their mother forever
They look after the herd’s calves
976.e: When male elephants grow up, they leave the family herd. They then usually live alone or with other bulls.

977.q: Which emperor penguin usually keeps the egg warm?
a: Both parents at the same time
977.e: In emperor penguins, the male carries the egg on its feet and keeps it warm under a fold of skin. Meanwhile the female goes off to find food.
977.m: The male emperor penguin keeps the egg warm.

978.q: How small can the world’s smallest octopus be?
978.e: There are tiny kinds of octopus that grow only a few centimetres long. Some would even fit in your hand.

979.q: Which kind of hyena is the biggest?
979.e: The spotted hyena grows much bigger than the other kinds. Adults often weigh 40 to 80 kilograms.
979.m: The spotted hyena is the biggest hyena.

981.q: What does an elephant use its trunk for when greeting others of its kind?
981.e: Elephants often touch each other with their trunks. This is how they greet each other and recognise each other by smell.
981.m: The trunk is also used for greeting.

982.q: On which continents do magpies or closely related species live?
982.e: The magpie and its close relatives are found across large parts of Europe and Asia, and related species also live in North America. This makes it one of the most widespread members of the crow family.
982.m: Magpies and their relatives live on several continents.

983.q: Why do dung beetles roll their dung ball away in as straight a line as possible?
a: To get it away from rivals quickly
983.e: Lots of beetles crowd around a dung heap. By taking a straight route, a beetle gets away quickly from rivals that might steal its ball.
983.m: Straight paths protect against ball thieves.

985.q: How small can the smallest kind of jellyfish be?
985.e: Some jellyfish are tiny and measure only a few millimetres. You can hardly see them in the sea.

986.q: Which group of vertebrates does the eel belong to?
986.e: The eel is a bony fish, even though it looks like a snake. It breathes with gills.
986.m: The eel is a fish, not a snake.

987.q: What does a ladybird do before it flies?
a: It first opens its hard wing cases to the side
It first runs off very fast
It dips into the water briefly
987.e: Before a ladybird takes off, it opens its hard wing cases. Only then can it spread the flying wings underneath and fly away.
987.m: First open the wing cases, then fly.

988.q: Which family does the African buffalo belong to?
988.e: The African buffalo is a bovid, like cattle and antelopes. Deer have antlers, not horns.
988.m: African buffalo are bovids, not deer.

989.q: What does a dog use to hear very quiet or high sounds that people cannot hear?
989.e: Dogs can hear much higher sounds than people and pick up noises from further away. Their ears are very mobile.

990.q: Are many kinds of sea turtle in danger today?
a: No, there are far too many of them
Only one single species is in danger
990.e: Sadly, many sea turtles are considered threatened or endangered. Reasons include fishing nets, plastic litter and destroyed beaches.
990.m: Many sea turtles are endangered today.

991.q: Where does the female European pond turtle lay her eggs?
a: In a pit she digs on land
Straight into the water on the bottom
In a nest of twigs in a tree
In a cave in the rocks
991.e: To do this, the female leaves the water and looks for sunny, loose soil. Afterwards she covers the eggs up again.
991.m: The eggs go into a pit on land.

992.q: What does a cat mainly use its miaow for?
992.e: Adult cats hardly miaow at each other, but they miaow a lot to people. This is how they have learnt to tell us what they want.
992.m: Miaowing is mainly meant for people.

993.q: What makes penguin feathers so waterproof?
a: They are packed tightly and oiled with fat
They are very long and soft
993.e: Penguin feathers lie very close together and are oiled with fat from a gland. This keeps the water out and the skin dry.
993.m: Dense, oiled feathers keep penguins dry.

994.q: How does a garden cross spider usually react to people?
a: It runs away or sits still
It jumps at people straight away
994.e: Garden cross spiders do not attack people. If you come close, it usually runs away or sits completely still.

995.q: Does the barn owl make a deep hooting call like some other owls?
a: Yes, that is exactly what it does
No, it barks like a dog
995.e: The barn owl does not hoot like some other kinds of owl. Its call sounds more like a loud screech.

996.q: How many species of orangutan are there today?
996.e: There is the Bornean orangutan, the Sumatran orangutan and the Tapanuli orangutan. The last one was described as a separate species in 2017.
996.m: There are three species of orangutan.

997.q: What does a fully grown wels catfish eat?
a: Fish, frogs, crayfish and sometimes water birds
997.e: The wels catfish is a predatory fish. It mainly eats fish, but also crayfish, frogs and occasionally small water birds.
997.m: The wels catfish is a predatory fish.

998.q: How does the grey heron sometimes behave towards people’s fish ponds?
a: It sometimes fishes there, which annoys pond owners
It destroys the ponds with its beak
It lays its eggs in them
998.e: Because the grey heron likes eating fish, it also visits artificial fish ponds. This can sometimes be a problem for pond owners.

a: A fork in a branch where it wedges cones
999.e: In a fork like this, the woodpecker holds a cone firmly so it can work on it more easily. This helps it get at the seeds.
999.m: That is where it wedges its cones.

1000.q: How do a duck’s feet help it swim?
a: With a wing on each foot
1000.e: A thin skin is stretched between the duck’s toes. This webbing works like a paddle in the water.

1001.q: How does a donkey often show that it gets on well with another donkey?
a: They often stand close together and doze side by side
They fight each other all the time
1001.e: Donkeys that are friends often stand close together, doze side by side and swish the flies away from each other with their tails. This shows their close bond.
1001.m: Donkeys that are friends stand close together.

1002.e: Depending on the species and the plant, aphids have different colours. Green aphids are well camouflaged on leaves.

1003.q: What does a wasp’s sting contain?
1003.e: When it stings, the wasp injects venom into the skin. That causes the burning pain.

1004.q: Which of a squirrel’s teeth keep growing all its life?
1004.e: A squirrel’s front gnawing teeth keep growing throughout its life. Gnawing keeps them at the right length.

1005.q: Which of these animals is a sign in the Chinese calendar?
1005.e: The Chinese calendar has twelve animal signs, and one of them is the rooster. Each animal year comes round again every twelve years.
1005.m: The rooster is a Chinese zodiac sign.

1006.q: Why are a horse’s nostrils especially large?
a: So it can breathe in lots of air when running
So it can neigh more loudly
1006.e: The large nostrils help the horse breathe lots of air in and out when it runs fast. This is important because horses are long-distance runners.

1007.q: Why is it important to clean a hamster’s cage regularly?
a: So the hamster gets more colours
So the hamster learns to fly
1007.e: A clean cage prevents illness and bad smells. The hamster also feels more comfortable.
1007.m: A clean cage keeps it healthy.

1008.q: How endangered is the ring-tailed lemur in the wild?
1008.e: The number of ring-tailed lemurs living in the wild is falling. That is why the species is listed as endangered on the Red List.
1008.m: Ring-tailed lemurs are endangered in the wild.

1009.q: What covers the barn owl’s face like a veil?
1009.e: Especially fine, white feathers grow all around the barn owl’s face. Together they form a heart-shaped disc called the facial disc.
1009.m: Fine feathers form the facial disc.

1010.q: How does a badger usually react when it meets a person?
a: It stands still and lets you stroke it
1010.e: Badgers are shy by nature and avoid contact with people. If they meet us, they usually vanish quickly into the undergrowth.

1011.q: What can happen if an earwig pinches a finger with its pincers?
1011.e: The pincers are usually too weak for human skin. At most you feel a slight pinch.
1011.m: The pinch is usually barely noticeable.

1012.q: Where in the world is the housefly found?
1012.e: The housefly lives almost all over the world, wherever people live. That is why it is called a species that follows humans.

1013.q: Who looks after bee colonies and harvests the honey?
1013.e: A beekeeper cares for the bee colonies, keeps them healthy and harvests the honey from the combs. There are many beekeepers in Switzerland too.
1013.m: The beekeeper looks after the bees.

1014.q: How does a peregrine falcon usually carry its prey after catching it?
a: Carried through the air in its talons
Swallowed into its crop and brought up again
Never moved, but eaten on the ground
1014.e: After a catch, the peregrine falcon usually carries its prey in its strong talons to a safe place to eat. There it plucks and eats it.

1015.q: How good is a badger’s eyesight?
1015.e: The badger does not see very well. Instead, it relies much more on its nose.

1016.q: What should you do before stroking a dog you do not know?
1016.e: You should always ask the owner first whether you may stroke the dog. That way the dog does not get a fright or feel threatened.

1017.q: Why is the bearded vulture considered important for the mountain ecosystem?
a: It clears away carcass remains that would otherwise be left lying
It spreads flower seeds in the Alps
1017.e: Because the bearded vulture also eats the large bones of dead animals, it helps with the natural ‘clean-up’ in the mountains. That is why it is seen as a kind of health inspector of the mountains.
1017.m: It clears bones from the mountains.

1018.q: How well does a lion see in the dark compared with people?
1018.e: Lions’ eyes are perfectly adapted to the night. This means they can hunt well even in low light.
1018.m: Lions see very well at night.

1019.q: Roughly how heavy can a large male tiger get?
1019.e: Large male tigers can weigh up to 300 kilograms. That is as heavy as several adults put together.
1019.m: A tiger can weigh up to 300 kilograms.

1020.q: How well can a common toad see on land?
a: Only in black and white and shapes
1020.e: The common toad’s eyes are well adapted to life on land. It can recognise prey and danger quite well with them.
1020.m: Common toads see well on land.

1021.q: What is the first thing a bumblebee queen does in spring?
a: She looks for a place for a new nest
She builds honeycombs straight away like a honeybee
1021.e: After hibernating, the queen wakes up and looks for a sheltered spot. There she lays the first eggs for her new colony.
1021.m: In spring the queen looks for a nest.

1022.q: What do we call animals that, like the alpaca, mainly eat plants?
1022.e: Herbivores feed on grasses, leaves and other plants. Cows and sheep are herbivores too.

1023.q: What colour is the European mantis usually?
1023.e: Green or brown matches plants and dry grass well. That way it hardly stands out.

1024.q: What is sensible when hiking in areas with adders?
a: Wear sturdy shoes and do not reach blindly into the grass
Lift stones with your bare hands
1024.e: Sturdy shoes protect against bites. You should also stay on the paths and not put your hands into hiding places.
1024.m: Sturdy shoes, never reach in blindly.

1025.e: By howling, wolves keep in touch with their pack and warn other packs away from their territory. The howling can be heard for kilometres.

1026.q: What does the law of conservation of energy say?
a: Energy can be neither created nor destroyed, only converted
Energy keeps appearing out of nothing
1026.e: In a closed system, the total energy always stays the same; it can only change into other forms, for example from kinetic energy into heat. This basic principle applies throughout physics.
1026.m: Energy never disappears, it changes form.

1027.q: What is it called when ducks lose their old feathers each year and grow new ones?
1027.e: Like many birds, ducks change their plumage once a year. This process is called moulting.
1027.m: When birds moult, new feathers grow.

1028.q: Where does the mallard build its nest?
a: On the ground, hidden in the grass near water
On a rock in the mountains
1028.e: The female looks for a well-hidden spot on the ground near the water. There she lines the nest with feathers.
1028.m: Nests are hidden on the ground.

1029.q: What does the alpine salamander do when its surroundings get very dry?
a: It hides so it does not dry out
It drinks large amounts of water from puddles
It changes the colour of its skin
1029.e: Because its skin has to stay moist, the alpine salamander retreats to shady, damp hiding places when it is dry. These animals cope badly with sun and dryness.
1029.m: When it is dry, it hides.

1030.q: How do many seahorse pairs live?
a: They live alone all their lives
1030.e: Some kinds of seahorse stay with the same partner for a long time. They even meet up again regularly.

1031.q: What does a harbour seal need its long whiskers for?
a: To feel fish in the water
1031.e: The whiskers are very sensitive. With them, the seal can feel the movements of fish in the water, even in murky, dark water.

1032.q: What did the jaguar mean to the Aztecs and the Maya?
a: It was seen as a sacred, powerful animal
1032.e: In the cultures of Central America, the jaguar was honoured as a symbol of strength. It appears in art, myths and orders of warriors.
1032.m: The jaguar was a sacred symbol of power.

1033.q: What does an elephant use its trunk for, among other things?
a: Only for singing like a bird
1033.e: The trunk is a combination of nose and upper lip. It is used as a gripping tool, for smelling and for sucking up water.
1033.m: The trunk is both nose and gripping arm.

1034.e: The cross reminds people of the death of Jesus on the cross. You find it on many churches and in Christian homes.
1034.m: The cross is the symbol of Christianity.

1035.q: Roughly how much does an adult bonobo weigh?
1035.e: Males are heavier than females. Overall, adult bonobos weigh about as much as a teenager or an adult human.

1036.q: In which area of Switzerland are you most likely to come across the alpine salamander?
a: In the Alps and the Pre-Alps
In the Swiss Plateau near big cities
Only in Ticino on the lakeshore
1036.e: As its name says, the alpine salamander lives mainly in the Alps and the Pre-Alps. You hardly ever find it in the lower parts of the Swiss Plateau.
1036.m: It lives mainly in the Alps.

1037.q: What does the great spotted woodpecker need its stiff tail for?
a: As a prop when climbing the trunk
1037.e: The tail presses against the bark and helps it not to fall off. This lets it sit upright on the trunk.
1037.m: The tail props it up on the tree.

1038.q: What else is a female hippo called?
1038.e: An adult female hippo is sometimes called a cow. She looks after her calf with great care.
1038.m: A female hippo is called a cow.

1039.q: Why do donkeys cope well with heat and little water?
a: Their ancestors lived in dry deserts
Their ancestors lived in the rainforest
Their ancestors lived at the North Pole
1039.e: The African wild ass, the ancestor of our domestic donkey, lived in dry desert areas. That is why donkeys still cope well with heat and little water today.

1040.q: How many young does a marmot mother usually have?
1040.e: A litter usually has two to four baby marmots. They are born naked and blind in the safety of the burrow.
1040.m: Marmots have only a few young per litter.

1041.q: How can you often tell that a carp is searching for food on the bottom of the water?
a: The water is stirred up and cloudy
1041.e: When a carp roots around on the bottom, it stirs up mud and small particles. This often makes the water cloudy.
1041.m: Carp rooting for food make the water cloudy.

1042.q: Which kind of ladybird has spread to Switzerland and can push out native species?
1042.e: The harlequin ladybird comes from Asia and was brought in to fight pests. Today it also lives in the wild here and eats the food of native ladybirds.
1042.m: The harlequin ladybird came from Asia.

1043.q: How does a swift look different from a pigeon in flight?
a: Its wings are narrow and curved like a sickle
Its wings are broad and rounded
It flies much more slowly than a pigeon
1043.e: Pigeons have broad, rounded wings, while the swift has narrow, curved, sickle-shaped wings. This makes it much faster and more agile in the air.
1043.m: Sickle-shaped wings set it apart from pigeons.

1044.q: Roughly how long do baby tapirs keep their striped pattern?
1044.e: After about six months, the pattern starts to fade. Then the animals look like the adults.
1044.m: The pattern disappears after a few months.

1045.q: How well can a mole see?
a: Very poorly, its eyes are tiny
Just as well as an eagle
It sees only colours, not shapes
1045.e: The mole’s eyes are tiny and almost hidden under its fur. It hardly needs them underground.

1046.q: Where do koalas live in the wild?
1046.e: Koalas are only found in Australia, mainly in the east of the country. There they live in eucalyptus forests.

1047.q: What does an otter’s fur look like?
1047.e: The otter’s fur is evenly brown and especially thick, which helps it stay warm even in cold water. On the belly it is often a bit lighter.

1048.q: How many entrances can a large badger sett have?
1048.e: An old badger sett is often extended over many years. This creates lots of entrances and tunnels.
1048.m: Badger setts often have many entrances.

1049.q: What hatches first from a housefly’s egg?
1049.e: First a white maggot without legs hatches from the egg. Only after some weeks does it turn into a fully grown fly.
1049.m: A maggot hatches from the egg.

1050.q: How do the whale shark and the basking shark feed, even though they are so huge?
a: They filter tiny creatures out of the water
1050.e: Both sharks swim through the water with their mouths open. This way they collect small living things such as plankton.
1050.m: Whale sharks and basking sharks filter their food.

1051.q: What can help protect orangutans in everyday life?
a: Choosing products with sustainable palm oil
1051.e: If you look for sustainably grown palm oil and labels, you can help reduce forest clearing. Less packaging and careful shopping also help.

1052.q: What are materials that do not conduct electricity called?
1052.e: Insulators such as rubber or plastic stop electricity flowing through them. That is why they are wrapped around cables for protection.
1052.m: Insulators stop the flow of electricity.

1053.q: How many eggs does a mute swan usually lay in a nest?
1053.e: A clutch usually has five to eight eggs. The female patiently sits on them until they hatch.
1053.m: Usually five to eight eggs in the nest.

1054.q: Which animal is part of the coat of arms of the Principality of Liechtenstein?
1054.e: Liechtenstein's coat of arms is divided into several fields. One of them shows a black eagle on a gold background. Above it sits the princely crown.
1054.m: Liechtenstein's coat of arms includes an eagle.

1055.q: An apple falls from a tree to the ground. What happens to the energy?
a: Potential energy is converted into kinetic energy
The apple creates new energy out of nothing
1055.e: While the apple hangs high up in the tree, it has stored potential energy. As it falls, this is gradually converted into kinetic energy.
1055.m: Falling converts potential energy into movement.

1056.q: What are the carrion crow’s different calls for?
a: For warning and communicating within the flock
They make no sounds at all
1056.e: Carrion crows use different calls to warn each other or to communicate within the flock. The calls sound different depending on the situation.

1057.q: What is the jellyfish called that is known for living a very long time and being able to turn back into a young form?
1057.e: The so-called immortal jellyfish can turn back into a young form when it is under stress. This way it sometimes escapes death.
1057.m: Some jellyfish can make themselves young again.

a: They sleep with only one half of the brain so they can keep breathing
They sleep for days without surfacing
1058.e: Orcas have to keep coming up to breathe. That is why only one half of their brain sleeps at a time.
1058.m: Orcas sleep with half their brain.

1059.q: Roughly how much does a mole weigh?
a: About as much as a bar of chocolate
Only a few grams, like a mosquito
1059.e: A mole usually weighs between 70 and 120 grams. That is about as much as a bar of chocolate.

1060.q: Which animal belongs, like the sand lizard, to the family of wall lizards (Lacertidae)?
1060.e: The sand lizard and the common wall lizard are both lacertids. Geckos and chameleons form their own families, and the slow worm is a legless lizard of another family.
1060.m: Sand lizards and wall lizards are lacertids.

1061.q: Where does the hippo mainly live?
1061.e: Hippos live in rivers and lakes in Africa, south of the Sahara. There is warm water and plenty of grass there.

1062.q: What does the common earwig feed on?
1062.e: The earwig is an omnivore. For example, it eats parts of plants and small animals.

1063.q: Where do least weasels often get completely white fur in winter?
a: In very cold, snowy regions in the north
1063.e: In regions with long, snowy winters, such as Scandinavia, some least weasels turn white in winter. This gives them good camouflage in the snow.
1063.m: In the far north the least weasel often turns white.

1064.q: Where does the lion mainly live in the wild?
1064.e: Lions live mainly in open grasslands, the savannahs of Africa. There is enough prey and room to hunt there.

1065.q: How does an alpine salamander usually react when a predator threatens it?
a: It often stays still, because its poison protects it
It climbs a tree in a flash
1065.e: Because the poison in its skin puts many predators off, the alpine salamander does not need to flee as fast as other animals. Many predators let go of it again after one bite.
1065.m: Its poison protects it from enemies.

1066.q: How do elephants communicate over long distances too?
a: With deep sounds that are hard to hear
1066.e: Elephants produce infrasound, which means very low sounds. These sounds travel far and can even be passed on through the ground.
1066.m: Elephants use deep sounds to communicate.

1067.q: What happens when an animal moults its skin?
a: The animal sheds its outer covering when it gets too tight
The animal throws off its legs
The animal changes its colour for ever
1067.e: The hard outer skeleton does not grow with the animal. That is why it has to be shed several times so the animal can get bigger.

1068.q: How does the peregrine falcon usually catch its prey?
a: It strikes it in flight with its talons
It digs it out of holes in the ground
It catches it from the water with its beak
1068.e: The peregrine falcon usually catches its victims right in the air by striking them with its strong talons. Then it kills them with a well-aimed bite.
1068.m: Prey is usually struck in mid-air.

1069.q: Which group of animals does the wels catfish belong to?
1069.e: The wels catfish is a bony fish and breathes with gills. It lives only in water.
1069.m: The wels catfish is a fish.

1070.q: How does the adder kill its prey?
a: With a sting in its tail
By crushing it with its teeth
1070.e: It bites and injects venom. Then it swallows the prey whole.

1071.q: Who usually leads a group of chimpanzees?
1071.e: In a group of chimpanzees, there is usually a strong male who leads the group. The others show him respect.
1071.m: A strong male leads the group.

1072.q: What does an eel mainly breathe with in the water?
1072.e: Like other fish, the eel takes oxygen from the water through its gills. It can also take in some extra oxygen through its moist skin.

1073.q: When is the barn owl mainly active?
1073.e: The barn owl is a night animal. During the day it usually sleeps in a hidden place.
1073.m: The barn owl hunts at night.

1074.q: How are young fire salamanders born?
a: As live larvae that can swim in water
As eggs buried in the sand
As fully formed little salamanders with no larval stage
1074.e: The females carry the eggs inside their bodies and release ready-made larvae into the water. This is called giving birth to live young, or ovoviviparity.

1075.q: Where do millipedes usually live in Central Europe?
a: In the soil, under leaves, stones and wood
In the open water of lakes
On mountain peaks in the snow
1075.e: They like it damp and dark. That is why they hide under leaves, bark and stones.
1075.m: They love damp, dark hiding places.

1076.q: Is the black rhino seriously endangered today?
a: Yes, it is threatened with extinction
No, there are lots of them
No, it is not endangered at all
It only lives in zoos now
1076.e: The black rhino is one of the most threatened animals in the world. Only a few thousand still live in the wild.
1076.m: The black rhino is seriously endangered.

1077.q: What happens in the incomplete metamorphosis of an insect like the grasshopper?
a: The larvae already look like the adults
The larva turns completely into a pupa
A flying animal hatches straight from the egg
1077.e: In incomplete metamorphosis, small nymphs that already look like the adults hatch from the egg. They moult several times until they are fully grown.
1077.m: Nymphs already look like the adults.

1078.q: The mute swan’s German name means ‘knob swan’. Where does this name come from?
a: From the knob on its beak
From the humps on its back
From hard lumps on its feet
1078.e: The black knob above the beak gave the bird its German name. It is especially easy to see on males.
1078.m: The knob sits right on the beak.

1079.q: Roughly how long have millipedes existed on Earth?
1079.e: Fossils show that millipedes were among the first land animals. They lived long before the dinosaurs.
1079.m: Millipedes are very old land animals.

1080.q: Why does a cheetah sometimes lose its catch to lions or hyenas?
a: Because it is too exhausted after the sprint to fight
Because it does not like the prey itself
Because it is afraid of its own prey
1080.e: After its fast sprint, the cheetah is very exhausted. Stronger predators such as lions can then simply take the prey away from it.
1080.m: Exhausted cheetahs often lose their prey.

1081.q: What is a male goose called?
1081.e: The male goose is called a gander. It is often a little bigger than the female.
1081.m: A male goose is called a gander.

1082.q: Is the grass snake dangerously venomous to people?
1082.e: The grass snake has no venom that would be dangerous to people. That is why it is harmless.
1082.m: Grass snakes are harmless to people.

1083.q: How do peregrine falcon pairs usually live over the years?
a: They often stay with the same partner for a long time
They never live as a pair
They live in big groups of ten falcons
1083.e: Peregrine falcons usually stay with the same partner for several years and often return to the same nesting site. This loyalty to a place is called site fidelity.
1083.m: Falcon pairs often stay together for a long time.

1084.q: Which beetle belongs, like dung beetles, to the scarab beetles?
1084.e: You can recognise scarab beetles by their antennae with leaf-like plates. The cockchafer has such eye-catching fans.
1084.m: The cockchafer is a relative of dung beetles.

1085.q: What are the marsh frog’s strong back legs especially important for?
a: For powerful jumps and fast swimming
1085.e: The long, muscular back legs with webbed feet help the frog jump on land and swim fast in water. Without them it could hardly escape its enemies.
1085.m: Strong back legs help with jumping and swimming.

1087.q: How can you best tell male and female adult golden eagles apart?
a: By their body size, females are bigger
By the colour of their feathers
By the sound of their calls alone
1087.e: Because the feathers of males and females hardly differ, experts look mainly at body size. Females are clearly bigger and heavier than males.

1088.q: When is the elk rutting season?
1088.e: The elk rut takes place in September and October. Then the bulls fight over the cows.

1089.q: What is the time called when wild boar mate?
1089.e: The mating season of wild boar is called the rut. It usually takes place in winter.
1089.m: The mating season is called the rut.

1090.q: On which animal does Jesus ride into the city of Jerusalem on Palm Sunday?
1090.e: The Bible tells how Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a donkey. Palm Sunday remembers this.
1090.m: The donkey is part of this Bible story.

1091.q: Roughly how long do the young stay with their mother?
a: About one and a half to two years
1091.e: During this time they learn to hunt and climb. Then they look for a territory of their own.
1091.m: The young learn from their mother for about two years.

1092.q: Why does a lion roar so loudly?
1092.e: With its loud roar, the lion shows other lions that an area is already taken. The roar can be heard several kilometres away.

1093.q: Why do the host birds still feed the much bigger cuckoo chick?
a: Because it begs especially loudly and insistently
Because it looks exactly like them
Because the cuckoo brings them food
Because it is not bigger at all
1093.e: The cuckoo chick begs very loudly and opens its beak wide, and this makes the host birds want to feed it. They do not realise that it is not their own chick.
1093.m: Loud begging fools the foster parents.

1094.q: How can you help grass snakes in the garden?
a: With a pond and a pile of leaves
1094.e: A pond provides frogs as food, and leaves are a place to lay eggs. This creates a habitat.
1094.m: A pond and a leaf pile help.

1095.q: What does a brown bear do especially intensely before winter?
a: It eats a lot to build up fat reserves
It looks for a partner to mate with
1095.e: In autumn, a brown bear eats a great deal to store enough fat for its winter rest. It can put on a lot of weight in a short time.
1095.m: Before winter, the bear eats to build up fat.

1096.q: How many bearded vultures have been released into the Alps since the project began?
a: None, they came back on their own
1096.e: Since 1986, young bearded vultures raised in breeding centres have been released again and again in different Alpine countries. In total, several hundred birds have returned to the mountains this way.
1096.m: Hundreds of birds have been released.

1097.q: What is a puma good at doing with its claws?
a: Climbing and holding on to prey
1097.e: Pumas have sharp claws that they can pull in. They help with climbing and grabbing prey.
1097.m: Puma claws are sharp and can be pulled in.

1098.q: What is another word for a sheep’s whole coat of wool?
1098.e: The thick woolly coat of a sheep is also called a fleece. After shearing, the fleece usually stays together in one piece.
1098.m: The woolly coat is also called a fleece.

1099.q: What is a baby pig called?
1099.e: A young pig is called a piglet. It stays with its mother, the sow, for a few weeks.
1099.m: A baby pig is called a piglet.

1100.q: What do sparrow parents feed their little chicks in the nest?
1100.e: Even though adult sparrows like eating seeds, the chicks mainly get insects. These contain lots of protein for growing.

1101.e: Dromedaries are active during the day. In the greatest heat they often rest.

1102.q: What does a young kangaroo do when it is a bit bigger but not yet fully independent?
a: It often just pokes its head out of the pouch
It leaves its mother for ever
It swims away on its own
1102.e: A slightly bigger joey no longer fits completely into the pouch. Often only its head or legs stick out.
1102.m: Bigger babies peek out of the pouch.

1103.q: What colour are a mallard’s feet usually?
1103.e: The mallard’s feet are usually bright orange. It uses them to paddle well in the water.
