2048.e: The exact number depends on the species and on whether it is male or female. After each moult, the insect is a bit bigger.

2050.q: What is a young baby goose called?
2050.e: A little goose chick is called a gosling. At first it has soft, fluffy down.
2050.m: A goose chick is called a gosling.

2051.q: When is the roe deer's breeding season, called the rut?
a: In summer, around July and August
Never, roe deer breed all year round
2051.e: The breeding season of roe deer is called the rut and takes place in summer. That is when buck and doe seek each other out.
2051.m: The roe deer rut is in summer.

2052.q: In tawny owls, which is usually heavier, the male or the female?
2052.e: In tawny owls, females are usually bigger and heavier than males. This is normal in many owl species.
2052.m: Female tawny owls are heavier than males.

2053.q: Why does the koala need such strong back teeth?
a: To grind up the tough eucalyptus leaves
2053.e: Eucalyptus leaves are tough and hard, so the koala needs strong back teeth to grind them finely. This lets its body take in the nutrients better.

2054.q: Why are great tits useful for gardeners?
a: They eat lots of caterpillars and pests
2054.e: Great tits eat lots of harmful caterpillars and insects in the garden. That is why gardeners are happy to have them.
2054.m: Great tits eat lots of garden pests.

2055.q: Which lake is especially famous for the blue whitefish (Blaufelchen)?
2055.e: The blue whitefish is the most important fish for fishing on Lake Constance. It is found there naturally.
2055.m: The blue whitefish is the fish of Lake Constance.

2056.q: Is there only one kind of octopus?
a: No, there are very many different species
Yes, all octopuses are the same
No, there are exactly two species
2056.e: There are very many different species of octopus; scientists know about 300. Some are tiny, others very big.
2056.m: There are many different octopus species.

2057.q: What is a “long call” in male orang-utans?
a: A long, loud call to announce their territory
A warning call by the females
A song sung by the young
2057.e: Males call so they can be heard far away, to attract females and keep rivals at a distance. The call can carry more than a kilometre.
2057.m: The long call announces a male.

2058.q: How does a chimpanzee usually move about on the ground?
a: It leans on the knuckles of its hands
It only walks on two legs
2058.e: Chimpanzees often walk on all fours, leaning on the knuckles of their hands. This is called knuckle-walking.
2058.m: Chimpanzees often walk on their knuckles.

2060.q: How many queens are there normally in a wasp colony?
2060.e: A wasp colony usually has only one queen. She lays all the eggs in the nest.

2061.q: What is the bristly tuft of feathers below the bearded vulture's beak called?
2061.e: This striking, dark tuft of feathers grows under the beak and looks like a beard. It gave the bird its name.
2061.m: The beard gave it its name.

2062.q: Which fish from Swiss streams is the salmon closely related to?
2062.e: Salmon and trout both belong to the salmon family. They also look similar.
2062.m: Salmon and trout are closely related.

2063.q: Which country has the elephant as its national animal?
2063.e: In Thailand, the elephant is the national animal. There it is a symbol of strength and good luck.
2063.m: Thailand's national animal is the elephant.

2064.q: Why does an iceberg float in the sea instead of sinking?
a: Ice has a lower density than water
The seawater is too cold for sinking
2064.e: When water freezes, it expands and so becomes lighter per volume than liquid water. That is why ice floats on the surface of the water, even huge icebergs.
2064.m: Ice is lighter than the same amount of water.

2065.q: How do wasps react when their nest is threatened?
a: They all fly away at once
2065.e: When danger threatens, many wasps defend their nest together. That is why you should never get too close to a wasps' nest.

2066.q: What is a danger to puma populations?
a: Loss of habitat and hunting by people
Too many predators in the sea
2066.e: Roads, settlements and hunting cause problems for the puma. That is why it has become rare in some regions.

2067.q: Roughly how old can a cow get?
2067.e: A cow can live to about 20 years, even though many dairy cows don't get that old. It also depends on how they are kept.

2068.q: How do elephants use their trunk when they swim through a deep river?
a: As an anchor on the riverbed
2068.e: Elephants are good swimmers. When crossing rivers, they hold their trunk above the water like a snorkel so they can breathe.
2068.m: The trunk works as a snorkel.

2069.q: What is striking about the telescope eye, a special kind of goldfish?
2069.e: The telescope eye is a goldfish with strikingly large, round eyes. But with these eyes it sees worse than a wild goldfish.
2069.m: The telescope eye has especially big eyes.

2070.q: What makes a seahorse look very different from an ordinary fish?
a: Its horse-like head and upright body
2070.e: With its horse's head and upright body, the seahorse looks completely different from most fish. That is why it is so easy to recognise.
2070.m: A horse's head and upright body are typical.

2071.q: Has the carp always lived in Switzerland?
a: No, people brought it here long ago
Yes, it has always been in all Swiss lakes
No, it only swam here on its own last year
Yes, it comes from the mountain streams of the Alps
2071.e: The carp originally comes from Asia and was brought to Europe, including Switzerland, by people. Today it lives here in many ponds and lakes.
2071.m: The carp was once brought to Switzerland.

2072.q: What especially threatens the kingfisher in Switzerland?
a: straightened riverbanks without natural steep banks
too many fish in the water
2072.e: When riverbanks are built up or straightened, the kingfisher has no steep earth banks to dig its nest burrow in. That is why natural banks are very important for it.

2073.q: Which class of vertebrates does the edible frog belong to?
2073.e: Frogs are amphibians. As tadpoles they live in water, and later both in water and on land.
2073.m: The edible frog is an amphibian.

2074.q: Which animals often eat the eggs of the European pond turtle?
2074.e: Predators dig up the clutches using their noses. That is why many nests are lost.

2075.q: Is the red panda active more during the day or at dusk?
a: Mainly at dusk and at night
Only in winter, it sleeps in summer
2075.e: The red panda sleeps a lot during the day and becomes active mainly at dusk and at night. That is when it looks for food.
2075.m: The red panda is active at dusk.

2076.q: How do wels catfish often move near the bottom of the water?
2076.e: Usually they glide calmly over the bottom and lie in wait for prey. Only when they attack do they speed up in a flash.
2076.m: Glide calmly, then snap in a flash.

2077.q: How many legs does a butterfly have?
2077.e: Like all insects, the butterfly has six legs. The legs are attached to the animal's chest.

2078.q: Which statement about the praying mantis in Switzerland is true?
a: It is rare and only found in warmer regions
It is common everywhere in the Alps
It is thought to have died out
2078.e: In this country it is limited to warm places. With the warmer climate, it is able to spread further in some areas.

2079.q: Why does a cheetah have to rest after a fast sprint?
a: Because the sun makes it tired
2079.e: When running fast, the cheetah's body gets very hot. Afterwards it needs a break so it can cool down again.
2079.m: After a sprint, the cheetah has to cool down.

2080.q: Why does the alpine salamander, unlike the fire salamander, not need any water to have young?
a: Because it gives birth to live, fully formed young instead of larvae
Because it can't breathe in water
Because it only lives in trees
Because it reproduces by splitting in two
2080.e: Because the young are born fully developed, there is no larva stage in the water. This makes the alpine salamander independent of ponds or streams.
2080.m: Live birth means the alpine salamander needs no water.

2081.q: Roughly how far away can you hear a donkey's loud hee-haw?
a: Not at all, donkeys are silent
2081.e: A donkey's bray is very loud and can be heard over long distances. This means donkeys can communicate with each other even from far away.
2081.m: You can hear donkeys from very far away.

2082.q: What is typical of the jaguar's fur pattern?
2082.e: The jaguar's fur has ring-shaped spots called rosettes. Often there are one or more small dots inside the rosettes.

2083.q: How does the common frog often protect itself from enemies?
a: It jumps away quickly and hides
2083.e: With powerful jumps, the common frog can escape quickly. Its brown colour also helps it hide among leaves.
2083.m: Common frogs escape with big jumps.

2084.q: How is the housefly different from the mosquito?
a: The housefly doesn't bite and doesn't drink blood
2084.e: The mosquito bites and sucks blood, but the housefly does not. It feeds on other liquid or soft things.
2084.m: Only the mosquito bites, not the fly.

2085.q: Why shouldn't you suddenly grab a guinea pig from above?
a: Because it reminds them of attacks by birds of prey
Because they fall asleep straight away
Because it makes them especially happy
Because they don't mind at all
2085.e: In the wild, guinea pigs are sometimes attacked from above by birds of prey. So a sudden grab from above can give them a big fright.
2085.m: Grabbing from above frightens guinea pigs.

2086.q: What job do some geese do on a farm because of their loud honking?
a: They warn of intruders like a guard dog
2086.e: Because geese immediately and loudly announce strange noises and people, they are sometimes kept as natural guards on farms.

2087.q: Why is a mosquito bite in Switzerland usually not dangerous?
a: Because hardly any dangerous diseases are passed on here
Because Swiss mosquitoes can't bite at all
Because there are no mosquitoes in Switzerland
Because mosquitoes here don't like blood
2087.e: In Switzerland, most mosquitoes don't carry dangerous germs. So a bite is usually just annoying and itches a bit.

2088.q: What does a grasshopper use to chirp?
a: It rubs its legs or wings together
It taps its feet on the ground
2088.e: The grasshopper rubs certain parts of its body together. This makes the chirping sound.

2089.q: Where does the African elephant mainly live?
a: In savannahs and forests south of the Sahara
2089.e: The African elephant lives in various habitats south of the Sahara. These include savannahs, forests and sometimes swamps.
2089.m: Elephants live south of the Sahara.

2090.q: What makes the barn owl's feathers so quiet when it flies?
a: A fine, soft comb on the edge of the feathers
2090.e: The barn owl's feathers have a soft, comb-like edge. This breaks up the flow of air and makes its flight almost silent.
2090.m: Fine feather combs make it quiet.

2091.q: What is the general conservation status of the kestrel in Switzerland?
a: It is not currently seen as seriously endangered and is fairly common
It has already died out in Switzerland
It is only found in one single valley
It has never been recorded in Switzerland
2091.e: The kestrel is one of the more common birds of prey in Switzerland and is not currently seen as seriously endangered. Even so, like all birds of prey, it is protected.
2091.m: The kestrel is fairly common in Switzerland.

2092.q: Why is the spectacled penguin called that?
a: It has markings around its eyes like glasses
It sees especially well in the dark
2092.e: The spectacled penguin has a black stripe around its eyes that looks like a pair of glasses. That is where its name comes from.
2092.m: The spectacled penguin has markings like glasses.

2095.q: Which of these animals is the African wild dog most closely related to?
2095.e: Like the wolf, the African wild dog belongs to the dog family. Despite its spots, it is not closely related to hyenas.
2095.m: The wild dog is related to the wolf, not the hyena.

2096.q: What happens when a bumblebee flies from flower to flower?
a: It carries pollen from one flower to the next
It gets tired and falls asleep straight away
2096.e: When flying from flower to flower, the bumblebee keeps picking up pollen. In this way it helps plants to make fruit and seeds.
2096.m: Bumblebees carry pollen from flower to flower.

a: Diplomats cannot be arrested in the host country like ordinary citizens
Diplomats do not have to pay taxes in their home country
Diplomats are not allowed to vote
Diplomats have to change country every year
2097.e: Diplomatic immunity protects embassy staff from being prosecuted in the host country. This is so that they can do their work independently and safely.

2098.q: What does it mean that whitefish are cold-blooded?
a: Their body temperature depends on the water temperature
They live in the sea in summer
2098.e: Cold-blooded animals can't control their body heat themselves. So in a cold lake, whitefish are cool too.
2098.m: In cold-blooded whitefish, the water sets the body temperature.

2099.q: What damage can aphids do to plants?
a: They eat the roots up completely
They dig tunnels in the trunk
They lay eggs in fruit like wasps
2099.e: While sucking, aphids can pass on plant viruses. They also weaken the plants by taking their sap.
2099.m: Aphids weaken plants and pass on viruses.

2100.q: Roughly how long is a female hippo pregnant?
2100.e: A hippo's pregnancy lasts about eight months. Then usually a single calf is born.
2100.m: Baby hippos grow for eight months in the belly.

2101.q: What is the difference between saving and investing?
a: Saving puts money aside safely, investing puts money in with risk to earn more
Saving and investing mean exactly the same
Saving always earns more than investing
2101.e: Saving means putting money aside safely but with little return, for example in a savings account. Investing, for example in shares, can earn more, but also carries the risk of losing money.
2101.m: Saving is safe, investing is riskier.

2102.q: What happens to a marmot's heart during hibernation?
a: It beats much more slowly than usual
2102.e: During hibernation, the heartbeat slows down a lot, sometimes to just a few beats a minute. This saves energy the animal needs to survive.

2103.q: Where do gibbons spend almost their whole lives?
2103.e: Gibbons are typical tree dwellers. They eat, play and sleep high up in the trees.
2103.m: Gibbons live almost only in trees.

2104.q: In Asia there are mahouts. Which animal do they work with?
2104.e: A mahout leads and cares for an elephant. In Asia, elephants have been kept as working animals for a long time.
2104.m: An elephant keeper is called a mahout.

2105.q: What have researchers found out about carrion crows and their relatives recognising people?
a: they can recognise individual human faces
they only recognise animals, not people
they forget every face straight away
2105.e: Studies of crows and their relatives have shown that they can remember individual human faces for a long time. This helps them tell friendly people from dangerous ones.

2106.q: Roughly how many African wild dogs are still living in the wild?
2106.e: Today there are only a few thousand African wild dogs left. That is why the species is considered endangered.
2106.m: Only a few thousand African wild dogs are left.

2107.q: What does a mole's fur feel like?
2107.e: A mole's fur is especially soft and fine, almost like velvet. It helps it move easily through its tunnels.

a: The green pigment that captures sunlight
2108.e: Chlorophyll is found in the green parts of a plant and captures sunlight for photosynthesis. It is what gives leaves their green colour.
2108.m: Chlorophyll makes leaves green and captures light.

2109.q: What is the Roman snail's so-called love dart?
a: A small chalky needle used in the mating ritual
2109.e: When mating, the snail shoots out a small needle made of lime, the so-called love dart. It is thought to have an extra effect on the partner.
2109.m: The love dart is part of mating.

2110.q: What does a sparrow do to keep its feathers clean?
2110.e: Sparrows like bathing in sand or dust to care for their feathers. This gets rid of annoying little parasites.

2111.q: How do the parent golden eagles behave after the young have left the nest?
a: They keep feeding the young for a few more weeks
They drive the young away completely at once
They never return to the nest again
They take the young to a zoo
2111.e: Even after their first flight, young golden eagles are still fed by their parents for several weeks. Only after that do they have to find a territory of their own.
2111.m: Parents still feed the young after they fledge.

2112.q: What is it called when a slow-worm sheds its old skin?
2112.e: The slow-worm regularly sheds its old skin. It usually comes off in one piece or in scraps.
2112.m: When sloughing, the old skin comes off.

2113.q: Why doesn't the garden spider get stuck in its own sticky web?
a: It walks on threads that aren't sticky and has oily feet
Because it doesn't build a sticky web at all
Because it flies instead of walking
Because it never touches the web itself
2113.e: Not all the threads in the web are sticky; some are just a framework. An oily layer on its legs also stops the spider from sticking.
2113.m: Some threads in the web aren't sticky.

2115.q: Which season is usually the warmest in Switzerland?
2115.e: In summer the sun is higher in the sky and the days are long. That is why it gets warmest then.

2116.q: What is true about pond skaters' wings?
a: They all have big colourful wings
None of them can ever have wings
2116.e: In many species there are winged and wingless pond skaters. With wings, a pond skater can reach a new pond or stream.

2117.q: On which continents does the barn swallow breed, among others?
a: In Europe, Asia and North America
2117.e: The barn swallow breeds across the whole northern half of the world, including Europe, Asia and North America.
2117.m: The barn swallow breeds in Europe, Asia and North America.

2118.q: Why are spotted hyena droppings often light in colour?
a: Because of all the bones they digest
Because of the grass in their food
Because of the salt in the water
2118.e: Bones contain a lot of calcium, which makes the droppings whitish. This is a sign of their bone-rich diet.

2119.q: What does the leatherback turtle especially like to eat?
2119.e: Leatherback turtles love jellyfish and eat huge numbers of them. Their throat even has sharp spikes so that the slippery jellyfish can't escape.

2120.q: Are ladybirds used on purpose in organic farming?
a: Yes, to fight aphids without poison
No, they are never used there
Yes, to pollinate fields like bees
No, they are seen as pests there
2120.e: Because ladybirds eat so many aphids, farmers sometimes use them on purpose. That way they need to use fewer pesticides.

2121.q: Which subspecies of the Asian elephant lives on an island in the Indian Ocean?
2121.e: A subspecies of its own lives on Sri Lanka. It is called the Sri Lankan elephant.
2121.m: Sri Lanka has its own elephant subspecies.

2122.q: Which fish travel from rivers to the sea to spawn, the opposite of salmon?
2122.e: Eels grow up in fresh water and spawn in the sea. Salmon do it the other way round: they grow up in the sea and spawn in rivers.
2122.m: Eels spawn in the sea, salmon in rivers.

2123.q: On which continents are pike found?
a: In Europe, Asia and North America
2123.e: Pike live in many lakes and rivers in Europe, Asia and North America. They like cool fresh water.

2124.q: What does a male kingfisher sometimes do to impress a female?
a: it gives her a fish it has caught
it builds her a nest of flowers
it sings for hours without stopping
2124.e: During courtship, the male brings the female a fish as a present. If she accepts it, it is a sign that they are pairing up.
2124.m: The male gives the female a fish.

2125.q: Roughly how big are newly hatched European pond turtles?
2125.e: The young are tiny and still have a soft shell. That is why they are easy prey for many animals.
2125.m: Newly hatched turtles are only thumb-sized.

2126.q: The Adélie penguin has a white ring around its eyes. Where does it live?
2126.e: The Adélie penguin is one of the most common penguins in Antarctica. It has a striking white ring around its eyes.
2126.m: The Adélie penguin lives in Antarctica.

2127.q: What happens to the female octopus after the eggs have hatched?
a: She looks for a new partner
2127.e: The female octopus guards her eggs for a very long time without eating. Shortly after the little octopuses hatch, the mother dies.
2127.m: The octopus mother dies after hatching.

2128.q: Roughly how much time does a gorilla spend eating every day?
2128.e: Because plants are not as nourishing as meat, a gorilla has to eat a great deal. So it spends a large part of the day looking for food and eating.
2128.m: Gorillas eat for many hours a day.

2129.q: Why do European pond turtles like lying in the sun?
2129.e: Because they are cold-blooded, they need warmth from outside. Only when they are warm can they actively hunt and digest.
2129.m: Sunbathing replaces their own body heat.

2130.q: What kind of animal is a scarab, the dung roller?
a: A beetle that rolls dung into balls
A snail with a pill-shaped shell
2130.e: Dung rollers form dung into balls and roll them away. They belong to the scarab beetles.
2130.m: Dung rollers roll balls of dung.

2131.q: Where do young bonobos usually sleep?
a: In the nest with their mother
In the males' nest far away
2131.e: Young bonobos sleep close to their mother, usually in the same nest. This keeps them safe and warm.
2131.m: The young sleep with their mother.

2132.q: What does a cheetah like to eat most?
2132.e: Cheetahs are meat-eaters and like hunting fast prey such as gazelles. They catch them with a fast sprint.

2134.q: Which habitats does the common wall lizard like best?
a: Dry, sunny, stony places such as walls and rocks
2134.e: Stone walls and rocks store heat and offer lots of hiding places. That is exactly what the wall lizard needs to survive.

2135.q: What do you call a group of male cheetahs that live together?
2135.e: Some male cheetahs stay together all their lives and help each other. This group is called a coalition.

2136.q: What colour is the grass snake usually?
2136.e: Its colouring helps with camouflage. It often has dark spots on its sides.
2136.m: Grey to olive green, well camouflaged.

2137.q: What colour is the tip of the tail in most red foxes?
2137.e: The tip of the bushy fox tail is white in most red foxes. This is a typical feature for recognising this kind of fox.
2137.m: The tail tip is usually white.

2138.q: Where do millipedes take in air to breathe?
a: Through small holes on the sides of the body
Through a lung in the mouth
2138.e: Millipedes have small breathing holes on the sides of their bodies, called spiracles. From there, fine tubes called tracheae lead into the body.
2138.m: Millipedes breathe through holes in their sides.

2139.q: What makes chamois hooves especially good for climbing?
a: Soft, springy soles with a hard rim
Very long claws like a cat's
2139.e: Chamois hooves have a hard rim and a soft, grippy sole. This combination gives them a good hold on smooth rock.
2139.m: Soft soles and a hard rim give grip.

2140.q: What does the German name “Ringelnatter” for the grass snake probably refer to?
a: It wears gold rings around its neck
It lives in rings of stone
2140.e: The name is linked to the German word “ringeln”, which means coiling the body up. It has nothing to do with jewellery.

2141.q: In which country is the robin especially linked with Christmas?
2141.e: In Great Britain, the robin is a popular symbol of Christmas. You often see it on British Christmas cards.
2141.m: In Great Britain it is a Christmas symbol.

2142.q: How does a cow protect itself from the cold in winter?
2142.e: In winter, cows grow a thicker coat that protects them from the cold. They can also find shelter from wind and snow in the cowshed.
2142.m: Cows grow a thick winter coat.

2143.q: Which animal barks and is often called man's best friend?
2143.e: The dog is one of humanity's oldest pets. It barks to warn or to play.
2143.m: The dog is our best friend.

2144.q: How does an alpine salamander normally react if you carefully watch it in the wild?
a: It usually tries to slowly get away or stays completely still
2144.e: Alpine salamanders are not aggressive animals and avoid contact with people. When disturbed, they usually try to retreat or simply stay motionless.
2144.m: It usually keeps out of people's way.

2145.q: Roughly how many species of starfish are there on Earth?
2145.e: There are over 1,500 different species of starfish in the world. They differ in size, colour and shape.
2145.m: There are very many starfish species.

2146.q: Where did the first beavers brought back to Switzerland come from?
a: From other European countries, for example France and Norway
2146.e: For the reintroduction, beavers were brought from other European countries where they had survived. This allowed stable populations to form in Switzerland again.
2146.m: The beavers came back from other European countries.

2147.q: Where can you still see live sharks in Switzerland?
a: In the gardens of many houses
2147.e: Sharks are kept and shown in special tanks in zoos and aquariums. So visitors can watch them in Switzerland too.
2147.m: In Switzerland you only see sharks in aquariums.

2148.q: Roughly how long do young leopards stay with their mother?
a: They leave her after a week
2148.e: The young learn to hunt from their mother. At about 18 to 24 months they become independent.
2148.m: Young leopards learn for two years.

2149.q: What is the best thing to do when a wasp is flying around you?
2149.e: If you stay calm, the wasp usually loses interest quickly. Frantic flapping, on the other hand, tends to make it nervous.

2150.q: Which different kinds of burrow does an alpine marmot dig?
a: A home burrow, escape burrows and a winter burrow
Just one single burrow for its whole life
2150.e: Marmots have a home burrow for everyday life, small escape burrows for a quick getaway and a deep winter burrow for hibernation. Each burrow has its own purpose.

2151.q: What do chickens use to scratch the ground for food?
2151.e: Chickens scratch the ground with their claws to find insects and grain. Then they peck up what they have found.

2152.q: In which habitats are moles often found in Switzerland?
a: Only high in the mountains above 3,000 metres
2152.e: Moles like loose, damp soil, like the soil in meadows, gardens and woods. There are also enough worms to eat there.

2153.q: What is an adult male goat called?
2153.e: The male animal is called a billy goat. It often has big horns.
2153.m: The male goat is a billy goat.

2154.q: What does it usually mean when a cat lashes its tail quickly from side to side?
2154.e: A fast-lashing tail usually shows that the cat is annoyed or worked up. It is better to leave it alone then.

2155.q: Where does the female raise her young?
a: In a rock cave or crack in the rock
In an underground burrow like a badger
2155.e: The den is lined with the mother's hair. It protects the young from cold and enemies.
2155.m: The young grow up in rock caves.

2156.q: What is especially typical of the red kite's way of life when it comes to hunting prey?
a: it often catches weakened or sick animals
it only eats plants and seeds
it only hunts in huge flocks
2156.e: The red kite often spots and catches weakened, sick or injured animals, which are easier to catch. This also helps remove sick animals from nature.
2156.m: Red kites often catch weakened animals.

2157.q: What does a native dung beetle such as the dor beetle usually look like?
a: Black with a bluish or violet shimmering gloss
2157.e: Many dung beetles have a dark, shiny body. In the light it often shimmers blue, green or violet.
2157.m: Dung beetles are dark with a metallic sheen.

2158.q: Roughly how fast can large dragonflies fly?
a: Up to about 50 kilometres per hour
2158.e: Large species reach around 50 kilometres per hour for short bursts. This makes them fast hunters in the insect world.

2159.q: What about the ring-tailed lemur's hands is typical of primates?
a: The thumb can be placed opposite the other fingers
The fingers have grown together into flippers
The hands have only two fingers
2159.e: With their gripping hands, ring-tailed lemurs hold on to fruit and branches. This is a typical feature of primates.

2160.q: Dolphins make clicking sounds. What comes back when a click hits a fish?
2160.e: The click bounces off the fish and comes back as an echo. That is how the dolphin knows where the fish is.

2161.q: Which animals can be dangerous to wild camels in the wild?
2161.e: Wolves live in the same habitat as the wild camel. They can catch young camels in particular.
2161.m: Wolves are enemies of young camels.

2162.q: Roughly how long does it take for the young to hatch from the eggs?
2162.e: The exact time depends a lot on how warm the ground is. The warmer the summer, the faster the embryos develop.
2162.m: The young hatch after about six to eight weeks.

2163.q: What is the narrow, warm chamber deep in the badger's sett where the young grow up called?
2163.e: Deep in the sett there is a specially lined chamber, the breeding chamber. There the little badgers are well protected and warm.
2163.m: Young badgers grow up in the breeding chamber.

2164.q: Roughly how long do African wild dogs live in the wild?
2164.e: In the wild, they often live to around 10 years. But many die earlier.
2164.m: Wild dogs live about ten years.

2165.q: What does the adder do in winter?
a: It rests through the winter in a frost-free hiding place
It keeps hunting as in summer
It digs itself into the ice
2165.e: As a cold-blooded animal, it spends the cold season stiff and still in holes in the ground or cracks in rocks. It stays frost-free there.
2165.m: It spends winter stiff in a hiding place.

2166.q: Roughly how heavy can an adult wolf get?
2166.e: Depending on the subspecies and habitat, adult wolves usually weigh between 30 and 50 kilograms. Males are usually a bit heavier than females.

2167.q: What is especially powerful in the jaguar?
a: Its bite, with very strong jaws
2167.e: For its body size, the jaguar has one of the strongest bites of all cats. It can even crack turtle shells with it.
2167.m: The jaguar has an extremely strong bite.

2168.q: What by-product of photosynthesis do plants release into the air?
2168.e: In photosynthesis, plants use light energy to turn water and CO2 into glucose. Oxygen is made as a by-product and released through the stomata.
2168.m: Photosynthesis releases oxygen as a by-product.

2169.q: Who elects the government in a democracy?
2169.e: In a democracy all citizens may choose who governs them. That keeps power under control.
2169.m: The power to vote lies with the people.

2170.q: Which habitat does the European tree frog absolutely need in order to breed?
a: A calm, often sunny pond without many fish
2170.e: Tree frogs need sunny, still ponds without many fish, because fish would eat their eggs and tadpoles. Ponds like this are getting rarer and rarer.
2170.m: Sunny ponds without fish are important.

2171.q: What is special about ring-tailed lemurs compared with many other lemurs?
a: They spend a lot of time on the ground
They only live at the tops of trees
2171.e: Ring-tailed lemurs do climb, but they often walk on the ground. There they look for food and sunbathe.
2171.m: Ring-tailed lemurs are often on the ground.

2172.q: What does the Federal Department of Foreign Affairs (FDFA) do?
a: It looks after relations with other countries
2172.e: The FDFA is Switzerland’s foreign ministry. It keeps up contacts with other states and helps Swiss people abroad.
2172.m: The FDFA looks after foreign relations.

2173.q: Who lays the eggs in a bumblebee colony?
2173.e: Only the queen lays the eggs in a bumblebee colony. The workers take care of food and look after the larvae.

2174.q: How does the brown bear spend the winter in cold regions?
a: It rests through the winter in a den
It stays awake and keeps looking for food
2174.e: In cold areas, the brown bear retreats to a den and slows down its body functions. It lives off its fat reserves and loses a lot of weight.
2174.m: In winter, the brown bear rests in a den.

2175.q: What does a hamster in a cage need so that it can always drink enough?
2175.e: A hamster always needs fresh water, usually from a drinking bottle on the cage. This keeps it healthy.

2176.q: What is the main job of a police dog?
a: It supports the police, for example by tracking down people or drugs
It only guards the police station
2176.e: Police dogs are specially trained to track down people, drugs or explosives and to support officers. Their sensitive noses make them especially suitable for this.
2176.m: Service dogs track down people and substances.

2177.q: What does the tip of the African wild dog's tail usually look like?
2177.e: The tip of the tail is usually white. It probably helps the animals see each other better in tall grass when hunting.
2177.m: A white tail tip as a signal.

2178.q: At what time of day do rhinos especially like to eat?
a: Early in the morning and in the evening
Only in the middle of the night
Never, they eat in their sleep
2178.e: Rhinos prefer to eat in the cooler morning and evening hours. In the heat of midday they would rather rest.
2178.m: Rhinos eat in the morning and evening.

2179.q: How fast does a mosquito fly?
2179.e: Compared with many other insects, mosquitoes are rather slow fliers. That is why you can sometimes easily shoo them away with your hand.

2180.q: Why are polluted or drained ponds especially harmful to the edible frog?
a: It needs clean water for its spawn and tadpoles
It lives only in the air
It doesn't need any water at all
2180.e: The edible frog depends on reasonably clean water for laying its eggs and for its tadpoles to develop. Pollution or ponds drying out put its young at risk.
2180.m: The edible frog needs clean water to spawn.

2181.q: What is typical of bull elephants in the so-called musth?
a: They are very worked up and can be dangerous
2181.e: In musth, the bulls' hormone levels rise sharply. They are then very aggressive, and you should not get too close to them.
2181.m: Bull elephants in musth are dangerous.

2182.q: Is the polar bear a good swimmer?
a: Yes, it can swim for hours
No, it can't swim at all
2182.e: Polar bears are amazingly good swimmers. They can swim for many hours in the cold sea to reach an ice floe.
2182.m: Polar bears can swim for a very long time.

2183.q: Which prey does the kestrel sometimes eat as well as mice?
2183.e: As well as mice, the kestrel also catches insects such as grasshoppers, small songbirds and sometimes lizards. So its menu is varied.
2183.m: Kestrels also eat insects and lizards.

2184.q: Where do European eels lay their eggs?
a: In the Sargasso Sea in the Atlantic
In the North Sea near Heligoland
2184.e: European eels travel to the Sargasso Sea to spawn. It is an area of sea in the western Atlantic.
2184.m: Eels spawn in the Sargasso Sea.

2185.q: Why does the European tree frog especially need ponds without fish?
a: So that fish don't eat its eggs and tadpoles
So that it can catch fish itself
So that the water stays cleaner
So that it can swim faster
2185.e: Fish like eating frogs' eggs and tadpoles. That is why ponds without fish are especially important for the tree frog to breed successfully.
2185.m: Ponds without fish protect the young.

2186.q: What does the mother mainly protect her eggs from when she cleans them?
2186.e: In the damp soil, fungi can attack the eggs. That is why the mother cleans them again and again.
2186.m: Cleaning protects the eggs from fungi.

2187.q: Roughly how old do gibbons get in human care?
2187.e: Gibbons can get quite old in zoos, sometimes over 30 years. In the wild their age is often a bit lower.

2188.q: Why are chimpanzees such good climbers?
a: Because they have strong arms and gripping hands
Because they have suction pads on their feet
Because they are as light as feathers
2188.e: Chimpanzees have very strong arms and can grip well with their hands and feet. That is why they climb easily from branch to branch.
2188.m: Strong arms make chimpanzees good climbers.

2189.q: What does a wood mouse do with its paws when it eats?
a: It skilfully holds its food with them
It only uses its mouth, not its paws
2189.e: The wood mouse holds its food with its little front paws while it nibbles on it.

2190.q: How can you often tell that a cat is stressed?
a: it hides, eats less or grooms itself too much
2190.e: Stressed cats often withdraw, eat less or groom themselves strikingly often. Cat owners should take signs like these seriously.

2191.q: What do guinea pigs absolutely need in their enclosure to hide in?
2191.e: Guinea pigs are prey animals and need places where they can safely retreat. Little houses or tubes give them exactly this protection.

2192.e: Tapirs are mostly active at dusk and at night. During the day they often rest in the shelter of the forest.
2192.m: Tapirs are mostly active at night.

2193.q: What does a salmon breathe with?
2193.e: The gills take oxygen from the water. This works in both fresh and salt water.

2195.q: What does the kingfisher mainly eat?
2195.e: The kingfisher feeds mainly on small fish such as minnows or sticklebacks. It catches them right in the water with its pointed beak.
2195.m: Small fish are on the menu.

2196.q: Why is it important to get enough sleep?
a: So that your body and brain can recover
So that you get hungry faster
2196.e: While you sleep, your body recovers and your brain sorts out what you learnt during the day. Without sleep you are tired and cannot concentrate.

2198.q: Which family do meerkats belong to?
2198.e: Meerkats belong to the mongoose family. So they are not related to marmots.

2199.q: In what kind of social groups do alpine marmots usually live?
a: In family colonies with several animals
In huge herds of hundreds of animals
2199.e: Alpine marmots live in colonies made up of a pair of parents and their young from different years. In this way the animals help each other.

2200.q: What happens to a tadpole when it turns into a toad?
a: It grows legs and its tail disappears
It just gets bigger, everything else stays the same
2200.e: Over time, the tadpole grows legs and its tail disappears. In a few weeks it becomes a little toad.

2201.q: How does a pair of common swifts often behave over several years?
a: it stays together and uses the same nest again
it splits up after every breeding season
both partners look for a new partner every year
they build a nest in a completely different place every year
2201.e: Many swifts return to the same nesting place year after year and often stay with the same partner. This improves their chances of breeding successfully.
2201.m: Swifts often stay loyal to their nest.

2202.q: How good is a brown bear's eyesight compared with its sense of smell?
a: Much better than its sense of smell
2202.e: Compared with their very good sense of smell, brown bears see rather poorly. That is why they mainly rely on their nose and hearing to explore their surroundings.
2202.m: Bears smell better than they see.

2203.q: How do male mosquitoes find female mosquitoes?
2203.e: Males and females hum differently when they fly. With their fine antennae, the males hear the females' humming and fly towards it.
2203.m: Male mosquitoes hear the females' humming.

2204.q: How does a mother brown bear behave when she sees her cubs threatened?
a: She defends the cubs very fiercely
She runs away on her own straight away
She hides and leaves the cubs behind
2204.e: A mother brown bear defends her cubs very fiercely against possible dangers. It is exactly these situations that are seen as especially risky when bears meet people.
2204.m: Mother bears fiercely defend their cubs.

2205.q: Which part of the body is especially long and strong in many grasshoppers?
2205.e: The back legs are much thicker and longer than the other legs. They make the big jumps possible.
2205.m: Strong back legs for big jumps.

2206.q: What kind of landscape does the barn swallow like living in best?
a: High up in the rocks above the tree line
Only in big cities with tower blocks
2206.e: The barn swallow prefers open farmland with meadows and fields near farms. There it finds enough insects and suitable nesting places in barns.
2206.m: It prefers open land near farms.

2207.q: What do you call animals that are used on purpose to control pests, for example ladybirds against aphids?
2207.e: Beneficial animals eat or fight pests. In gardening, people encourage them on purpose.

2208.q: What does a hedgehog like to eat most?
2208.e: Hedgehogs are insect-eaters and really like beetles, worms and snails. In this way they keep gardens free of pests.
2208.m: Hedgehogs eat insects, worms and snails.

2209.q: Which senses especially help the jackal find food?
a: The sense of touch in its wings
A heat sense like snakes have
2209.e: Jackals have a very good sense of smell and hearing. So they find prey and carrion even in the dark.
2209.m: Nose and ears lead to prey.

2210.q: What should you offer hedgehogs in the garden as well as food?
2210.e: Like all animals, hedgehogs need water to drink. A shallow bowl in the garden helps them, especially in dry summers.

2211.q: What is a well-known home remedy for aphids on house plants?
a: Spraying them off with water or soapy water
2211.e: You can remove the aphids with a strong jet of water or a mild soap solution. Beneficial insects also help.
2211.m: Water or soapy water helps against aphids.

a: Two or more parties link their lists to work together when seats are shared out
A list of all the laws
2213.e: With a list alliance, smaller parties can add their votes together. This helps them win more seats in parliament.
2213.m: List alliances combine the votes of several parties.

2214.q: Why is a healthy breakfast important?
a: It gives you energy for the day
It makes you tired straight away
It makes you grow faster than anything else
2214.e: In the morning your body is empty and needs new energy. A good breakfast helps you learn and play.

2215.q: What else do wolves sometimes eat besides live prey?
2215.e: Wolves are not fussy and also eat carrion when they find a dead animal. This helps them find enough food even in hard times.
2215.m: Wolves also eat carrion they find.

2216.q: How are the wild dog's paws different from a pet dog's?
a: It has no fifth toe at the front
It has claws it can pull in like a cat
2216.e: Pet dogs usually have five toes on their front feet, but the wild dog has only four. This makes it well built for running.
2216.m: Wild dogs have four front toes.

2217.q: How common is the edible frog in large parts of Central Europe?
a: It is one of the most widespread frog species
It is an extremely rare species
It is more endangered than any other frog
It is the only frog species in Europe
2217.e: In large parts of Central Europe, the edible frog is one of the most common and widespread frog species. You find it at a great many ponds and lakes.
2217.m: The edible frog is widespread and common.

2218.q: What happens if a pond dries out before the tadpoles have turned into frogs?
a: They hop into the next pond
They dig themselves in and wait for rain
2218.e: Tadpoles need water to develop into frogs. If their pond dries out too early, many of them cannot survive.
2218.m: Drying ponds are dangerous for tadpoles.

2219.q: Which rhino still has some hair on its skin?
2219.e: The Sumatran rhino is the only species with some reddish hair on its skin. The other rhino species are almost hairless.
2219.m: The Sumatran rhino has a little hair.

2220.q: The scientific name of the sand lizard is Lacerta agilis. What does the Latin word “agilis” mean?
2220.e: “Agilis” means nimble or quick-moving, like the English word “agile”. The sand lizard really can run away very fast.

2221.q: Which predatory fish from Swiss lakes is a close relative of the perch?
2221.e: Zander and perch both belong to the perch family. Both have a spiny front dorsal fin.
2221.m: The zander is a relative of the perch.

2222.q: What is the largest known species of jellyfish called?
2222.e: With its tentacles, the lion's mane jellyfish can be several metres long. Its bell can be over two metres wide.
2222.m: The lion's mane is the largest jellyfish.

2223.q: Why do wild boar like wallowing in mud?
a: To cool down and get rid of parasites
2223.e: Wild boar bathe in mud because it helps against heat and annoying insects. This keeps their skin healthy.
2223.m: A mud bath protects against heat and parasites.

2224.q: When are European pond turtles old enough to breed?
2224.e: The animals grow slowly and need many years before they can have young. That is why their numbers recover only slowly.
2224.m: They are only able to breed late.

2225.q: What happens to an earthworm when the soil gets too dry?
a: It can't breathe as well and looks for damper soil
It doesn't need any moisture at all
2225.e: Because the earthworm breathes through its skin, it needs moisture to do so. If the soil is too dry, it digs deeper.

2226.q: When does the toad migration usually take place?
a: in early spring, often at night when it rains
in high summer in the sun
2226.e: As soon as it gets milder in spring and it rains, common toads set off in the evening. Damp, warm nights are ideal for this.
2226.m: Toad migration starts with warm rain.

2227.q: What are a kangaroo's ears especially good at?
a: They can turn independently of each other
2227.e: Kangaroo ears can each turn in different directions. This lets them hear sounds from all directions without moving their head.

2228.q: The scientific name of the alpine salamander is Salamandra atra. What does the word atra refer to?
2228.e: The Latin word atra means black. It refers directly to the animal's striking, completely black body.

2229.q: What is a male guinea pig called?
2229.e: A male guinea pig is called a boar. The female, on the other hand, is called a sow.
2229.m: A male guinea pig is a boar.

2230.q: How do goldfish often behave at feeding time?
a: They swim excitedly to the surface
2230.e: Many goldfish notice when it is feeding time and swim expectantly to the surface. This shows that they can get used to a routine.

2231.q: What do two male rhinos sometimes do to defend their territory?
a: They fight each other with their horns
2231.e: When two male rhinos argue over a territory, they sometimes butt each other with their horns. This decides who is stronger.
2231.m: Male rhinos fight with their horns.

a: Standing on one leg, head tucked into their feathers
Hanging upside down from a perch
2232.e: When sleeping, the budgie often stands on one leg and tucks its head into its feathers. This keeps it warm and rested.
2232.m: Budgies often sleep on one leg.

2233.q: Which statement about alpacas is correct?
2233.e: Unlike camels in Asia or Africa, New World camelids such as the alpaca have no humps. They are more slender overall.

2234.q: What is special about how brown bear embryos develop?
a: Their development is delayed and only continues in late autumn
They develop completely straight after mating
The embryos only grow in water
They need no time at all to develop
2234.e: In brown bears, the embryo's development is put on hold, so it only properly continues in late autumn. This makes sure the young are born right during the winter rest.
2234.m: Bear embryos only grow on late in the year.

2235.q: What is one way a puma marks its territory?
a: With scratch marks and scent marks
2235.e: Pumas scrape soil and leaves into piles and leave urine or droppings there. This is a message to other pumas.
2235.m: Pumas mark with scent and scratching.

2236.q: What colour are the great crested grebe's eyes?
2236.e: The bright red eyes are a striking feature of the great crested grebe. They are especially easy to see in its breeding plumage.
2236.m: Red eyes are typical of grebes.

2237.q: Why are some penguin species endangered today?
a: Because of climate change and less food in the sea
Because there are too many penguins
2237.e: Climate change is melting ice and changing where penguins find food. So some penguin species have less habitat and food today.
2237.m: Climate change threatens some penguin species.

2238.q: Roughly how long does the grey heron sit on its eggs?
2238.e: After about four weeks, the young grey herons hatch from their eggs. During this time, the parents take turns keeping the clutch warm.

2239.q: Which bird family does the common raven belong to?
2239.e: The common raven belongs to the crow family, the Corvidae. This family also includes crows, magpies and jackdaws.
2239.m: The raven belongs to the crow family.

2240.q: What colour are the great crested grebe's freshly laid eggs at first?
a: Whitish, later turning brownish from the nest material
2240.e: The eggs are light at first and take on a brownish colour from the damp plant material in the nest. This camouflages them even more.
2240.m: The nest stains the eggs brown.

2241.q: What does the fire salamander do when it feels seriously threatened?
a: It squirts poison from the glands behind its eyes
It plays dead and doesn't move
It jumps high into the air
2241.e: In great danger, the fire salamander can squirt poison from the glands behind its eyes. This is meant to scare off predators.

2242.q: What is the list that endangered animals such as the chimpanzee are on called?
2242.e: The Red List includes animals that are threatened and need special protection. The chimpanzee is one of them.
2242.m: Endangered animals are on the Red List.

2243.q: What is special about elephants' teeth?
a: They are replaced several times and wear down
It has only one set of teeth for ever
It has cutting teeth like a lion
It has no teeth at all
2243.e: The back teeth move from the back to the front and are replaced. In total there are six sets of teeth in a lifetime.
2243.m: Elephants replace their back teeth several times.

2244.q: Where does the garden spider lay its eggs?
a: In a cocoon made of spider silk
In an open hole in the ground
2244.e: The female spins a strong cocoon and lays many eggs in it. The cocoon protects the eggs from cold and enemies.
2244.m: The eggs lie in a cocoon.

2245.q: How are male common wall lizards often different from females?
a: Males are usually sturdier and more colourful
Males are always twice as long as females
2245.e: Males often show more striking colours and a sturdier build. They use this to impress rivals and attract females.

2247.q: Roughly how many eggs can a female European tree frog lay at once?
2247.e: A female usually lays several hundred eggs in batches. Not all the eggs end up becoming adult frogs.

2249.q: What pattern do the light spots on the garden spider's back form?
2249.e: The light spots are arranged so that they look like a cross. That is where the spider's other name, cross spider, comes from.

2250.q: How far can European tree frogs travel when they migrate to their breeding pond?
2250.e: To reach suitable ponds for laying eggs, tree frogs sometimes travel several kilometres. That is quite an achievement for such a small animal.
2250.m: Sometimes many kilometres to the pond.

2251.q: Which statement about the African wild dog is true?
a: It is a hunter that lives in groups
2251.e: It lives and hunts in a close-knit group. That makes it a very social predator.
2251.m: Wild dogs are very social animals.

2252.q: Can you watch blue whales in the wild in Switzerland?
2252.e: Blue whales live in the oceans, and Switzerland lies in the middle of Europe with no sea of its own. So you can't see them there in the wild.
2252.m: Blue whales only live in the sea.

2253.q: What is one way to protect the African wild dog?
a: Vaccinating pet dogs nearby against rabies
Splitting the packs into small groups
2253.e: Rabies and distemper are often passed on by pet dogs. Vaccination programmes and large protected areas help the packs.
2253.m: Vaccinations and protected areas help the wild dog.

2255.q: When does a cheetah usually hunt?
2255.e: Unlike many other big cats, the cheetah usually hunts during the day. With its good eyes, it sees prey from far away.
2255.m: Cheetahs hunt by day with sharp eyes.

2256.q: What is a converging lens used for, for example in glasses or a camera?
a: It brings light rays together at one point
It scatters light in all directions
It changes the colour of light
2256.e: A converging lens is thicker in the middle than at the edge and bends parallel light rays so that they meet at a focal point. This creates sharp images in cameras or on the retina.
2256.m: Converging lenses focus light at one point.

2257.q: Roughly how big is the red panda compared with a pet cat?
a: A bit bigger than a pet cat
Exactly the same size as an elephant
2257.e: The red panda is a dainty animal, a bit bigger than a pet cat. With its long tail, though, it looks bigger.
2257.m: The red panda is a bit bigger than a cat.

2258.q: How do meerkats react when a snake threatens them?
a: They often surround it and try to drive it away
2258.e: Several meerkats approach together and make pretend attacks. This is called mobbing behaviour.

2259.q: How does the tiny baby kangaroo get into its mother's pouch?
a: The mother carries it in her mouth
2259.e: Straight after birth, the tiny baby crawls all by itself through its mother's fur into the pouch. There it drinks milk and keeps growing.
2259.m: The baby crawls into the pouch by itself.

2261.q: Many African wild dogs live in the Selous Game Reserve. Which continent is it on?
2261.e: The Selous Game Reserve (now Nyerere National Park) is in the south of Tanzania in Africa. It is one of the most important areas for African wild dogs.
2261.m: The Selous Game Reserve is in Tanzania in Africa.

2262.q: What does a red squirrel eat in winter when its stores have run out?
a: Nothing, it goes hungry all winter
2262.e: When its stores run low, the squirrel also eats buds and bark from trees. This helps it get through the winter.
2262.m: In an emergency it eats buds and bark.

2263.q: How are peregrine falcon numbers in Switzerland today compared with the past?
a: They have clearly recovered after a decline
They are growing out of control
2263.e: After DDT was banned and thanks to protection measures, their numbers recovered. Today, many peregrines live in Switzerland again, even in towns.

2264.q: Roughly how long does a little kangaroo stay in the pouch?
2264.e: The young stays in its mother's warm pouch for many months. There it drinks milk and slowly gets bigger.
2264.m: Kangaroos stay in the pouch for months.

2265.q: What sounds does a stone marten make, especially during the breeding season?
2265.e: In the breeding season, stone martens get louder and make chattering or screaming calls. You hear these sounds mainly at night in summer.
2265.m: Chattering calls give away the breeding season.

2266.q: Do penguins have feathers on their feet?
a: No, their feet are almost bare
2266.e: Penguin feet have hardly any feathers. So that they still don't freeze, only a little warm blood flows into them.

2268.q: How well can a red squirrel jump?
a: It jumps skilfully from branch to branch
It only jumps on the ground
2268.e: Squirrels are excellent jumpers and leap safely from branch to branch, even across bigger gaps.

2269.q: Which animals are among the enemies of aphids and lay their eggs inside them?
2269.e: Some parasitic wasps lay an egg inside an aphid. The wasp larva then develops inside the aphid.
2269.m: Parasitic wasps use aphids for their young.

2270.e: The octopus has no real sense of hearing and can only sense sounds in a very limited way. But it sees and feels all the better.

2271.q: How do orang-utans mainly move about in the trees?
a: They glide with flaps of skin
2271.e: Orang-utans are heavy and move rather carefully. They usually hold on with several limbs.

2272.q: Which large predator with white fur lives on the Arctic ice?
2272.e: The polar bear is the largest predator on land and lives in the Arctic, not at the South Pole. Its thick fur and a layer of fat protect it from the cold.
2272.m: The polar bear lives on the Arctic ice.

2273.q: How many broods can a barn swallow have in one summer?
2273.e: Barn swallows usually breed twice a summer, sometimes three times. This way they can raise enough young despite many dangers.

2275.e: Unlike adult frogs, tadpoles mainly eat algae and soft plant parts in the water. Only as frogs do they become meat-eaters.

2276.q: Roughly how old can a wild peregrine falcon get?
2276.e: In the wild, peregrine falcons can live to about 15 to 17 years. But many young birds don't survive their first year.

2277.q: Which family does the elk belong to?
2277.e: The elk is a relative of the red deer and roe deer. It belongs to the deer family.

2278.q: Can adult brown bears climb trees?
a: Only rarely, as they are too heavy
Yes, just as well as young bears
No, no kind of bear can climb
2278.e: Young brown bears climb quite skilfully to protect themselves from danger. Adults, however, are usually too heavy to climb trees well.
2278.m: Young bears climb better than adults.

2279.q: Which statement about the size of the eagle owl is true?
a: It is one of the largest owls in the world
It is the smallest owl in the world
It is smaller than a blackbird
It is bigger than a golden eagle
2279.e: The eagle owl is the largest owl in Europe and one of the largest owls in the world. Females grow a little bigger than males.
2279.m: The eagle owl is one of the world's largest owls.

2280.q: What do two rams sometimes do to show which one is stronger?
2280.e: Rams sometimes crash their heads and horns together hard to show which one is stronger. This is called head-butting.
2280.m: Rams butt heads to test their strength.

2281.q: What is panting mainly for in dogs?
2281.e: Because dogs can hardly sweat through their bodies, they cool down by panting quickly. Moisture evaporates from the tongue and airways.

2282.q: In which habitats do you typically find the grey heron?
a: Only high in the mountains above 3000 metres
Only in thick, dark forest with no water
2282.e: The grey heron lives by all kinds of waters, as long as it can find fish and other prey there. Sometimes you can even find it by ponds in towns and cities.
2282.m: It lives where there is water.

2283.q: Why does the sparrow like living near people so much?
a: because it finds food and nesting places there
because it is afraid of trees
because it has to live in water
2283.e: In towns and villages the sparrow finds lots of crumbs and good places to nest. That is why it likes living where people live.

2284.q: What helps trout get past small obstacles such as steps in a river?
2284.e: A fish ladder is made of several small steps in the water that make it easier for fish like trout to swim upwards. This way they get past obstacles.
2284.m: Fish ladders help trout on their journeys.

2286.q: How do male sand lizards often behave towards rivals in the mating season?
a: They fight and defend their territory against other males
They always share a territory peacefully
They leave the area at once
2286.e: Rival males can really bite each other to secure their territory and access to females. Such fights are seen more often in spring.
2286.m: Males defend their territory by fighting.

2288.q: Why are hamsters often hard to hold on to when you want to catch them?
a: They can escape through small holes
2288.e: Hamsters are very quick and can slip through tiny gaps. That is why they sometimes escape from their cage very fast.

2289.q: Which well-known film character from “Madagascar” is a ring-tailed lemur?
2289.e: In the “Madagascar” films, King Julien is a ring-tailed lemur. This made the animals better known around the world.
2289.m: King Julien is a ring-tailed lemur.

2290.q: What do many aphids release from two small tubes on their back end when an enemy comes?
2290.e: The two tubes on the back end are called siphunculi. A sticky defensive substance comes out of them, which is meant to scare off enemies.
2290.m: Aphids defend themselves with a sticky substance.

2291.q: Which Swiss organisation works, among other things, to protect amphibians such as the fire salamander?
2291.e: Pro Natura works to protect endangered habitats and species in Switzerland, including amphibians such as the fire salamander. For example, it supports measures such as amphibian fences.

2292.q: Does the European pond turtle live in salt water or fresh water?
a: Only in the salt water of the sea
Only in springs high in the Alps
Neither in water nor on land
2292.e: It lives in ponds, pools and old side arms of rivers. Sea turtles, on the other hand, are a completely different group.
2292.m: Pond turtles live in fresh water.

2293.q: What do bison like doing to get rid of parasites and look after their skin?
a: They roll in dust or sand
They bathe in lakes full of fish
2293.e: The dust bath helps against annoying insects and keeps the coat in good condition. The hollows it leaves behind are called wallows.
2293.m: Dust baths keep the bison’s coat healthy.

2294.q: How does a donkey usually behave when it gets a fright?
a: It often stands still calmly instead of running away
It jumps into the air at once
2294.e: Unlike horses, which often run off at once when in danger, donkeys often stand still first and watch what is happening. This helps them react sensibly.
2294.m: Donkeys often stay calm in danger.

2295.q: What happens when a mute swan is frightened and cannot fly away?
a: it attacks with a loud hiss
it disappears under water for hours
2295.e: If the swan feels cornered, it can suddenly attack. It hisses and snorts loudly as it does so.
2295.m: In an emergency the swan attacks.

2296.q: Spiders have no bones. What protects their body?
2296.e: Spiders do not have bones inside them like we do. Instead, a hard shell protects them from the outside. This is called an exoskeleton.
2296.m: Their skeleton is on the outside of the body.

2297.q: What does a mute swan like to eat most?
2297.e: Mute swans feed mainly on plants in and around the water. Meat hardly plays a part in their diet.

2298.q: Does a starfish have a heart?
2298.e: A starfish does not have a heart like we humans do. Its body works in a completely different way.

2299.q: How does a ring-tailed lemur usually move about on the ground?
a: With long hops like a kangaroo
2299.e: On the ground the ring-tailed lemur usually walks on four legs with its tail held up. In trees it jumps and climbs skilfully.
2299.m: Ring-tailed lemurs mostly walk on four legs.

2300.q: Why are small tunnels sometimes built under roads for frogs in Switzerland?
a: So that they can travel safely to their pond
So that they can spend the winter in them
So that they can lay their eggs in them
So that they can hide from the sun
2300.e: In spring many common frogs cross roads on their way to their ponds. Tunnels and fences help them reach their goal safely without being run over.

2301.q: What does the pike use to breathe under water?
2301.e: Like all fish, the pike breathes with gills. With them it takes in the oxygen dissolved in the water.

2302.q: At about what age do young wolf pups first open their eyes?
2302.e: In their first days of life, wolf pups are blind and helpless. Only after around two weeks do they slowly open their eyes and start to explore their surroundings.
2302.m: Pups open their eyes after about two weeks.

2303.q: Why did Yugoslavia under Tito have a special role among the communist states?
a: It stayed independent of the Soviet Union and went its own way
It was the Soviet Union's most loyal ally
It was the first country to introduce capitalism
2303.e: Josip Broz Tito broke with Stalin in 1948 and led Yugoslavia as a non-aligned socialist state. The country belonged neither to NATO nor to the Warsaw Pact.
2303.m: Tito went his own socialist way.

2304.q: How does an earwig develop from egg to adult?
a: Through larval stages without a pupa
Through a pupa, like a butterfly
It hatches fully formed straight away
It grows up as a worm in water
2304.e: A larva hatches from the egg and moults several times. There is no pupal stage.
2304.m: No pupa, just larvae that moult.

2305.q: Where does the mother mole build her nest for her young?
a: In a soft chamber deep underground
2305.e: Deep in her tunnel system the mother mole builds a cosy chamber. She lines it with grass and leaves.

2306.e: Only the male roe buck has antlers on his head. They fall off every year and grow back again.

2307.q: What is an ovipositor in female dragonflies?
a: An organ for inserting eggs into plants
A tool for digging in the ground
2307.e: Many damselflies and some larger dragonflies use the ovipositor to insert eggs into plant tissue. This keeps the eggs protected.
2307.m: The ovipositor puts eggs into plants.

2309.q: Which fish family does the European perch belong to?
2309.e: The European perch, called Egli in Switzerland, belongs to the true perch family. This family also includes, for example, the zander and the ruffe.
2309.m: The perch belongs to the true perches.

2310.q: About how fast can a barn swallow fly?
2310.e: Barn swallows can reach speeds of about 50 to 60 km/h in flight. They are very agile and can change direction quickly.
2310.m: The barn swallow flies at up to 60 km/h.

2311.q: What other role do cockchafer grubs play in the ecosystem?
a: They are food for many animals
2311.e: Cockchafer grubs are food for moles, badgers, hedgehogs and birds. This makes them part of the food chain.
2311.m: Grubs are food for other animals.

2312.q: What does a squirrel often do with its tail when it is excited?
a: It flicks it quickly back and forth
It goes completely stiff for ever
2312.e: When a squirrel is excited or alarmed, its tail flicks quickly. This is how it shows its mood.
2312.m: The tail flicks when it is excited.

2313.q: Which group of animals does the harbour seal belong to, even though it has flippers?
2313.e: The harbour seal belongs to the order of carnivores, even though it looks very different from a lion or a wolf. It feeds mainly on fish.
2313.m: The harbour seal is a carnivore.

2314.q: What is the mating season like for ring-tailed lemurs?
a: It lasts only a short time each year
It happens only every ten years
2314.e: Ring-tailed lemurs mate only during a short season. Because of this, the young are born at about the same time.

2316.e: Pigs grunt to tell other pigs something. Depending on whether they are happy or afraid, the grunting sounds different.

2317.q: Why does a house fly so often escape when you try to catch it?
a: Because it spots movements very quickly
Because it smells and nobody wants to touch it
2317.e: The fly’s compound eyes detect the tiniest movement in a flash. That is why it usually flies away before a hand can catch it.
2317.m: Flies see movements in a flash.

2318.q: What are the calluses on the chest and knees of the Bactrian camel for?
a: They cushion it when it lies down on hot or hard ground
2318.e: The hard pads protect the skin when the camel lies down. That way the skin does not get injured or burnt.
2318.m: Calluses cushion and protect the skin.

2319.q: What does an earthworm do with the leaves it pulls into its tunnels?
a: It digests them into nutrient-rich humus
It builds a roof with them
2319.e: Earthworms eat leaves together with soil. What comes out is fertile humus for the soil.

2320.q: How clever are pigs thought to be compared with other domestic animals?
a: They are thought to be one of the cleverest domestic animals
They are thought to be rather unintelligent
They are less clever than fish
They cannot learn anything at all
2320.e: Studies show that pigs learn very well and can solve tasks, for example. Some researchers even compare their intelligence with that of dogs.

2321.q: Which dangerous disease must a dog be vaccinated against if it travels abroad?
2321.e: Rabies is a dangerous viral disease that can also infect humans. Switzerland is considered free of rabies, so a dog needs the vaccination mainly for trips abroad.
2321.m: Dogs need a rabies jab to travel abroad.

2322.q: Which sense is especially strong in the wolf?
2322.e: With their sensitive noses, wolves can detect tracks and prey from a long way off. Their sense of smell is much better than that of humans.
2322.m: Wolves have an excellent sense of smell.

2323.q: What kind of animal is the pike?
2323.e: The pike is a fish that hunts other animals. Fish like this are called predatory fish.
2323.m: The pike is a predatory fish.

2324.q: In which country does the okapi live in the wild?
2324.e: The okapi lives only in the rainforests in the north-east and centre of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It is not found in the wild anywhere else.
2324.m: Okapis live only in the Congo.

2325.q: How long does a mother rhino carry her baby before it is born?
2325.e: A mother rhino carries her baby for about 15 months, which is over a year. That is much longer than in most animals.
2325.m: Rhino babies grow for 15 months before birth.

2326.q: Why do wasps have the warning colours yellow and black?
2326.e: The bright colours tell other animals: careful, I can sting. That is why many enemies prefer to leave the wasp alone.
2326.m: Yellow and black warn of a sting.

2327.q: What are the dark patches around the panda’s eyes probably for?
a: They help with camouflage and communication
2327.e: Researchers think that the dark eye patches help camouflage the panda from enemies. Other pandas can also recognise the patches.
2327.m: Eye patches camouflage and help with recognition.

2328.q: About how big does an adult hedgehog get?
2328.e: An adult hedgehog usually measures between 20 and 30 centimetres. That means it fits nicely into a flower bed or under hedges.
2328.m: Hedgehogs grow to about 20 to 30 centimetres.

2329.q: In brown bears, which sex is usually bigger and heavier?
a: Both are always the same weight
2329.e: Male brown bears are usually much bigger and heavier than the females. This difference is especially noticeable during the mating season.

2330.q: The praying mantis belongs to the group called mantises. Is it a true grasshopper?
a: No, it forms its own group of insects
Yes, it is a large bush cricket
Yes, it is a kind of cricket
2330.e: Mantises are a separate order of insects. The German name “Fangschrecke” comes from its grasping legs, but mantises are not closely related to true grasshoppers.

2331.q: Which habitat did the huge bison herds of North America mainly live in?
a: The prairie, an open grassland landscape
2331.e: The prairie offers lots of grass to eat. The herds travelled long distances there.
2331.m: Bison lived mainly on the prairie.

2332.q: What colour is a great tit’s belly?
2332.e: The great tit has a bright yellow belly. It also has a black stripe down the middle.
2332.m: Great tits have a yellow belly.

2333.q: What role does the otter play as an indicator in the ecosystem?
2333.e: Because otters can only survive in clean waters with enough fish, they are considered important indicators of healthy rivers and lakes. If they return, it is a good sign.

2334.q: How does a herd of African buffalo often defend itself against lions?
a: The animals face the attacker together
All the animals hide under the surface of the water
They bury themselves in the ground
2334.e: The herd can fight off attackers with their horns. Sometimes buffalo even rescue a herd member in danger.
2334.m: Together, buffalo are strong against attackers.

2335.q: How many cubs does a female brown bear usually have in one litter?
2335.e: A female brown bear usually has one to three cubs, sometimes four. The cubs are born during the winter rest in the safety of the den.
2335.m: Brown bears usually have two cubs.

2336.q: Whose droppings do minotaur beetles and their larvae often feed on?
2336.e: The minotaur beetle carries rabbit or sheep droppings into its tunnels. There they serve as a food store for the larvae.
2336.m: Minotaur beetles collect rabbit and sheep droppings.

2337.q: Does the sparrow fly to a warm country in winter?
a: no, it stays here all year
yes, it always flies to Africa
yes, it flies to the North Pole
yes, it flies to an island
2337.e: Sparrows are resident birds, which means they stay in one place all year round. So they have to find food here in winter too.
2337.m: Sparrows don’t fly away in winter.

2338.q: Which animal are all pet rabbits descended from?
2338.e: All pet rabbits were bred from the European wild rabbit many hundreds of years ago. That is why they still look similar.
2338.m: Pet rabbits come from the wild rabbit.

2339.q: How do budgies often greet each other with their beaks?
a: They pull each other’s feathers out
2339.e: Budgies often greet each other by gently touching beaks. It is a friendly gesture between friends.
2339.m: A gentle beak touch is a greeting.

2341.q: What is typical of the shape of the great crested grebe’s beak?
a: It is pointed and dagger-like, good for catching fish
It is broad and flat like a duck’s
It is strongly hooked like a bird of prey’s
It is tiny and hardly visible
2341.e: The pointed, dagger-like beak is excellent for catching slippery fish under water. It is also used as a signal during courtship.
2341.m: The beak is as pointed as a dagger.

2342.q: Does the mother slow worm look after her young?
a: No, the young are independent from the start
Yes, she feeds them in the nest
Yes, she carries them on her back
2342.e: The young have to manage on their own straight after birth. They soon eat small prey.
2342.m: Young slow worms are independent at once.

2343.q: About how much does an adult barn owl weigh?
2343.e: An adult barn owl weighs about as much as three bars of chocolate, so around 300 to 350 grams. That is why it flies so lightly.
2343.m: It weighs only a few hundred grams.

a: No, they have a horny beak
Only a few teeth at the front
2344.e: Sea turtles have no teeth. Instead they have a hard beak made of horn, which they use to break up their food.
2344.m: Instead of teeth they have a horny beak.

2345.q: Does rhino horn really help against illnesses, as some people believe?
a: No, that has not been proven
2345.e: Scientists have shown that the horn has no special healing power. It is made only of keratin, like our fingernails. Sadly, rhinos are still hunted for it.
2345.m: The horn has no healing power.

2346.q: When are chamois kids usually born?
2346.e: Most chamois kids are born in late spring, in May or June. By then there is already enough fresh green food in the mountains for the mother.
2346.m: Chamois kids are born in May or June.

2347.q: How does a pig use its snout to explore its surroundings?
a: It feels and smells things very precisely with it
It sees in the dark with it
It drinks with it like a straw
2347.e: The snout is full of sensitive nerves. With it, the pig feels and smells everything very precisely.
2347.m: The snout is for both touch and smell.

2348.q: What happens to a sick or very old bee in the hive?
a: Other bees carry it out of the hive
2348.e: Everything in the hive must stay clean so that diseases do not spread. That is why healthy bees carry dead or sick bees out of the hive.
2348.m: Sick bees are carried out of the hive.

2349.e: The octopus lives in salty sea water, often near the coast or in the deep sea. It is not found in fresh water.
2349.m: The octopus lives in the sea.

2350.q: What does the brown trout use to take in oxygen from the water?
2350.e: Water flows through the mouth and over the gills. There the oxygen passes into the blood.

2352.q: Which is usually bigger, the male or the female garden spider?
a: Both are always exactly the same size
2352.e: Female garden spiders are much bigger than the males. They need the bigger body to carry lots of eggs.

2353.q: What are some kinds of duck, such as the tufted duck, especially good at?
2353.e: Diving ducks such as the tufted duck go right under water to look for food on the bottom. Dabbling ducks, on the other hand, do not dive as deep.

2354.q: What does the Roman snail use to move?
2354.e: The snail glides on a single broad muscular foot. It moves in wave-like motions.

2355.q: How should you approach a guinea pig before you pick it up?
2355.e: Guinea pigs are easily frightened. That is why it is important to approach them slowly and calmly so that they feel safe.
2355.m: Always approach a guinea pig calmly and carefully.

2356.q: Which sense is especially good in the rhino?
2356.e: A rhino has a very good sense of smell and can recognise enemies or friends from far away. Its sense of smell is more important than its eyes.
2356.m: Rhinos have an excellent sense of smell.

2357.q: About how many aphids can a ladybird eat in a single day?
2357.e: Ladybirds are very greedy and can eat several dozen aphids in a day. That is why they are a great help to gardeners.
2357.m: A ladybird eats lots of aphids a day.

2358.q: What is the male roe deer called?
2358.e: The male roe deer is called a roe buck. Only he has antlers.

2359.q: What do pet rabbits absolutely need when they are kept?
a: Enough space to hop and hide
A small cage with no run
2359.e: Rabbits need lots of space to hop and hide. Other rabbits and a run are also important for their wellbeing.

2360.q: Which animal is often called the “king of the animals”?
2360.e: The lion lives in Africa in groups called prides. Because of its mane and strength it is often called the king of the animals.
2360.m: The lion is the king of the savannah.

2361.q: On average, how many hours a day does a cat sleep?
2361.e: Cats are champion sleepers and often doze for 12 to 16 hours a day. This saves energy for hunting.
2361.m: Cats sleep for half the day.

2362.q: What colour is an adult peregrine falcon’s back usually?
2362.e: Adult peregrine falcons have a typical blue-grey back. This camouflages them well against the sky.
2362.m: Blue-grey is the falcon’s back colour.

2364.q: What is the male salmon called at spawning time, when its lower jaw curves?
2364.e: At spawning time males develop a hook-shaped lower jaw, called a kype. It is used mainly in fights with rivals.
2364.m: The kype shows a male salmon.

2366.q: Which insect is a well-known predator of aphids?
2366.e: Ladybirds and their larvae eat huge numbers of aphids. That is why they are considered helpful creatures in the garden.
2366.m: Ladybirds and their larvae eat aphids.

2367.q: What is the biggest threat to gibbons today?
a: Too cold a climate in the tropics
2367.e: Gibbons need tall trees to move about and find food. When the forest is cut down, they lose their habitat.

2368.q: How can you often tell an alpaca from a llama by its appearance?
a: The alpaca is smaller and has shorter ears
The alpaca is bigger than a horse
2368.e: Alpacas are smaller and lighter than llamas and have shorter, pointed ears. Their face also looks flatter.

2369.q: What is the best way to help dragonflies in the garden?
a: With a natural pond without fish
With a concrete pool without plants
2369.e: A pond with plants at the edge and under water gives larvae and dragonflies a place to live. Fish would eat many of the larvae.

2370.q: About how much weight can a llama carry?
a: About a quarter of its body weight
Just as much as a horse
Only a tenth of its weight
2370.e: A llama carries about 25 to 30 kilograms. If the load is too heavy, it often lies down.
2370.m: Llamas carry about a quarter of their weight.
