2371.q: How many eggs does a female common swift usually lay in a clutch?
2371.e: A swift’s clutch usually has two or three white eggs. The parents could hardly feed more young with insects.
2371.m: There are usually two to three eggs in the nest.

2374.q: What does the great spotted woodpecker eat most in summer?
2374.e: In summer there are lots of beetles and larvae under the bark. These are its main food at that time.

2375.q: What sound do you often hear when a mute swan flies?
a: a whistling sound from its wings
2375.e: The wings of a flying mute swan make a special whistling sound. Sometimes you can hear it before you see it.
2375.m: Swans’ wings whistle as they fly.

2376.q: What do the feathered young birds do shortly before they fly for the first time?
a: They practise flapping their wings at the edge of the nest
They jump straight into the air without any preparation
They suddenly grow twice as big overnight
They lose all their feathers and have to grow new ones
2376.e: Shortly before their first flight, young kestrels train their flight muscles by flapping their wings hard at the edge of the nest. This prepares them for their first real flight.
2376.m: Wing flapping is practice for the first flight.

a: Yes, its population is considered vulnerable
No, there are huge numbers of giraffes everywhere
2377.e: Because of habitat loss and poaching, the number of giraffes has fallen sharply in recent decades. That is why conservationists are working to protect them.

2378.q: Which group of animals is related to millipedes and has six legs?
2378.e: Like millipedes, insects belong to the animals that breathe through tubes called tracheae. But they have only three pairs of legs.

2379.q: What does a chimpanzee like to eat most?
2379.e: Chimpanzees especially like sweet fruit such as figs. Sometimes they also eat leaves, insects or a little meat.
2379.m: Fruit is the chimpanzee’s favourite food.

2380.q: What does the grass snake often give off when in danger?
2380.e: It can release a stinking liquid from glands on its body. This scares off enemies.
2380.m: A bad smell protects against enemies.

2381.q: Which animal has been the most common symbol of courage and kingship in European heraldry since the Middle Ages?
2381.e: The lion has been the most common heraldic animal in Europe since the Middle Ages and stands for courage, strength and kingship. It appears on the coats of arms of England, Belgium and the Netherlands, among others.
2381.m: The lion symbolises courage and kingship.

2382.e: Baby dolphins are born tail first. This way they can quickly swim up to breathe as soon as the head is free.
2382.m: Baby dolphins come out tail first.

2383.q: What role did the kestrel play in traditional falconry in the past?
a: It was seen as a falcon for beginners because it was easier to train
It was never used in falconry
It was the most feared hunting bird for large game birds
Only kings were ever allowed to train it
2383.e: In traditional falconry the kestrel was seen as a bird for beginners and simpler hunting, because it was easier to train than larger falcons. Today it is hardly used in falconry any more.
2383.m: The kestrel was seen as a beginner’s falcon.

2384.q: About how thick is a hippo’s skin?
2384.e: A hippo’s skin is very thick, often several centimetres. This protects it well from injuries in fights.
2384.m: Hippo skin is several centimetres thick.

2385.q: Why are alpacas sheared in spring or summer?
a: So that they don’t get too hot when it is warm
So that they call more loudly
2385.e: The thick fleece can get too warm in summer. After shearing it grows back again.

2386.q: What do otters have between their toes?
2386.e: The webbed feet help the otter move quickly and skilfully in the water. Without them it would be a much worse swimmer.
2386.m: Webbed feet make the otter a swimming pro.

2387.q: Which members of a lion pride hunt most often?
2387.e: Usually the lionesses hunt together because they are faster and more agile. The males protect the territory instead.
2387.m: Lionesses usually hunt for the pride.

2388.q: What do red deer often do in winter when there is little food?
a: They move down into the valley
2388.e: In winter red deer go to lower areas. There is less snow and more food to be found there.
2388.m: In winter deer move down to the valley.

2389.q: Which prey animals do African wild dogs often hunt?
2389.e: Wild dogs mainly hunt medium-sized hoofed animals, for example antelopes. Elephants and rhinos are far too big.
2389.m: Antelopes are often on the menu.

2390.e: A glacier forms when snow is pressed together into ice over many years. There are many glaciers in the Swiss Alps.
2390.m: A glacier is a large mass of ice.

2391.q: How often does a pair of golden eagles use the same eyrie?
a: Often again and again over many years
Never for longer than a week
Each year in a completely different place
2391.e: A pair of golden eagles usually has several eyries in its territory and uses them in turn over years or decades. The eyries are repaired again and again.
2391.m: Eyries are reused for many years.

2392.q: Which group of animals does the common frog belong to?
2392.e: The common frog is an amphibian. Amphibians live both in water and on land.

2393.q: What does the hammerhead shark like to eat?
2393.e: The hammerhead shark hunts fish and likes to look for rays hidden in the sand. With its wide head it is good at tracking them down.
2393.m: The hammerhead hunts fish and rays.

2394.q: What nickname do camels have because they can cross the desert?
2394.e: Like a ship, the dromedary carries people and goods across a vast and hostile area. That is where the nickname comes from.
2394.m: Dromedaries are called ships of the desert.

2395.q: In German, walking “im Gänsemarsch” means walking like geese. What does it mean?
a: Walking one behind the other in a line
2395.e: Geese often walk one behind the other in a line. So this saying describes people walking just as neatly one behind the other, like walking in single file.
2395.m: In a goose march you walk in single file.

2396.q: What is a typical feature of the places marmots prefer for their burrows?
a: Loose but stable soil on sunny slopes
Only steep rock faces with no soil
2396.e: Marmots prefer loose but stable enough soil on sunny slopes for their burrows. Places like this are easy to dig and offer plenty of warmth.

2397.q: Where is the garden spider often found in Switzerland?
a: In gardens, meadows and at the edge of woods
Only high above the snow line
2397.e: In Switzerland the garden spider lives in gardens, in meadows and at the edge of woods. There it finds lots of plants for its web.
2397.m: It often lives in the garden.

2398.q: Apart from fighting, what other job do a stag’s antlers have?
a: They show other stags how strong it is
They are used to cut grass
2398.e: Large antlers show other stags straight away how strong an animal is. This way weaker stags often avoid a fight.

2399.q: Which enemies mainly threaten the eggs and young of grey herons in the colony?
2399.e: Members of the crow family and some birds of prey sometimes raid unguarded nests. Adult grey herons, on the other hand, have hardly any natural enemies.
2399.m: Crows threaten eggs and young birds.

2400.q: What does the common buzzard use its hooked beak for?
a: To dig holes in the ground
2400.e: The downward-curved, hooked beak helps the buzzard tear meat from its prey. To kill, however, it mainly uses its talons.
2400.m: The hooked beak tears the meat.

2401.q: What do several ravens often do together when they find a large carcass?
a: they call other ravens over and eat together
they hide the find from everyone else at once
they fly away and ignore it
they attack each other at once
2401.e: At large food sources ravens often attract others of their kind, which lets them deal with large animals such as a carcass together. This way several birds benefit from the find at the same time.
2401.m: Ravens call others to a find.

a: No, they don’t bite or sting dangerously
Yes, they sting with a poisonous sting
2402.e: Cockchafers are harmless to humans. At most they can tickle with their legs.

2403.q: What colour is the okapi’s tongue?
2403.e: The okapi’s tongue is dark and bluish in colour. The same is true of the giraffe.
2403.m: Okapis and giraffes have dark tongues.

2404.q: What colour is an octopus usually when it isn’t camouflaging itself?
2404.e: Without camouflage, the skin of many octopuses is brownish or grey. This matches the sand and stones on the sea floor well.

2405.q: How do many grasshoppers survive the winter in Switzerland?
a: They swim through the winter in a pond
2405.e: The eggs lie protected in the ground while it is cold outside. In spring, new little grasshoppers hatch from them.
2405.m: The eggs wait safely in the ground.

2406.q: How does the common wall lizard reproduce?
a: It gives birth to live young
2406.e: The common wall lizard lays eggs. This is called being oviparous. The young later hatch from the eggs on their own.

2407.q: How does the grass snake reproduce?
a: It gives birth to live young in water
2407.e: In summer the female lays eggs with a soft, leathery shell. They are often laid in warm places.

2408.q: Which bird is a close relative of the magpie and has blue feathers on its wing?
2408.e: Like the magpie, the jay belongs to the crow family. Its blue and black barred wing feathers are typical.
2408.m: The jay is a member of the crow family like the magpie.

2409.q: Where do mute swans usually build their nest?
a: on the bank among the reeds
in a crack in the rocks
in the middle of the forest
2409.e: Swans build their nest right by the water, often hidden in the reeds. This keeps the eggs well protected.
2409.m: Nests are on the bank among the reeds.

2410.q: Where does the kingfisher build its nest?
a: in a hole it digs itself in a steep riverbank
in reed nests on the water
in cracks in the rocks of high mountains
2410.e: Kingfishers dig a nesting tunnel into vertical banks along rivers and streams. At the end of the tunnel there is a small nest chamber.
2410.m: A nesting tunnel in a steep riverbank.

2411.q: Are there also wasps that live completely alone?
a: Yes, many kinds of wasp live alone
No, all wasps live in large colonies
No, wasps always live in pairs
Yes, but only the queen in summer
2411.e: Besides the well-known wasps with large colonies, there are many species that live alone. They build their nest without a queen and without helpers.

2412.q: What do llamas lack compared with dromedaries and Bactrian camels?
2412.e: Llamas have no hump on their back. This is how they differ from the camels of the Old World.

2413.q: Why do people say that someone with very sharp eyes is “lynx-eyed”?
a: Because of the lynx’s sharp gaze and good eyes
Because of its love of fish
Because of the colour of its fur
2413.e: The lynx has long been said to have especially sharp eyesight. That is where expressions for keen, careful watching come from, such as “lynx-eyed” in English and “luchsen” in German.
2413.m: Sharp eyes gave us the expression.

2414.q: How well can an elk swim?
a: Very well, even over long distances
2414.e: Elk are good swimmers and cross lakes and rivers. They can also dive to reach water plants.

2415.q: Why do tigers often hide in tall grass or bushes?
2415.e: In tall grass tigers can hide well and creep up on their prey unnoticed. Their stripes help them to hardly stand out.

2416.q: Do blue whales usually live in huge herds or rather alone?
a: Usually alone or in small groups
Always in huge herds of a thousand animals
Always in families of a hundred animals
2416.e: Blue whales often travel alone or stay in small groups. Only rarely do you find many of them in one place.

2417.q: What does a harbour seal pup’s fur usually look like shortly after birth?
a: Grey with spots like its parents’
2417.e: Most harbour seal pups are born with grey, spotted fur, similar to their parents. They have usually already lost their white baby fur before birth.
2417.m: Harbour seal pups already look like their parents.

2419.q: What should you rather not give ducks in the park?
2419.e: Bread is unhealthy for ducks and fills them up quickly without giving them important nutrients. Oat flakes or special duck food are better.

2420.q: What is the bee dance for?
a: To show other bees the way to food
2420.e: With a special dance a bee shows her sisters where there are lots of flowers with nectar. This way the whole colony finds the best source of food.
2420.m: The dance shows the way to food.

2421.q: How does a common toad usually move about?
a: it hops a long way like a frog
2421.e: Common toads have shorter back legs than frogs, so they move more by crawling. Only sometimes do they make small hops.

2422.q: What can you often see barn swallows doing before it rains?
a: They fly especially low because that is where the insects are
They disappear completely and are never seen again
They build a new nest at once
They sing much louder than usual
2422.e: Before rain many insects fly lower because the air is damper and heavier. The barn swallows follow them and so also fly especially low.
2422.m: Low flying often means rain is coming.

2423.q: About how fast can a chamois run when fleeing?
2423.e: When fleeing from danger a chamois can reach speeds of up to 50 kilometres per hour. It moves very surely even on steep ground.
2423.m: Chamois flee at up to 50 km/h.

2424.q: What does the octopus need from the water in order to breathe?
2424.e: Like many water animals, the octopus needs oxygen to breathe. It takes it from sea water with its gills.
2424.m: The octopus needs oxygen to breathe.

2425.q: Is the common toad protected in Switzerland?
a: no, you can catch and sell it
2425.e: The common toad is a protected species in Switzerland. So you must not simply catch it or harm it.
2425.m: Common toads are protected in Switzerland.

a: The leader of the Khmer Rouge in Cambodia.
2427.e: Pol Pot ruled Cambodia in the 1970s. Under his rule around two million people died from violence, hunger and forced labour.
2427.m: Pol Pot was responsible for millions of deaths.

2429.q: Why is chocolate dangerous for cats?
a: the substance theobromine is poisonous to them
they don’t like the taste and are sick because of it
chocolate only makes them hyperactive for a short time
2429.e: Chocolate contains theobromine, which cats and dogs cannot break down properly. Even small amounts can cause serious poisoning.
2429.m: Theobromine in chocolate is poisonous to cats.

2430.q: How many ribs does an adult usually have?
2430.e: People usually have 12 pairs of ribs, so 24 ribs. They form the ribcage and protect the heart and lungs.
2430.m: 24 ribs protect the heart and lungs.

2431.q: Which big obstacles do barn swallows have to cross on their migration to Africa?
2431.e: On their way to Africa barn swallows have to cross the Mediterranean Sea and the huge Sahara. These are dangerous stretches where many birds do not survive.
2431.m: The Mediterranean and the Sahara are big obstacles.

a: The majority of all voters in Switzerland say Yes
The Federal Council votes for the people
2432.e: The popular majority is reached when more than half of the votes cast say Yes. For changes to the constitution, a majority of the cantons is also needed.
2432.m: The popular majority means more than half say Yes.

2433.q: About how long is a female puma pregnant?
2433.e: The young are born after around 90 days. They usually hide in a sheltered den.
2433.m: Pumas are pregnant for about three months.

2434.q: Is the mole specially protected in Switzerland?
a: It is protected in some cantons
It can be hunted anywhere without rules
It is a pet and is sold
It doesn’t live in Switzerland at all
2434.e: In some Swiss cantons the mole is protected because it is useful for the soil. So you must not simply catch or kill it.
2434.m: Moles are protected in some places.

2435.q: What does the blue shark mainly eat?
2435.e: In the open sea the blue shark mainly hunts fish and squid. Its back shimmers blue, so it is well camouflaged from above.
2435.m: The blue shark eats fish and squid.

2436.q: How many eggs does a robin usually lay?
2436.e: A robin usually lays five to six eggs in its nest. That is quite a large number for such a small bird.
2436.m: Robins lay five to six eggs.

2437.q: Did sharks exist before dinosaurs lived on Earth?
a: Sharks and dinosaurs appeared at exactly the same time
Sharks have only existed for 100 years
2437.e: Sharks have lived on Earth for a very, very long time. They were already here long before there were dinosaurs.
2437.m: Sharks have existed for longer than dinosaurs.

2438.q: What are the stripes on the okapi’s legs probably for?
a: Camouflage in the half-light of the forest
2438.e: In the shade of the forest the stripes look like light and shadow. This helps with camouflage and helps mother and young find each other.
2438.m: Stripes help with camouflage in the forest.

2439.q: Is a red deer a plant eater or a meat eater?
2439.e: The red deer eats only plants such as grass, leaves and buds. So it is a pure plant eater.
2439.m: The red deer is a plant eater.

2440.q: Which bird had been wiped out in the Alps and was reintroduced from 1986?
2440.e: The bearded vulture had been wiped out in the Alps and was successfully reintroduced from 1986. Today it flies over the Swiss mountains again.
2440.m: The bearded vulture returned to the Alps.

2441.q: What happens when a kangaroo walks slowly instead of hopping?
a: It also supports itself with its tail
It rolls up into a ball
2441.e: When walking slowly the kangaroo uses its tail like an extra leg for support. So it moves forward as if on three legs.
2441.m: The tail acts as a third leg.

2442.q: What is typical of a kestrel’s talons?
a: They are sharp and curved to hold prey
They are blunt and used only for walking
They are soft like a chicken’s
This species has none at all
2442.e: As in all birds of prey, the kestrel’s talons are sharp and strongly curved. With them it can grip and hold its prey securely.
2442.m: Sharp talons grip the prey tightly.

2443.q: How can a male goldfish sometimes look different from a female at spawning time?
a: Males get small white spots on their gill covers and fins
2443.e: At spawning time male goldfish often show small white spots, called breeding tubercles, on their gill covers and chest fins. This way you can sometimes tell males and females apart.
2443.m: Males show white spots at spawning time.

2444.q: What does the blood-brain barrier do?
a: It protects the brain from harmful substances in the blood
It pumps blood into the brain
2444.e: The blood-brain barrier is a special barrier in the blood vessels of the brain. It only lets certain substances through to the delicate nerve tissue.
2444.m: The blood-brain barrier protects your brain.

2445.q: What does the otter mainly feed on?
2445.e: The otter is a skilful hunter in the water and feeds mainly on fish. It also sometimes eats crayfish, frogs or water birds.

a: No, it always stays on the ground
2446.e: Thanks to strong muscles and sharp claws the lynx climbs trees well. It sometimes uses this to rest or to keep watch.
2446.m: The lynx is a skilful tree climber.

2447.q: What is the study of coats of arms, featuring animals such as lions, eagles and leopards, called?
2447.e: Heraldry deals with coats of arms. They often show animals, for example the bear on the coat of arms of Bern or the ibex on the coat of arms of the Grisons.
2447.m: Heraldry is the study of coats of arms.

a: Alternating day and night in short periods
Only in the middle of the night
2448.e: The mole does not keep to day and night but switches between short periods of rest and activity. So it is out and about again and again around the clock.
2448.m: Moles take turns resting and working.

2449.q: What do you call animals that might only be saved in zoos or nature reserves because they are almost disappearing in the wild?
2449.e: For critically endangered species, breeding in zoos often helps. Nature reserves also help the animals survive.
2449.m: Zoos and nature reserves help endangered species.

2450.q: How does the eagle owl’s hearing differ from our human hearing?
a: It is much more sensitive and helps it locate prey even in the dark
It is much weaker than our hearing
It only hears very low sounds, not high ones
Its hearing only works during the day
2450.e: The eagle owl’s hearing is very fine and helps it pinpoint prey even in complete darkness. The slightly uneven position of its ear openings helps it hear where sounds come from.
2450.m: Eagle owls hear prey precisely even in the dark.

2451.q: Which bird is often confused with the grey heron?
2451.e: Both birds are large, with long legs and a long neck. But you can tell them apart by how they look in flight and by their colour.
2451.m: White storks and grey herons look similar.

2452.q: What do young common swifts do right after leaving the nest for the very first time?
a: they fly off on their own at once
they return to the nest every evening
their parents keep feeding them in the nest
they first walk around on the ground for a while
2452.e: Unlike many other kinds of bird, young swifts do not return to the nest after their first flight. They have to hunt and fly on their own from the start.
2452.m: After leaving the nest they are independent at once.

2453.q: How good is an elephant’s sense of smell?
a: Very good, better than a dog’s
2453.e: Elephants have an extraordinarily good sense of smell. With their trunk they can smell water and food from a long way off.
2453.m: Elephants have an excellent sense of smell.

2454.q: How do dolphins sometimes herd shoals of fish together?
a: They circle the fish as a team
They build a net of seaweed
They dig a pit in the sand
They call out to the fish
2454.e: Several dolphins swim together in a circle around a shoal of fish. This way they push the fish tightly together and can eat more easily.
2454.m: Dolphins sometimes hunt together in a circle.

2455.q: How do several marmots survive the cold together in their winter burrow?
a: They heat the burrow with fire
They stay far apart from each other
They leave the burrow every day
2455.e: In the winter burrow the family members huddle close together. This way they keep each other warm and save energy.

2456.q: How many toes does a brown bear have on each paw?
2456.e: Like humans, the brown bear has five toes with claws on each paw. They leave easily recognisable tracks in soft ground.
2456.m: Brown bears have five toes per paw.

2457.q: What is one purpose of howling in jackals?
a: Keeping in contact with others and marking territory
2457.e: By howling, jackals keep in contact with each other. It also shows other jackals that an area is taken.
2457.m: Howling connects them and marks territory.

2458.q: Some orca families always stay in the same area of sea. What do they mainly eat there?
2458.e: Some orca families always live in the same area and mainly eat fish there, for example salmon.
2458.m: Some orcas always stay in the same place.

2459.q: What is an adult female horse called?
2459.e: An adult female horse is called a mare. She looks after her foal after it is born.
2459.m: A female horse is called a mare.

2460.q: What do rabbits do with their soft night droppings?
a: They eat them again because they contain important nutrients
They always get rid of them
2460.e: Rabbits eat certain soft droppings a second time to take in important nutrients. This is called caecotrophy.

2461.q: What do hippos do when water becomes scarce where they live?
a: They move to another river or lake
They dig themselves in like a hedgehog in winter
They always stay in the same place, whatever happens
2461.e: If the water in a river becomes too scarce, hippos sometimes move to another river or lake. They cannot survive long without water.

2462.q: Where does the golden eagle prefer to build its eyrie?
a: On rock faces in the mountains
On the ground in the middle of a thick forest
2462.e: Golden eagles usually build their large nests, called eyries, on hard-to-reach rocky ledges in mountain areas. There the eggs and young are well protected from enemies.
2462.m: Eyries are on steep rock faces.

2463.q: How does a common toad usually react when you touch it carefully?
2463.e: Common toads are rather calm animals and rely on their poison rather than biting. Even so, it is best to leave them in peace.
2463.m: Toads usually stay calm and still.

2464.q: What is special about the tawny owl’s eyes?
a: They are very large and can see excellently in twilight
They are tiny and almost blind
They can see colours better than human eyes
They glow in the dark like a lamp
2464.e: The tawny owl’s eyes are very large compared with its head and are especially sensitive to light. This lets it see well even when there is little light.
2464.m: The tawny owl has large, light-sensitive eyes.

2465.q: What is the name of the reddish-brown animal with a ringed tail that climbs trees and eats bamboo?
2465.e: The red panda has reddish-brown fur and a long, ringed tail. It mainly eats bamboo.
2465.m: The red panda is reddish brown.

2466.q: What is the name of a well-known, especially large rabbit breed?
2466.e: The German Giant is a rabbit breed that can become very large and heavy. Some weigh over eight kilograms.
2466.m: The German Giant is a large rabbit.

2467.q: At about what age does the mane slowly start to grow on young male lions?
2467.e: In young male lions the mane only starts to grow slowly from about one year old. Over time it becomes fuller and darker.

2468.q: Why is a penguin’s dark back useful when it swims?
a: Seen from above, it camouflages it from enemies
2468.e: Seen from above, the penguin’s dark back looks like the dark water. This makes it harder for enemies in the air to spot it.
2468.m: A dark back camouflages the penguin from above.

2469.q: What does an orangutan enclosure in a zoo especially need?
2469.e: In the zoo orangutans need ways to climb and swing. Ropes and tall structures match their life in the trees.

2470.q: Which wild animal is our domestic donkey descended from?
2470.e: The domestic donkey was bred from the African wild ass a long time ago. It originally lived in dry areas of Africa.
2470.m: Donkeys come from the African wild ass.

2471.q: What are the see-through young eels that arrive at the coasts called?
2471.e: Young eels are see-through, so they are called glass eels. They reach the coasts of Europe and some swim into the rivers.
2471.m: Glass eels are see-through young eels.

2472.q: Why is it important for goldfish that there are enough plants in the water?
a: They produce oxygen and offer shelter
They are only decoration with no use
2472.e: Water plants produce oxygen and at the same time give fish hiding places and shade. That is why plants belong in a good aquarium or pond.
2472.m: Plants give goldfish oxygen and shelter.

2473.q: What is a group of meerkats that lives together called?
2473.e: Meerkats live in groups that are often called a clan or a mob. A group is usually made up of several family members.

2474.q: What do baby hedgehogs look like straight after birth?
a: They already have hard brown spines
They have no spines and have fur
2474.e: Newborn hedgehogs first have soft white spines so that the birth does not hurt. Only later do the spines become hard and brown.
2474.m: Baby hedgehogs have soft spines at first.

2476.q: What does the adder’s head look like?
a: Clearly set off from the neck, with a marking on top
With yellow half-moons behind the head
2476.e: The head looks somewhat triangular and is set off from the neck. On top there is often an X- or V-shaped marking.
2476.m: Head set off from the neck, marking on top.

2477.q: How can you often tell that a common toad feels threatened?
a: It puffs itself up a little
2477.e: If a common toad feels threatened, it puffs up its body a little. This makes it look bigger and harder to swallow.
2477.m: In danger the toad puffs itself up.

2478.q: How do mute swans move when they are on land?
a: they roll up into a ball
2478.e: On land swans with their webbed feet look rather clumsy and waddle slowly. In the water, however, they are very elegant.

2479.q: How does a young bearded vulture differ in colour from an adult?
2479.e: Young bearded vultures have dark, almost blackish-brown feathers. Only over the years do the head and belly become lighter and get the typical pale colouring.
2479.m: Young birds are darker than adults.

2481.q: What is a goose’s neck like compared with many other birds?
a: It has no neck at all
2481.e: Geese have a strikingly long neck. With it they can keep a good lookout and reach food.

2482.q: Why is the house fly probably called the “house fly”?
a: Because it is often found in homes
Because it lives only in the forest
Because it lives only in caves
2482.e: The house fly is found especially often in houses and flats. That is probably where its name comes from.
2482.m: House flies like living in houses.

2483.q: What can you detect with your tongue?
a: Tastes such as sweet or salty
2483.e: There are tiny taste buds on the tongue. They detect, for example, sweet, sour, salty and bitter.

2484.q: How many legs does an aphid have?
2484.e: Aphids are insects and, like all insects, have six legs. Spiders, on the other hand, have eight.
2484.m: Insects have six legs, aphids too.

2485.q: How does a pair of great crested grebes defend its nest against intruders?
a: With loud calls and aggressive behaviour towards rivals
By leaving the nest at once
2485.e: Rival grebes are often driven off with loud calls and threatening behaviour. This way the parents protect their eggs and their territory.
2485.m: Loud calls defend nest and territory.

2486.q: What is our home planet, where we live, called?
2486.e: The Earth is the third planet from the sun. So far it is the only known planet with life.
2486.m: We live on the planet Earth.

2487.q: How long do young lynx stay with their mother?
2487.e: The young learn hunting and survival from their mother. After around 10 months they become independent.
2487.m: After 10 months they go it alone.

2488.q: What do many common buzzards from northern countries such as Scandinavia do in winter?
a: They migrate south to warmer areas
They stay at the North Pole all year
2488.e: Buzzards from colder northern regions often move south in winter because there is more prey to be found there. So visitors from the north can also turn up in Switzerland.

2489.q: What colour is an Alpine salamander almost always?
2489.e: The Alpine salamander is completely black, without the yellow patches of the fire salamander. This colour also gave it its Latin name, Salamandra atra.

2490.q: What does the beekeeper do to get honey out of the combs?
a: He carefully spins the honey out of the combs
2490.e: With a special extractor the honey is spun out of the combs without destroying them. This way the bees can use the combs again later.
2490.m: The beekeeper spins the honey out.

2492.q: What does a tiger mainly eat?
a: Meat from deer and wild boar
2492.e: Tigers are meat eaters and hunt large animals such as deer and wild boar. They are skilful hunters.

2493.q: Why does a robin often come close to people in the garden?
a: It hopes for worms that have been disturbed
It is looking for water to bathe in
It wants to play with the people
2493.e: When you dig in the garden, worms and insects come to the surface. The robin takes advantage of this and looks for food nearby.

2494.q: What are the cockchafer’s antennae mainly for?
2494.e: The fan-like antennae have lots of sense cells for smells. With them the beetles find food and partners.
2494.m: The antennae are organs of smell.

2495.q: What does it often mean when a dog yawns even though it isn’t tired at all?
a: It can be a sign of stress or of calming things down
It always means it is hungry
It shows that it is about to become aggressive
It has no meaning at all
2495.e: In dogs, yawning can be a so-called calming signal, used to reduce tension or avoid conflict. Behaviour researchers often see such signals in uncertain situations.
2495.m: Yawning can show stress in a dog.

2496.q: About how tall at the shoulder can an adult bull elephant grow?
2496.e: Adult bull elephants are huge and can be up to four metres tall at the shoulder. This makes them taller than almost any other land animal.
2496.m: Elephants are huge at the shoulder.

2497.q: How many points does a snowflake usually have?
2497.e: When water freezes, its molecules arrange themselves into six-sided patterns. That is why snowflakes often look like stars.

2498.q: What water conditions does the lake trout need?
2498.e: The lake trout is a cold-water fish. Warm water contains less oxygen and harms it.
2498.m: Lake trout like cool, clean water.

2499.q: How big are gibbons compared with gorillas?
2499.e: Gibbons usually weigh only a few kilograms, the siamang about ten. Gorillas, on the other hand, are much heavier.

2500.q: About how much does a newborn elephant calf weigh?
2500.e: Elephant calves are already very big at birth. At about 100 kilograms they weigh more than an adult human.
2500.m: A calf weighs about 100 kilograms at birth.

2501.q: What do many children think of the ladybird as?
2501.e: Many children and adults believe that a ladybird on your hand brings good luck. That is why many people are pleased when one visits them.
2501.m: Ladybirds are said to bring luck.

2502.q: Where do salmon swim when they want to lay their eggs?
a: From the sea up the rivers
From the river out into the deep sea
Only back and forth in the sea
2502.e: Salmon grow up in the sea and swim up rivers to spawn, often to where they hatched themselves. Migrating fish like this are called anadromous.

2503.q: Why should guinea pigs never be kept on their own?
a: Because they need the company of other guinea pigs
Because they would get too fat
Because they would get too loud
2503.e: Guinea pigs are very social animals and feel lonely and stressed on their own. In Switzerland it is even against the law to keep them alone.

2504.q: What is a baby koala called?
2504.e: A baby koala is called a joey, just like a baby kangaroo. It first grows in its mother’s pouch.
2504.m: A baby koala is called a joey.

2505.q: Which family do jackals belong to?
2505.e: Jackals are carnivores and belong to the dog family. This makes them more closely related to wolves and pet dogs than to cats.

2506.q: What do elephants do with their trunks to greet each other?
2506.e: When elephants that are friends meet, they often twist their trunks together. This is their way of greeting each other happily.
2506.m: Elephants greet each other with their trunks.

2507.q: About how long does an adult Alpine marmot grow, not counting the tail?
2507.e: The body of an adult marmot measures around 50 to 60 centimetres without the tail, plus a bushy tail of about 15 centimetres. This makes it one of the largest squirrels in Europe.
2507.m: Marmots are large, sturdy members of the squirrel family.

2508.q: What often grows on the honeydew left by aphids on leaves?
2508.e: Dark fungi settle on the sticky honeydew. The leaves then look as if they were covered in soot.
2508.m: Black sooty mould grows on honeydew.

2509.q: What do reindeer bulls mainly use their antlers for?
a: For fights over rank and females
2509.e: In the rutting season bulls fight with their antlers over females. Antlers also play a part in the ranking within the herd. Reindeer scrape food free with their hooves, however.
2509.m: Antlers are for fights and ranking.

2510.q: What do you call it when a harmless animal copies the appearance of a dangerous animal to scare off enemies?
2510.e: In mimicry a harmless species copies the appearance of a dangerous species. One example is the hoverfly, which looks like a wasp.

2511.q: How big can a blue whale’s mouth be?
a: Huge, many tonnes of water fit inside
It has no mouth at all
2511.e: The blue whale’s mouth is so huge that a great deal of water with krill fits into it at once. Then it pushes the water out again.

2513.q: Why should you check the seller and reviews before buying online?
a: So you do not fall for dodgy shops or scams
Because online shops otherwise automatically get more expensive
Because otherwise you will not get a bill
2513.e: On the internet there are also dishonest sellers who take your money without delivering the goods. Reviews and checking whether a shop is trustworthy help you avoid scams.

2514.q: What do pigs like to eat most?
a: They eat almost anything, plants and animals
2514.e: Pigs are omnivores and like, for example, roots, fruit, worms and grain. This varied diet helps them grow quickly.

2515.q: What is special about the earwig’s wings?
a: The large back wings are folded under short front wings
It has no wings at all
Its wings are see-through and always spread out
2515.e: The front wings are short and tough. Underneath them the large back wings lie cleverly folded up.
2515.m: Large wings lie folded under short wing covers.

2516.q: Which group of animals does the ring-tailed lemur belong to?
2516.e: The ring-tailed lemur is a primate and so belongs to the same order as monkeys, apes and humans. Within the primates it is one of the lemurs.
2516.m: The ring-tailed lemur is a primate.

2517.q: What is the shared money that many countries of the European Union use called?
2517.e: Many, but not all, EU countries pay with the euro. Switzerland still has its own currency, the franc.
2517.m: Many EU countries pay with the euro.

2518.q: Whose horns are much bigger in the Alpine ibex?
a: Both sexes have horns of the same size
None of the animals has horns
2518.e: Male ibex have much bigger, sabre-like curved horns than the females. Their horns can grow up to a metre long.
2518.m: The males’ horns are much longer.

2519.q: What does a dog often do when it is very happy?
a: It lies flat and goes to sleep
2519.e: Tail wagging is a typical sign of happiness in dogs. But the tail can also show other moods.
2519.m: A dog shows happiness by wagging its tail.

2520.q: How many young does a female marten usually have in a litter?
2520.e: A female marten usually has three to five young. They are born blind and helpless and at first stay in the safety of the den.

2521.q: How do African wild dogs usually hunt?
a: Together in a pack, with a long chase
With traps made of earth and branches
2521.e: The packs chase their prey for a long time and share the work. This way they can bring down larger animals too.
2521.m: Teamwork and stamina lead to success.

2522.q: How does the Alpine newt’s skin on land differ from its skin in water?
a: On land it is drier and less shiny
In water it has scales like a fish
2522.e: On land the Alpine newt’s skin becomes drier and somewhat duller, while in water it looks smoother and shinier. This is linked to how it lives in each place.
2522.m: On land the skin looks drier.

2523.q: Where does the ladybird larva attach itself when it turns into a pupa?
a: To a stone in a river
2523.e: The larva finds a leaf or stem, holds on to it and turns into a pupa. This keeps it well protected from enemies.
2523.m: The pupa hangs firmly on a leaf.

2524.q: What are a puppy’s first teeth, which later fall out, called?
2524.e: Puppies first get small milk teeth, which later fall out. Then the bigger, permanent teeth grow in.
2524.m: First come the small milk teeth.

a: No, but it can feel vibrations
Yes, it has very good ears
2525.e: The Roman snail has no ears for hearing. But it can sense shaking and vibrations in the ground.

2526.q: Apart from in trees, where else does a squirrel look for food?
2526.e: Squirrels look for nuts, seeds and mushrooms not only in the treetops but also on the forest floor.
2526.m: Food is also searched for on the ground.

2527.q: What is the male lion’s main job in the pride?
2527.e: The male lion defends the pride and the area against strange lions. He is bigger and stronger than the lionesses.
2527.m: The male lion protects the pride.

2529.q: What do many pairs of sparrows often do for their whole lives?
2529.e: Sparrows often form pairs that stay together for a long time, sometimes even for their whole lives. Together they also look after their chicks.
2529.m: Sparrow pairs often stay together for a long time.

2530.q: How is the heart muscle different from skeletal muscle?
a: It works tirelessly without you consciously controlling it
It is the only muscle without a blood supply
It can be moved at will like an arm
2530.e: The heart muscle beats automatically, for a whole lifetime without a break. Skeletal muscles, on the other hand, you control consciously.
2530.m: Your heart works tirelessly by itself.

2531.q: Why is it best to breathe through your nose rather than your mouth?
a: The nose cleans and warms the air
The nose makes the air colder
The nose makes the air drier
You cannot smell anything through your nose
2531.e: In the nose the air is cleaned, warmed and moistened. That way cleaner air gets into the lungs.
2531.m: Your nose cleans the air you breathe.

2532.q: Which group of animals does the alpaca belong to?
2532.e: Alpacas have fur, give birth to live young and feed them with milk. That makes them mammals.

2533.q: How do many kinds of aphid survive the winter?
2533.e: In autumn, males and females develop and mate. The females lay eggs, which survive the winter on plants.
2533.m: Many aphids spend the winter as eggs.

2534.q: About how long does a nanny goat carry her kid before it is born?
2534.e: A goat’s pregnancy lasts about 150 days, which is almost five months. Then the kid is born.
2534.m: A goat kid takes five months.

2535.q: What do hens sometimes do when their chicks are in danger?
2535.e: A hen bravely defends her chicks against enemies. She puffs herself up and tries to drive the enemy away.

2536.q: Which small fin between the back and the tail is typical of salmon-like fish such as the lake trout?
2536.e: The adipose fin is a small, fleshy flap of skin without supporting rays. It sits at the back on top of the fish.
2536.m: The adipose fin is a feature of salmon-like fish.

2537.q: Is the great spotted woodpecker the most common woodpecker in Europe?
a: it is only found in Asia
2537.e: Of all the woodpeckers in Europe, the great spotted woodpecker is the one you see most often. It is found in almost every wood.
2537.m: It is Europe’s most common woodpecker.

2538.q: What does the grass snake do in winter?
a: It goes into a winter torpor in a hiding place
It hunts actively in the snow
It builds a nest of twigs
2538.e: As a cold-blooded animal it becomes stiff and still in the cold. It spends the winter in holes in the ground or under piles of stones.
2538.m: In winter the grass snake rests, stiff and still.

2539.q: At what time of day is the red deer most active?
a: At dawn and dusk, morning and evening
In the middle of the night at full moon
Only at midday in blazing sun
2539.e: Red deer are mainly out and about at dawn and dusk. During the day they often rest hidden in the forest.
2539.m: Red deer are active at dawn and dusk.

2540.q: What helps great tits find enough food in winter?
2540.e: In winter there are hardly any insects. Bird tables and fat balls with seeds and fat help great tits through the cold season.
2540.m: In winter feeding places help tits.

2541.q: What do you call a badger family that lives together in a sett?
2541.e: Several badgers can live together in one sett. This is called a badger clan. Even so, they usually look for food alone.
2541.m: Badgers sometimes live in a clan.

2542.q: Which people in northern Europe traditionally keep herds of reindeer?
2542.e: The Sámi live in the north of Scandinavia and Finland. Reindeer herding has been important to many of them for a long time.

2543.q: What happens when an Alpine salamander is in danger and is grabbed by an animal?
a: Its poisonous skin secretion can scare off the attacker
It loses its tail like a lizard
It can make itself invisible at once
It changes its colour to red
2543.e: Unlike some lizards, the Alpine salamander cannot simply drop its tail. Instead it uses its skin poison against attackers.
2543.m: Poison, not losing its tail, protects it.

2544.q: What does it mean that the African buffalo is a ruminant?
a: It brings food back up into its mouth and chews it again
It eats only once a month
It never chews but swallows everything whole
2544.e: Ruminants have a stomach with several parts. The food is brought back up and chewed again so that the tough grass can be digested better.

2545.q: Apart from seals, which animals are sometimes also food for the polar bear?
2545.e: If there are no seals to be found, the polar bear also eats fish, birds or their eggs. This helps it get through difficult times.
2545.m: Sometimes the polar bear eats fish or birds.

2546.q: What do young eagle owls do before they can fly properly?
a: They leave the nest on foot and climb about as so-called branchers
They lie still in the nest until their first flight
Their parents carry them to a second nest
2546.e: Young eagle owls often leave the nest before their first flight and climb about nearby as so-called branchers. Only after a few weeks can they fly properly.
2546.m: Young eagle owls climb about as branchers.

2547.e: Almost all jellyfish live in the salty sea. Only a very few small species live in fresh water, even in some Swiss lakes.
2547.m: Jellyfish mostly live in the sea.

2548.q: Apart from warmth, what is especially important for the sand lizard in its habitat?
a: Places to hide such as piles of stones or thick plants
2548.e: Hiding places protect it from predators and give shelter in bad weather. Without such features the lizard can hardly find a suitable habitat.
2548.m: Hiding places are vital for its survival.

2549.q: What role did the edible dormouse play in ancient Rome?
a: it was a delicacy and was bred
it was a sacred animal of the gods
it was kept as a pet
it was used as a guard
2549.e: The ancient Romans kept edible dormice in special containers and fattened them up to eat as a delicacy. This tradition is well documented in history.
2549.m: Romans ate dormice as a delicacy.

2550.q: Which bird is often one of the first to sing early in the morning in Switzerland?
2550.e: The blackbird is one of the birds that start singing first, very early in the morning. This is also called the dawn chorus.
2550.m: Blackbirds sing early in the morning.

2551.q: How long can a giraffe’s neck grow?
a: Just as long as a cat’s
2551.e: A giraffe’s neck can grow up to two metres long. Even so, it has the same number of neck bones as a human.
2551.m: A giraffe’s neck grows up to two metres long.

2552.q: What is the shed skin of a snake called?
2552.e: The slough is often left behind in the bushes. It is thin and see-through.
2552.m: A snake’s shed skin is called a slough.

2553.q: What is unusual for an insect about the common earwig?
a: The mother also looks after the young larvae
2553.e: Most insects do not look after their young. With the earwig, the mother stays with the young for a while and cares for them.
2553.m: Earwig mothers care for their young.

2554.q: About how many light-sensing spots for seeing does a starfish have?
a: One at the tip of each arm, so usually five
A hundred eyes on its belly
2554.e: At the tip of each arm the starfish has a small light-sensing spot. With five arms that usually makes five such spots.
2554.m: Each arm tip has a light-sensing spot.

2555.q: How do the authorities in Switzerland often react when beavers cause damage to fields?
a: They try to find a balance with measures such as fences
Beavers are killed everywhere at once
Beavers may eat everything without limits
2555.e: Because the beaver is protected, the authorities rely on solutions such as protective fences or special strips along the banks to reduce conflicts with farming. This way people and beavers should be able to live side by side.

2556.q: Apart from sounds, how do bonobos communicate?
2556.e: Bonobos use many gestures and facial expressions. With them they show moods and wishes.
2556.m: Bonobos talk with gestures and faces.

2557.q: How many broods can a great tit raise in one year?
2557.e: A great tit usually raises one to two broods a year. The second brood often happens in summer.
2557.m: Great tits often breed twice a year.

2558.q: Which teeth does a cow lack at the top front of its mouth?
a: All the teeth in its mouth
2558.e: Cows have incisors only at the bottom at the front. At the top they have a hard pad. They use it to tear off grass.
2558.m: Cows have incisors only at the bottom.

2559.q: What were donkeys especially often used for in the past?
a: As pack animals for carrying heavy sacks
2559.e: Donkeys are strong and have lots of stamina, so in the past they carried heavy loads over long distances. They also helped plough the fields.
2559.m: Donkeys used to carry heavy loads.

2560.q: What kind of water does a trout prefer?
2560.e: Trout feel most at home in cool, clear, flowing water. In warm, still water they get too little oxygen.

2561.q: About how long can an otter live in the wild?
2561.e: In the wild otters usually live only a few years. In human care they can live much longer.

2562.q: What special feature does the reindeer’s body have against the cold?
a: Its legs and ears are rather small and well insulated
2562.e: Small ears and short limbs lose less heat. The thick coat also helps.

2563.q: The European tree frog’s German name, “Laubfrosch”, means “leaf frog”. Why?
a: It likes to sit among the leaves of bushes and trees
It only spends the winter in autumn leaves
It is brown like dry leaves
2563.e: With the sticky pads on its toes the tree frog climbs into bushes and trees and sits there well camouflaged among the leaves. Its scientific name, Hyla arborea, also points to trees.
2563.m: The tree frog lives among the leaves of bushes and trees.

2564.q: What does growing antler feel like before it hardens?
a: Soft and covered with skin, called velvet
2564.e: A new antler is soft at first and covered with a hairy skin. This skin is called velvet.
2564.m: Young antler is soft and covered with velvet.

2565.q: What is a young ibex called?
2565.e: The young of the ibex is called a kid, just like with other goats. In Swiss German dialect it is also called Gitzi.

2566.e: Woodlice are mainly active at night. It is cooler and damper then.
2566.m: Woodlice are mostly active at night.

2568.q: How does a leopard usually kill its prey?
a: With a powerful bite to the throat or neck
2568.e: The leopard grabs its prey with its powerful canine teeth. It often kills smaller animals with a bite to the neck.
2568.m: Leopards kill with a powerful bite.

2570.q: How many legs does a dog have?
2570.e: Dogs are mammals and, like most of them, walk on four legs. This lets them run and jump fast.

2571.q: Which famous trade route used caravans of Bactrian camels?
2571.e: Goods were transported on the Silk Road between China and Europe. Bactrian camels were important pack animals there.
2571.m: On the Silk Road camels carried goods.

2572.q: Which well-known bird from Australia belongs to the kingfisher family?
2572.e: The laughing kookaburra is a large kingfisher from Australia. It is famous for its call, which sounds like loud laughter.
2572.m: The kookaburra is a relative of our kingfisher.

2573.q: When is the badger mainly active?
2573.e: The badger sleeps in its sett during the day and only goes looking for food after dark. So it is nocturnal.
2573.m: The badger is a night animal.

2574.q: What role does the blackbird often play in Swiss gardens?
a: It is one of the best-known garden birds
It is never seen in gardens
It only visits once a century
2574.e: Almost everyone knows the blackbird because it is so common in Swiss gardens. For many people its song is part of everyday life.
2574.m: The blackbird is a well-known garden bird.

2576.q: About how old can an Alpine salamander get in the wild?
2576.e: Alpine salamanders are among the longer-lived amphibians and can live for over ten years. This is also linked to how slowly they reproduce.
2576.m: It can live for over ten years.

a: A white butterfly whose caterpillar likes to eat cabbage
A butterfly that eats only meat
2577.e: The large white, also called the cabbage white, is a widespread white butterfly. Its green caterpillars are often found on cabbage plants in the garden.
2577.m: The large white likes cabbage plants.

2578.q: Which animals especially like eating house flies?
2578.e: Spiders catch flies in their webs, and many birds snap them up in flight. So flies are an important source of food for other animals.

2579.q: At which altitudes is the raven especially common in Switzerland?
a: in the Alps, especially in the mountains
2579.e: In Switzerland the raven is especially widespread in the Alps, where it finds suitable rocks for building its nest and enough food. In recent years, however, it has also been spreading more and more across the Central Plateau.

2580.q: How is the kingfisher doing in Switzerland?
a: It is rare and needs natural riverbanks
It is the most common bird in the country
It is found only in zoos
2580.e: The kingfisher is rare in Switzerland. It needs natural banks with steep sides into which it can dig its nesting hole.
2580.m: The kingfisher is rare and needs natural banks.

2581.q: What are soldiers called who keep the peace on behalf of the UN?
2581.e: Blue Helmets are called that because of their blue helmets. They are sent by the UN to crisis areas to keep the peace.
2581.m: UN soldiers are called Blue Helmets.

2582.q: What does the carp’s dorsal fin look like?
a: Long, with a hard spine at the front
Short and pointed like a shark’s
It has no dorsal fin at all
2582.e: The carp’s dorsal fin is strikingly long. At the front it has a hard spine.
2582.m: The carp’s dorsal fin is long.

2583.q: Which danger particularly threatens the African wild dog?
a: Too many fish in the water
2583.e: People are using more and more land for fields and settlements. This makes the wild dogs' habitat smaller.

2584.q: Can common swifts even sleep while flying?
a: yes, they sleep in flight high up
no, they always have to land to sleep
no, they sleep only on water
yes, but only sitting in trees
2584.e: In the evening swifts rise high into the air and sleep there in short bursts while they keep flying. This way they can go for months without landing.
2584.m: Swifts even sleep high up in flight.

2585.q: What is it called when a gosling thinks the first moving creature it sees after hatching is its mother?
2585.e: This behaviour is called imprinting. Newly hatched goslings follow the first larger creature they see as if it were their real mother.
2585.m: Goslings imprint early on a carer.

2586.q: What are a sea turtle’s large front flippers especially important for?
2586.e: With its strong front flippers the turtle beats through the water and moves forward. The smaller back flippers are used more for steering.

2587.q: What were heavy draught horses especially needed for in the past?
2587.e: Draught horses are strong, large horses that used to pull heavy loads and help in the fields. Today machines often do this work.
2587.m: Draught horses used to pull heavy loads.

2588.q: What happens when you pull hard on a rubber band?
a: It stretches and then pulls back together
2588.e: A rubber band is elastic: when you pull it, it gets longer, and when you let go, it pulls back together. This restoring force is called elastic force.
2588.m: Elastic things stretch and spring back.

2589.q: What colour is the fur of most orangutans?
2589.e: The long fur of orangutans is reddish to orange-brown. You can recognise them by it straight away.

2590.q: What does the bonobo lack, like all great apes?
2590.e: Great apes have no tail. This sets them apart from many other monkeys, for example macaques.

2591.q: Where does the mute swan most like to live?
2591.e: Mute swans need calm water to swim and feed. That is why they feel especially at home on lakes and ponds.

2592.q: Which popular Swiss food is made from cow’s milk?
2592.e: In Switzerland a lot of cheese is made from cow’s milk, for example Emmental or Gruyère. Switzerland is famous for its many kinds of cheese.
2592.m: Cheese is made from cow’s milk.

2593.q: What does the slow worm do with its tongue?
a: It flicks it to pick up smells
It catches flies in flight with it
2593.e: It picks up scents with its tongue. This is how it finds prey and others of its kind.

2594.q: How does the polar bear find seals’ holes in the ice?
a: With its fine sense of smell
Only with its eyes at night
2594.e: With its very fine nose the polar bear can smell seals’ breathing holes in the ice. That way it knows where to wait.
2594.m: Its nose shows the polar bear the seal holes.

2595.q: What is a fuse in a circuit for?
a: It breaks the circuit when too much current flows
2595.e: If too much current flows through a wire, it can get very hot and start a fire. The fuse then melts or switches off and breaks the circuit in time.
2595.m: Fuses protect against too much current.

2596.q: What does a praying mantis’s head look like from the front?
a: Round like a ball with no eyes
2596.e: The head looks like a triangle. The large eyes are at the sides.
2596.m: A triangular head with large eyes.

2597.q: Why is the grasshopper often green or brown?
a: So that it can hide in the grass
So that other animals find it prettier
So that it can fly faster
2597.e: This colouring is called camouflage. It means birds do not spot the grasshopper so easily.

2598.q: About how many bearded vultures are thought to live in the whole Alpine region again today?
2598.e: Thanks to reintroduction there are now several hundred bearded vultures in the Alps again. The population is slowly growing.
2598.m: Several hundred fly over the Alps again.

2599.q: Which animals like to hunt young trout?
2599.e: Birds such as the grey heron or the kingfisher like to catch small trout from the water. Larger fish can also be dangerous to young trout.
2599.m: Herons and kingfishers hunt young trout.

a: Yes, it can swim if it needs to
No, water is deadly for it
Yes, it even lives mostly in water
2600.e: When necessary, for example when escaping, it can swim. But its real habitat is dry land, not water.
2600.m: It can swim, but lives on land.

2601.q: Which animals are among the natural enemies of the edible dormouse?
2601.e: Owls and martens like to hunt the edible dormouse, as it is a small, light prey animal. Pet cats can also be dangerous to it.

a: A country’s representation in another country
2602.e: An embassy is a building where people from one country work in another country. They help their own citizens abroad, for example.
2602.m: An embassy represents a country abroad.

2603.q: Which animals suffered especially from the poison DDT in the middle of the 20th century?
a: The peregrine falcon and other birds of prey
2603.e: The insect poison DDT built up in the food chain and especially harmed birds of prey such as the peregrine falcon. Their eggshells became thin and broke, and many populations fell sharply.
2603.m: DDT was a serious threat to the peregrine falcon.

2604.q: Which statement about the pond skater’s body is true?
a: It is round like a ball
It is soft like a snail
It has a shell like a mussel
2604.e: The slim body spreads the weight well. Long legs also spread the load over a large area.
2604.m: Slim body, long legs, weight well spread.

2605.q: Which other bird can you roughly compare the size of a common buzzard with?
2605.e: A common buzzard is about the size of a large crow but has much broader wings. This makes it look much bulkier in flight.
2605.m: About the size of a crow with broad wings.

2607.q: What do kingfisher parents feed their young in the nest?
2607.e: All day long the parents bring small fish to the young in the nest chamber. This way the chicks grow quickly.
2607.m: Parents feed the young small fish.

2608.q: What does a dog do when it is very hot?
a: It pants with its mouth open
It lies down in the sun
2608.e: Dogs can hardly sweat, so they pant with their mouths open to cool down. They breathe in and out quickly as they do so.

2609.q: What does the tawny owl grab its prey with?
2609.e: Like all owls, the tawny owl grabs its prey with strong, sharp claws called talons. The beak is used more for tearing the prey apart.
2609.m: The tawny owl catches prey with sharp talons.

2610.q: What kind of water does a seahorse need in an aquarium?
2610.e: Seahorses live in the sea. That is why they need clean salt water at the right temperature in an aquarium.

2611.q: Which group of fish does the brown trout belong to?
2611.e: Predatory fish eat other animals. The brown trout hunts insect larvae, crayfish and small fish.
2611.m: The brown trout is a predatory fish.

2612.q: The German name for the least weasel is “Mauswiesel”, meaning “mouse weasel”. Where does the name probably come from?
a: Because it squeaks like a mouse
Because it is born in mouse holes
2612.e: The name points directly to its favourite prey. The least weasel is one of the most effective mouse hunters of all.
2612.m: The least weasel, the mouse hunter.

2613.q: Why is the earthworm a popular bait for fishing?
a: Because it moves and attracts fish
2613.e: The worm’s movements on the hook catch the fish’s attention. That is why anglers often use it as bait.

2614.q: Which sense helps aphids find suitable plants?
a: Smell and touch with their antennae
2614.e: With their antennae aphids sense scents and touch. This is how they recognise suitable plants.

2615.q: What is a large group of jellyfish in the sea called?
2615.e: When very many jellyfish swim together in the sea, it is called a swarm of jellyfish. This can happen on some coasts.

2616.q: At what altitude in the mountains does the Alpine ibex most like to live?
a: In steep rocky areas above the tree line
Deep in the forest in the valley
Only on flat meadows in the Central Plateau
2616.e: Ibex prefer steep, rocky ground above the tree line, often between 2000 and 3200 metres. There they are well protected from enemies.
2616.m: Ibex love steep rocks high up.

2617.q: Which bird often hunts young penguins or their eggs on land?
2617.e: Skuas are skilful raiders that can steal unguarded penguin eggs or small chicks. That is why penguin parents guard their young closely.
2617.m: Skuas threaten penguin eggs and chicks.

2618.q: What does the koala’s nose look like?
2618.e: The koala has a big, black, leathery nose. It looks almost like a leather button on its face.
2618.m: Koalas have a big, leathery nose.

2619.q: After how many weeks do young common buzzards first leave the nest?
2619.e: Young buzzards stay in the nest for around six to seven weeks before they fly for the first time. After that the parents still look after them for a while.
2619.m: The young fly after seven weeks.

2620.q: What does the ibex do when there is deep snow in winter?
a: It moves to lower, sunny slopes with less snow
It digs deep caves in the rock
It travels to warm countries like a migratory bird
2620.e: When there is a lot of snow, ibex move to lower, sunlit slopes where there is less snow and food can still be found. They do not hibernate.
2620.m: In winter they look for sunny slopes with little snow.

2621.q: What colours is a giant panda’s fur?
2621.e: Pandas have striking black and white fur. That is how you recognise them straight away.
2621.m: Panda fur is black and white.

2622.q: In a group of meerkats, who usually has the young?
a: A dominant female and a dominant male
All the animals at the same time
2622.e: Usually only the dominant pair has young. The other animals help to raise them.
2622.m: Usually only the leading pair has young.

2623.q: Which animal is the largest land mammal still living in the wild in Europe?
2623.e: The European bison, also called the wisent, was almost extinct and was saved by special breeding programmes. Today it lives in selected protected areas.
2623.m: The European bison is Europe's largest land mammal.

2624.q: Which danger especially threatens the Alpine salamander today?
a: The loss of its natural habitat
Too much rain in the desert
2624.e: Because of building projects, roads and changes in how land is used, the Alpine salamander is losing parts of its habitat. Climate change also harms it.
2624.m: Habitat loss threatens the Alpine salamander.

2625.q: About how many lynx live in the whole of Switzerland?
2625.e: Swiss lynx numbers are small but have grown since they were reintroduced. Today a few hundred lynx live in the Jura and the Alps.
2625.m: A few hundred lynx live in Switzerland.

2626.q: What does a sparrow do straight away when there is danger?
2626.e: Sparrows are very alert and all fly up together at the slightest danger. This way the whole group protects itself.
2626.m: Sparrows flee at once when in danger.

2627.q: What is the Great Red Spot on Jupiter?
a: A huge storm that is centuries old
2627.e: The Great Red Spot is an enormous storm in Jupiter’s atmosphere that is bigger than the Earth. It has been observed for centuries.
2627.m: The Great Red Spot is a gigantic storm on Jupiter.

2628.q: What does a bumblebee’s fur feel like?
2628.e: Bumblebees have a thick, soft coat of lots of tiny hairs. This coat keeps them warm even in cool weather.
2628.m: Bumblebee fur is soft and thick.

2629.q: What sound does a duck typically make?
2629.e: Quacking is the typical sound of a duck. Females especially quack very loudly.

2630.q: Where does the robin most like to hide its nest?
a: In thick undergrowth close to the ground
At the very top of tall trees
In the middle of a meadow
2630.e: The nest is well hidden in thick undergrowth close to the ground, often under bushes or ivy. This way enemies do not find it so easily.
2630.m: The nest is hidden in the undergrowth.

2631.q: What shape are a leopard's pupils?
2631.e: Big cats like the leopard have round pupils. Small cats like the house cat often have slit-shaped pupils.

a: So that fish can get past obstacles in a river
So that anglers can reach the bank more easily
So that the water gets warmer
2632.e: A fish ladder is made of several small pools arranged like steps. The fish jump or swim upwards from pool to pool.
2632.m: Fish ladders help fish past obstacles.

2633.q: What is a big danger for wild chimpanzees?
2633.e: When forests are cut down, chimpanzees lose their home. That makes it very hard for them to survive.

2634.q: What do researchers look at to tell individual wild dogs apart?
2634.e: Because each animal has its own pattern of patches, individual wild dogs can be recognised in photos. This lets researchers observe packs.
2634.m: The coat pattern gives away each individual animal.

2635.q: What colour is the skin of an edible frog usually?
2635.e: Edible frogs are usually green with dark, irregular spots. Often there is a lighter stripe down the back.
2635.m: The edible frog is green with dark spots.

2636.q: Can some starfish have more than five arms?
a: Yes, some species have more arms
2636.e: Not all starfish have five arms. Some species have ten, twenty or even more arms.
2636.m: Some species have more than five arms.

2637.q: What colour is a yellow eel’s back usually?
2637.e: The back is dark and the belly yellowish. This camouflages the eel well on the bottom of rivers and lakes.
2637.m: Yellow eels are dark with a yellow belly.

2639.q: Why is washing your hands important?
a: It removes germs and protects against illness
2639.e: Washing your hands with soap rinses away lots of bacteria and viruses. That way you get ill less often.

2640.q: What else is the cross spider called?
2640.e: Because it is found so often in gardens, the cross spider is also called the European garden spider. It likes living among plants.
2640.m: It is also called the European garden spider.

2641.q: Why are an alpaca’s padded feet better for pastures than hooves?
a: They are gentle on the soil and the turf
They fertilise the ground with salt
2641.e: The soft soles press the ground together less than hooves do. This keeps the meadow in better condition.
2641.m: Soft soles are gentle on the pasture.

2642.q: Which sense organ does the rattlesnake use to find warm-blooded prey in the dark?
2642.e: Rattlesnakes have small pits between the eye and the nose that sense heat. This lets them find their prey even in complete darkness.
2642.m: Pit organs sense heat in the dark.

2643.q: Do goats really eat tin cans?
a: No, they only nibble them out of curiosity
2643.e: Goats explore almost everything with their mouths because they are very curious. But they do not eat tin cans.

2644.q: How does a camel move when it lies down?
a: It bends its front legs first
It tips over onto its side
2644.e: Camels kneel down first and then lie down. For this they have calluses on their chest and knees.

2646.q: What danger can fish that have been released into a pond pose to edible frog spawn and tadpoles?
a: They bring the frogs extra food
They clean algae out of the water for the frogs
2646.e: Fish put into ponds often eat frogspawn and tadpoles. This can make it very hard for edible frogs to breed in that pond.
2646.m: Fish can eat spawn and tadpoles.

2648.q: Which animal is one of the snow leopard’s important prey?
2648.e: The snow leopard mainly hunts hoofed animals of the mountains, for example blue sheep and Siberian ibex. It also eats marmots and hares.
2648.m: It hunts wild sheep and ibex.

2649.q: How do dolphins find their prey in dark water?
a: With clicking sounds that bounce back
With their eyes in the dark
2649.e: Dolphins send out clicking sounds. When these hit a fish, an echo comes back and the dolphin knows where its prey is.
2649.m: Dolphins locate things with clicks and echoes.

2650.q: In a famous old fable, a grasshopper sings all summer instead of working. Who busily gathers food instead?
2650.e: In the fable the grasshopper prefers to sing instead of preparing for winter. The ant, on the other hand, busily gathers food.
2650.m: The ant gathers, the grasshopper sings.

2651.q: About how long is the body of an adult least weasel?
2651.e: Least weasels are very small and slim. Males grow a little bigger than females.
2651.m: Least weasels are only about the length of a hand.

2652.q: Why don’t you see barn swallows in Switzerland in winter?
a: They fly to Africa because there are no flying insects here
They turn white and invisible in winter
2652.e: In winter there are hardly any flying insects here. That is why barn swallows migrate to Africa south of the Sahara and come back in spring.
2652.m: With no insects in winter, the swallow goes to Africa.

2653.q: About how old can a koala get in the wild?
2653.e: Koalas can live to about 13 to 18 years in the wild. Females often live a little longer than males.
2653.m: Koalas often live for over ten years.

2654.q: What is the name of the famous medieval story character, a cunning fox with his own name?
2654.e: Reynard the Fox is a famous character from old European animal stories. He stands for an especially clever and cunning fox.
2654.m: Reynard the Fox is a cunning hero.

2655.q: Which family of animals does the chamois belong to?
2655.e: The chamois belongs to the bovid family and, within it, to the goat-like animals. Its scientific name is Rupicapra rupicapra.

2656.q: Is the hippo dangerous to people in Africa?
a: Yes, it can be very dangerous
No, it always runs away at once
2656.e: Although it eats only plants, the hippo is one of the most dangerous animals in Africa. It defends its territory fiercely and can attack quickly.
2656.m: Hippos are dangerous even though they eat plants.

2657.q: On which continent do most dromedaries live today?
2657.e: Most dromedaries are kept in north-east Africa. There are also many in Arabia.

2658.q: What colour is a red squirrel’s fur often?
2658.e: Most squirrels in Switzerland have reddish-brown fur. Some, however, are a little darker or lighter.

2659.q: About how big does an adult badger get?
a: About as big as a medium-sized dog
2659.e: An adult badger measures about 70 to 90 centimetres including the tail. That is roughly the size of a medium-sized dog.
2659.m: Badgers are about the size of a dog.

2660.q: What are a cow’s hooves called, because they are split into two parts?
2660.e: The split hooves of a cow are called cloven hooves. That is why the cow belongs to the cloven-hoofed animals.

2661.q: What does a goldfish absolutely need to be well?
a: A big enough aquarium or a pond
2661.e: Goldfish need lots of space to swim, otherwise they stay small and get ill. A small bowl is not enough.

2662.q: Who rules an ant colony and lays almost all the eggs?
2662.e: An ant colony usually has one queen, who lays eggs all day long. The workers look after food, the nest and the young.
2662.m: The queen lays almost all the eggs in the colony.

2663.q: How many pups does a female wolf usually have in a litter?
2663.e: A female wolf usually has between 4 and 6 pups in a litter. However, not all of them survive their first year.
2663.m: Female wolves usually have 4 to 6 pups.

2664.q: How does the great spotted woodpecker move up a tree trunk?
a: hopping upwards, using its tail as a prop
not at all, it just sits still
2664.e: The great spotted woodpecker skilfully hops upwards with both feet at the same time. It supports itself with its stiff tail.

2665.q: On 6 December many children celebrate the day of a holy man. What is his name?
2665.e: Saint Nicholas was a bishop who was especially kind to poor people. On his day he often brings children small presents.
2665.m: Saint Nicholas brings presents on 6 December.

2666.q: What do people in Switzerland do to help kestrels breed?
a: They put up special nest boxes on barns and buildings
They build swimming pools for them
They put out sugar water for them
2666.e: Because kestrels do not build nests themselves, special nest boxes are often fixed to barns, towers or masts. This makes it easier for them to find a suitable place to breed.

2667.q: What do young foxes like doing to practise hunting?
a: Playing and play-fighting with each other
2667.e: Fox cubs love to tussle and play with each other outside the den. Along the way they practise important movements for hunting later.
2667.m: Play is practice for hunting later.

2668.q: What does the squirrel do with nuts and seeds in autumn?
a: It hides them as a winter store
It eats them all straight away
It sells them to other animals
It builds its nest out of them
2668.e: The squirrel buries nuts in many places and finds some of them again in winter. Some forgotten nuts grow into new trees.
2668.m: Squirrels store food for the winter.

2669.q: What does it mean when lions eat together and growl?
a: They show who owns which part of the prey
They are just playing for fun
2669.e: When eating together, lions sometimes growl to defend their place at the prey. This settles who gets how much.
2669.m: Growling settles the ranking while eating.

2670.q: What are a penguin’s young called?
2670.e: Young penguins are called chicks, just like the young of many other birds. At first they have fluffy grey feathers.

2671.q: How many eggs does a female cuckoo usually lay in another bird’s nest?
2671.e: The female cuckoo usually lays only one egg in each other bird’s nest. She spreads her other eggs over many different nests.
2671.m: One cuckoo egg per strange nest.

2672.q: Which animals are among the natural predators of the carrion crow?
a: larger birds of prey such as the goshawk
2672.e: Larger birds of prey such as the goshawk can be dangerous to adult carrion crows. Young birds and eggs are also at risk from other nest raiders.

2673.q: In which habitat does the stag beetle feel especially at home?
2673.e: It needs broadleaf woods with old oaks and lots of dead wood. There it finds food and places for its larvae.
2673.m: Stag beetles love old oak woods with lots of dead wood.

2674.q: Why is the green sea turtle called “green”?
a: Because of its greenish body fat
2674.e: The name comes from the greenish fat in the turtle’s body, not from the colour of its shell. In the past it was even made into soup, which gave it its German name “Suppenschildkröte”, meaning soup turtle.

2675.q: Where does the earwig most like to hide during the day?
a: In dark cracks under stones or bark
Out in the open on a sunny meadow
2675.e: Its flat body fits well into narrow cracks. There it is protected from enemies and from drying out.
2675.m: During the day it hides in narrow cracks.

2676.q: When did the okapi become known in Europe?
a: Already in the time of the ancient Romans
2676.e: The shy okapi lives hidden in the rainforest of the Congo. Only around 1900 did skins reach Europe and the animal was scientifically described.
2676.m: The okapi only became known in Europe around 1900.

2677.q: How can researchers often tell individual pandas apart?
a: By the pattern of their black patches
By the smell of their bamboo
By the size of their ears alone
By the sound of their footsteps
2677.e: Every panda has a slightly different pattern of black patches. This lets researchers recognise individual animals.
2677.m: Patch patterns help tell pandas apart.

2678.q: What happens when a cow is milked?
a: Milk is taken from its udder
2678.e: When milking, the milk is taken from the cow’s udder, either by hand or with a milking machine. This milk is then sold.
2678.m: Milking takes the milk from the udder.

2679.q: What is the pale grey patch behind an orca’s dorsal fin?
2679.e: Every orca has a pale saddle patch behind its dorsal fin. It looks a little different on each animal.
2679.m: The saddle patch is behind the fin.

2681.q: Which animals are among the blackbird’s enemies?
2681.e: Cats and birds of prey such as the sparrowhawk are dangerous enemies of the blackbird. Young birds are especially at risk.

2682.q: What does the anthill use the warmth of the sun for?
a: To keep the inside of the nest warm
2682.e: The dark surface of the mound absorbs the sun’s warmth. This warmth helps keep the inside of the nest warm.
2682.m: The mound stores the sun’s warmth.

2683.q: What does it usually mean when a budgie dozes calmly on one leg?
2683.e: A relaxed budgie often stands calmly on one leg and dozes. This shows that it feels safe and comfortable.

2684.q: How can you often tell Asian elephants from African elephants straight away?
2684.e: The ears of the Asian elephant are much smaller than those of the African elephant. This is an easy way to tell them apart.

2685.q: What is a mistaken belief about spotted hyenas?
2685.e: Spotted hyenas often hunt for themselves and catch a large part of their food actively. They only eat carrion on top of that.
2685.m: Spotted hyenas are also successful hunters.

2686.q: What is a proposal in a vote?
2686.e: A proposal is the issue that voters can say Yes or No to, for example a new law.
2686.m: A proposal is the subject of a vote.

2687.q: How are whitefish often prepared in the kitchen?
a: Only raw with the scales on
2687.e: Whitefish fillets, called Felchen in Switzerland, are often fried in a pan. Smoked whitefish is also popular.
2687.m: Whitefish fillets are fried or smoked.

2688.q: What are the African buffalo’s horns for?
2688.e: Buffalo use their horns to defend themselves against enemies. Bulls also use them to test their strength.
2688.m: Horns are for defence and testing strength.

2689.q: What is known about donkeys’ memory?
a: Donkeys have a very good memory
