2689.e: Donkeys remember routes and familiar people for many years. They also recognise other animals they were friends with.

2690.q: When is the mating season of brown bears usually?
2690.e: Brown bears usually mate in May or June. Because of a delay in the process, the young only really start to develop in autumn.
2690.m: The bears’ mating season is in early summer.

2691.q: Which animals like to eat butterfly caterpillars?
2691.e: Many birds such as tits search for caterpillars in the garden. Caterpillars are an important, protein-rich food for them.

2692.q: Why is it important that there are several parties?
a: So that people can choose between different ideas.
So that there are more election posters.
So that everyone has the same opinion.
2692.e: Several parties offer different solutions to problems. That way the people can freely decide which idea they like best.
2692.m: Several parties give a real choice.

2693.q: What do armoured catfish from South America have on their bodies?
2693.e: Armoured catfish are covered with hard bony plates that protect them like armour. Their German name “Harnischwels” also comes from “Harnisch”, a knight’s armour.
2693.m: Armoured catfish wear armour of bony plates.

2694.q: What is the red, jagged thing on top of a chicken’s head called?
2694.e: The red comb sits on top of the head. In cockerels it is usually bigger and more striking than in hens.
2694.m: The comb sits on a chicken’s head.

2695.q: What do many people wrongly believe about the mole?
2695.e: Many gardeners think the mole destroys plants because it makes molehills. In fact it mainly eats worms and insects, not roots.

2696.q: How does the garden spider usually survive the winter as a species?
a: As eggs in a protected cocoon
As an adult in the middle of the snow
2696.e: Adult garden spiders usually die in winter. The cold season is survived as eggs in a cocoon spun to keep them warm.

2697.q: How many eggs does a female eagle owl usually lay in a clutch?
2697.e: A female eagle owl usually lays two to three eggs, sometimes more or fewer depending on how much food there is. The eggs are laid a few days apart.
2697.m: Eagle owls usually lay two to three eggs.

2698.e: Kangaroos really can swim well. When they are in danger they sometimes even escape into the water.

2699.q: Where does a stone marten most like to hide during the day?
2699.e: Stone martens rest in sheltered, dry places during the day. Lofts and barns protect them from enemies and bad weather.
2699.m: Lofts are popular marten hiding places.

2700.q: Which prey is especially often on the golden eagle’s menu in the Alps?
2700.e: In the Alps the golden eagle mainly hunts marmots, hares and other medium-sized mammals. Birds are sometimes also among its prey.
2700.m: Marmots are among its favourite prey.

2701.q: How long does a young koala usually stay with its mother?
2701.e: A young koala stays with its mother for about a year. After that it looks for its own home in the trees.
2701.m: Young koalas stay with their mother for around a year.

2702.q: What do newborn seahorses look like?
a: Like tiny mini versions of the adults
2702.e: Even at birth, baby seahorses look just like their parents, only much smaller. They have to look after themselves straight away.

2703.q: What body shape does the stone marten have that helps it slip through narrow gaps?
a: A body as round as a ball
2703.e: Its slim, long build lets the stone marten slip through very narrow openings and gaps. This way it easily gets into lofts and barns.
2703.m: A slim build helps it slip through.

2704.q: Which animal is the okapi most closely related to?
2704.e: Despite the zebra stripes on its legs, the okapi is the closest relative of the giraffe. Both have, for example, a long, dark tongue.
2704.m: The okapi is a relative of the giraffe.

2705.q: What are the GPS collars that scientists put on some wolves for?
a: To study their routes and territories
2705.e: With GPS transmitters researchers can track how far wolves travel and where they spend their time. This data helps plan how to protect the animals better.

2706.q: Which family do hyenas belong to?
a: Hyenas form their own family within the carnivores
They belong to the dog family
They belong to the cat family
They belong to the mustelid family
2706.e: Hyenas form the family Hyaenidae within the carnivores. They are more closely related to the cat-like carnivores than to dogs.
2706.m: Hyenas are a carnivore family of their own.

2707.q: What do dung beetles mainly feed on?
2707.e: Dung beetles look for the dung of animals such as cows, horses or sheep. In it they find food for themselves and their young.
2707.m: Dung beetles live on the dung of plant eaters.

2708.q: What tiny sacs make up the lungs, where gas exchange takes place?
2708.e: In the millions of air sacs, oxygen is taken into the blood. At the same time, carbon dioxide is released.
2708.m: Alveoli swap oxygen for carbon dioxide.

2709.q: What is the difference between the executive and the legislature?
a: The executive governs, the legislature makes laws
The executive makes laws, the legislature governs
Only the legislature exists in Switzerland
2709.e: The executive is the government, for example the Federal Council. The legislature is the parliament, which passes laws.
2709.m: The executive governs, the legislature makes laws.

2710.q: What do many millipedes do when they feel threatened?
a: They roll up into a spiral
2710.e: Many millipedes curl up. This protects their sensitive underside, and only the hard back is on the outside.

a: Money you get regularly from your parents to manage yourself
Money that may only be used for school
Money the bank gives you as a present
2711.e: Pocket money is money children get regularly and are allowed to manage themselves. This helps you learn early how to handle money.
2711.m: Learn to manage your pocket money yourself.

2712.q: Is the common frog protected in Switzerland?
a: Yes, it is protected by law
No, it can be caught anywhere
No, there is no law about it
2712.e: The common frog is protected in Switzerland because its habitat is getting smaller and smaller. You must not simply catch it or harm its spawn.
2712.m: The common frog is protected in Switzerland.

2713.q: What is special about an Alpine marmot’s front teeth?
a: They keep growing all its life
They fall out after a year and never grow back
It has no front teeth at all
They are as soft as rubber
2713.e: As in many rodents, marmots’ incisors keep growing throughout their lives. At the same time they are constantly worn down by gnawing on plants.

2714.q: What does a rhino’s skin feel like?
2714.e: A rhino’s skin is several centimetres thick and very tough. It protects the animal well from injuries.

2715.e: Wild boar are surprisingly good swimmers. They can even cross rivers or lakes.

2716.q: What is special about the dromedary’s body temperature?
a: It changes a lot during the day
It always stays exactly the same
2716.e: The animal lets its body get warmer during the day before it starts to sweat. This saves precious water.
2716.m: Body temperature changes to save water.

2717.q: At about what age is a red kite old enough to breed?
2717.e: Young red kites need a few years before they can breed themselves. Only at about 2 to 3 years old are they ready.
2717.m: Red kites can breed at 2 to 3 years.

2718.q: About how heavy can an adult male brown bear in Europe get?
2718.e: European male brown bears often weigh between 150 and 300 kilograms. But some subspecies in North America get much heavier.
2718.m: Male brown bears often weigh up to 300 kilograms.

2719.q: What do many millipedes of the double-legged kind do when they are threatened?
a: They roll up into a spiral
2719.e: Many of these millipedes, which have two pairs of legs on each body segment, curl up into a spiral. This protects their soft underside and their legs.

2720.q: What is special about a kangaroo’s front legs compared with its back legs?
a: They are much smaller and shorter
2720.e: Kangaroos’ front legs are short and small. The back legs, on the other hand, are very strong for hopping.

2721.q: How is the President of the Swiss Confederation chosen?
a: The Federal Assembly elects a member of the Federal Council for it every year
The people elect the president directly
The Federal Council is appointed by the UN
The president is chosen by the cantons
2721.e: Every year the Federal Assembly decides which member of the Federal Council will chair it for one year. That person still remains a member of the Federal Council with equal rights.
2721.m: The chair of the Federal Council changes every year.

2722.q: How often does the mother roe deer come to her hidden fawn to feed it?
a: Only a few times a day
All the time without a break
Never, the fawn looks for her itself
2722.e: The mother does not stay with the fawn all the time, because that could attract attention. She only comes by a few times a day to feed it with milk.
2722.m: The mother roe deer visits her fawn briefly.

2723.q: Why do you dress warmly in winter?
a: So that your body does not lose too much heat
So that your eyes see better
2723.e: Warm clothes keep your body heat in. That way you do not get cold so quickly.
2723.m: Warm clothes keep the heat in.

2724.q: Which mountain region do alpacas originally come from?
2724.e: Alpacas were bred in the Andes in countries such as Peru, Bolivia and Chile. There they live at high altitude.

2725.q: What does the Swiss foundation PanEco work for on Sumatra?
2725.e: PanEco, based in Switzerland, runs a programme on Sumatra to protect orangutans. Orphaned animals are cared for and released back into the wild.

2726.q: What does a sow build before her piglets are born?
a: A deep cave in the rock
2726.e: Before the birth the sow makes a soft nest of straw or other material. There her piglets are born safe and protected.
2726.m: Piglets are born in a soft nest.

2727.q: What does a cross next to ‘Yes’ on the ballot paper mean?
2727.e: If you tick Yes, you agree with the proposal. If you tick No, you reject it.

2728.q: How long does the female swan sit on her eggs?
2728.e: The female sits on the eggs for about five weeks. That is how long it takes until the cygnets hatch.
2728.m: Sitting on the eggs takes around five weeks.

2729.q: Why do geese usually live together in a group?
a: In a group they are safer from enemies
Because otherwise they are not allowed to eat
Because a single goose cannot honk
2729.e: In a larger group the animals notice more quickly when danger is near. This way they protect each other.
2729.m: Geese are safer in a group.

2730.q: How do bonobos often settle quarrels in the group?
a: With physical contact, comfort and affection
With loud fights until someone wins
2730.e: Bonobos often calm tensions with touching, hugs and affection. As a result, serious fights happen less often.

2731.q: About how many different kinds of bumblebee are there in Switzerland?
2731.e: Well over 40 different kinds of bumblebee live in Switzerland. They differ, for example, in size and fur pattern.
2731.m: There are many kinds of bumblebee in Switzerland.

2732.q: What is the unit of electric current called?
2732.e: Current tells you how much electric charge flows through a wire per second. The unit is named after the physicist André-Marie Ampère.

2733.q: How long does a mother giraffe carry her baby before it is born?
2733.e: Giraffes have a very long pregnancy of around fifteen months. That is much longer than in most other animals.
2733.m: Giraffe babies grow for about 15 months.

2734.q: On which continent do meerkats live in the wild?
2734.e: Meerkats live in southern Africa. They mainly live in dry, open landscapes.

2735.q: How does the wood mouse react to light?
a: It avoids bright light and hides
It is attracted to light like a moth
2735.e: As a night animal, the wood mouse avoids bright light and retreats to its burrow in daylight.
2735.m: It prefers to avoid bright light.

2736.q: What do some chimpanzees use to crack hard nuts?
2736.e: Some chimpanzees put a nut on a stone and hit it with another stone. This way they get to the tasty kernel.

2737.q: How old does a worker bumblebee usually get?
2737.e: Workers often live only a few weeks because their work is very tiring. The queen, on the other hand, lives much longer than the workers.
2737.m: Workers live only a few weeks.

2738.q: What kind of teeth does a horse have, because it chews so much?
a: Large grinding teeth that keep growing
Sharp tearing teeth like a cat’s
2738.e: Horses have large grinding teeth that they use to grind tough grass and hay well. These teeth wear down over time and keep growing.
2738.m: Horse teeth are made for grinding grass.

2739.q: What are a hedgehog’s ears like?
a: Hedgehogs have no ears at all
2739.e: The hedgehog’s ears are small and round and almost hidden in its fur and spines. Even so, it hears very well with them.

a: A canton uses it to ask the Confederation for a new law or a change to the constitution
A popular vote in a canton
An initiative only by young people
2740.e: With a cantonal initiative, a canton can make a proposal to the Confederation. Parliament then decides whether to take it up.
2740.m: A canton can make proposals with a cantonal initiative.

2741.q: Which group of animals do seahorses belong to?
2741.e: Seahorses live in water and breathe with gills, so they count as fish. They may look funny, but they are real fish.

2742.q: When is the adder’s mating season?
2742.e: After their winter rest the animals mate in spring. The males often fight each other with their bodies twisted together.
2742.m: Mating in spring after the winter rest.

2745.q: How do people in some countries protect fields from elephants?
2745.e: Elephants often eat plants in fields. Fences and ditches help reduce the damage.

2746.q: Where does the female woodlouse carry her eggs?
a: In a brood pouch on her belly
In a hole in the ground
In a cocoon on her back
2746.e: Under her body the female has a brood pouch filled with liquid. The eggs and the young develop there.
2746.m: Female woodlice carry their eggs on their belly.

2757.q: What is a municipal office building?
a: The building where the municipality's administration works
2757.e: In the municipal office building, people work who look after things in the village or town. You can apply for a passport there, for example.
2757.m: The municipal administration works in the municipal office building.

2765.q: How can advertising influence the way you spend money?
a: It can create wants that lead to spontaneous, unplanned purchases
Advertising has no effect on purchases
Advertising only informs about legal rules
2765.e: Advertising is designed to create wants and encourage you to buy, even if you do not really need the product. Thinking critically helps you stick to your budget.

a: An object with such strong gravity that not even light can escape
A hole in the Earth’s atmosphere
2776.e: A black hole often forms when a very massive star collapses in on itself at the end of its life. Its pull is so strong that not even light can escape it.
2776.m: Black holes let no light escape.

2779.q: What does it mean to buy something on credit or in instalments?
a: You pay for the product in several parts over time, often with extra costs
You pay the full price in cash straight away
You get the product as a present
You swap it for another product
2779.e: When paying in instalments, you do not pay everything at once but in parts. There are often extra costs or interest, which makes the product more expensive in the end.
2779.m: Paying in instalments can cost more.

2782.q: How endangered is the African wild dog according to the IUCN Red List?
a: It is only known in zoos
2782.e: The IUCN classes it as “endangered”. There are only a few thousand animals left.
2782.m: The African wild dog is endangered.

2787.q: Roughly how often a year can Swiss people go to the polls?
2787.e: In Switzerland there are usually four voting dates a year. People can then decide on various questions.
2787.m: There are usually four voting dates a year.

a: An organisation that connects the police forces of different countries
2819.e: Interpol helps police forces from different countries work together, for example when searching for criminals across borders. Its headquarters are in France.
2819.m: Interpol connects police forces around the world.

a: An office of a country abroad
2826.e: A consulate is an office of a country abroad. It helps, for example, if someone has lost their passport.

2841.q: In which habitats can a leopard be found?
2841.e: Leopards are very adaptable. They live in savannahs, forests, mountains and sometimes even close to cities.

2861.q: In which season do most flowers in Switzerland bloom for the first time?
2861.e: In spring it gets warmer and lighter. Many plants wake up from their winter rest and start to bloom.
2861.m: In spring the plants wake up.

2888.q: What does the abbreviation “EU” stand for?
2888.e: The EU is a group of countries in Europe. They work together on issues such as trade, the environment and travel.

2891.q: What does the law of the lever say, put simply?
a: Effort times effort arm equals load times load arm
The shorter the lever, the less force you need
2891.e: With a lever: the longer the effort arm compared with the load arm, the less force you need to use. That is why long seesaws are easier to work than short ones.
2891.m: A long lever arm saves force.

2896.q: What is the opposite of a dictatorship?
2896.e: In a democracy the people have a say in who governs. That is the opposite of a dictatorship, where one person decides alone.
2896.m: Democracy is the opposite of dictatorship.

2900.q: What is an election ballot paper?
a: A paper on which you tick names for an election
2900.e: The election ballot paper lists the names of people or parties. You tick who you want to elect.
2900.m: On the election ballot paper you choose people.

a: A very cold continent at the South Pole
A warm continent at the equator
An ocean near the North Pole
2901.e: Antarctica lies at the Earth’s South Pole and is mostly covered with thick ice. It is almost always very cold there.
2901.m: Antarctica is at the South Pole and is freezing cold.

2914.q: On which river does the old Landhaus in the town of Solothurn stand?
2914.e: The Landhaus is an old building right on the bank of the Aare. In the past, goods from the boats were stored there; today it hosts parties and concerts.
2914.m: The Landhaus in Solothurn stands on the Aare.

a: A friendship between two municipalities in different countries
A football club with players from many countries
2938.e: Two municipalities in different countries can form a partnership to visit each other and exchange ideas. In this way people from different cultures get to know each other.
2938.m: Town twinning links municipalities across borders.

2953.q: The scientific name of the African wild dog means roughly “painted wolf”. Why does that fit?
2953.e: The wild dog's coat has patches of black, yellow, brown and white. It looks as if someone has painted the animal.

2964.q: What are the coins worth less than one franc called?
2964.e: In Switzerland the small coins are called rappen (centimes in French). 100 rappen make one franc.

a: A thinker who had new ideas about a fair society
2977.e: Karl Marx was a German thinker in the 19th century. His ideas became the basis of communism.
2977.m: Karl Marx thought about a fairer world.

2978.q: In which cities does the European Parliament mainly meet?
2978.e: The European Parliament has its main seat in Strasbourg but often also meets in Brussels. There elected members represent the citizens of the EU countries.
2978.m: The EU Parliament meets in Strasbourg and Brussels.

2981.q: How do bonobos usually move around on the ground?
a: Only hopping on their back legs
Sliding on their belly like snakes
2981.e: On the ground, bonobos lean on the knuckles of their hands. Sometimes, though, they walk upright for short distances.

2982.q: Roughly how long do ravens incubate their eggs?
2982.e: After the eggs are laid, it takes about three weeks for young ravens to hatch. During this time the male mainly brings food.

2983.q: How big is a bumblebee colony compared with a honeybee colony?
a: Much smaller, often only a few hundred insects
Much bigger, with many thousands of insects
There is only one bumblebee per nest
2983.e: A bumblebee colony usually has only a few hundred insects. A honeybee colony is often much bigger, with many thousands of bees.
2983.m: Bumblebee colonies are small, honeybee colonies are big.

2984.q: What can zoos do for gibbons?
a: Run breeding programmes and teach people about the threats
They make gibbons live on the ground
2984.e: Many zoos take part in breeding programmes for endangered species. They also tell visitors how gibbons can be protected.

2985.q: Why does the bearded vulture often have rusty red feathers on its belly?
a: It mixes paint with its saliva
2985.e: Bearded vultures deliberately rub themselves in reddish soil or mud containing iron oxide. This gives their white feathers a rusty red colour.
2985.m: The rusty red comes from a mud bath.

2986.q: How long is a jaguar's tail compared with other big cats?
a: It has no tail at all
2986.e: Compared with its body, the jaguar's tail is rather short. It usually measures about 45 to 75 centimetres.
2986.m: Jaguars have a fairly short tail.

2987.q: What do we call the insects and spiders drifting high in the air that swifts eat?
2987.e: Aerial plankton is made up of tiny insects and spiders carried upwards by the wind. Swifts catch this food while flying.
2987.m: Aerial plankton is the swift's food.

2988.q: What does it mean that baboons are omnivores?
a: They eat both plant and animal food
2988.e: Omnivores use many sources of food. This helps baboons survive in different habitats.

2989.q: Where does a female carp usually lay her eggs?
a: In a hollow in the gravel
2989.e: The female carp sticks her eggs to water plants. There they are well hidden and protected.
2989.m: Carp eggs stick to water plants.

2990.q: How does the hooded crow look different from the carrion crow?
a: It has a grey body with a black head and wings
It is much bigger than an eagle
2990.e: The hooded crow is closely related to the carrion crow, but it has a grey body while its head, wings and tail stay black. In some places the two species form mixed pairs.
2990.m: Hooded crows have a grey body.

2991.q: What colour is a koala's fur usually?
2991.e: A koala's fur is usually grey or greyish brown. This gives it good camouflage in the trees.
2991.m: Koala fur is usually grey to brown.

2992.q: How many eggs does a mallard usually lay?
2992.e: A clutch usually has between eight and twelve eggs. The female then incubates them herself.

2993.q: Apart from its lungs, what else can the common frog breathe with?
2993.e: The common frog's skin is thin and moist. It can take in extra oxygen through it, especially in winter in the water.
2993.m: Common frogs also breathe through their skin.

2994.q: What do you call the movable connection between two bones?
2994.e: Joints connect bones and make movement possible. Cartilage, ligaments and fluid make sure they work well.
2994.m: Joints connect bones so they can move.

2995.q: What is the small device on a bike called that makes electricity for the light from the movement of the wheel?
2995.e: A dynamo makes electricity from the turning of the wheel. This lets the bike light shine without a battery.
2995.m: The dynamo turns movement into electricity.

2996.q: What does the female sea turtle mainly use her back flippers for on land?
a: Digging the nest for her eggs
2996.e: On land the female uses her back flippers like little spades to dig a hole for the eggs. Afterwards she carefully covers the nest with sand again.
2996.m: Back flippers dig the egg nest in the sand.

2997.q: How do adult bearded vultures usually react to people near their nest?
a: They are very sensitive to disturbance
They come closer out of curiosity
They show no reaction at all
2997.e: Bearded vultures react badly to disturbance near their nest and may even abandon their eggs or chicks. That is why it is important not to disturb nesting areas.
2997.m: Disturbance at the nest is dangerous.

2998.q: How does a grasshopper behave when it gets cold?
a: It becomes even faster than usual
It grows new wings at once
2998.e: Grasshoppers need warmth to be active. When it is cold they move only very slowly.
2998.m: Cold makes them tired and slow.

2999.q: What hatches from an ant egg?
2999.e: First a larva hatches from the egg. Later it becomes a pupa and then a fully grown ant.

3000.q: Why are bees important for plants and people?
a: They pollinate many flowers so that fruit can grow
They make noise to scare off pests
3000.e: When bees fly from flower to flower, they carry pollen along. This lets plants produce seeds, and lots of fruit and vegetables can grow.

3001.e: In electoral fraud votes are manipulated or miscounted so that the desired candidate wins. In dictatorships this is a common way of staying in power.
3001.m: False votes fake a real election.

3002.q: At what age are golden eagles usually able to breed?
3002.e: Golden eagles only get their full adult plumage at about 4 to 5 years old, and then they can breed. Before that they go through several juvenile plumages.
3002.m: They can breed at about 4 years old.

3003.q: What do great crested grebe chicks' feathers usually look like?
a: Black and white stripes like a little watermelon
3003.e: The young chicks have a typical black and white striped pattern that is often compared to a little watermelon. This pattern helps camouflage them.
3003.m: Chicks are striped black and white like a melon.

3004.q: Roughly how big is an ant?
3004.e: Most ants are tiny. They often measure only a few millimetres.
